Features e dependências

Features LANG selecionam contratos. native-engines habilita adapters reais e limitados de C/C++/Rust, sem baixar engines automaticamente. Os contratos LANG são opt-in; o registro não possui features default. CLI/agente preservam advanced-components como default e native/jit continuam opt-in. Dependências são transitivas e propagadas pelo rd-cli/rd-agent; o catálogo permanece completo em qualquer build. O MCP aceita seleção explícita launch.engine; consulte C/C++/Rust.

MóduloCargo featureDependências diretasNota
LANG-01lang-01—DEX compartilhado; VM existente tem cobertura parcial.
LANG-02lang-02LANG-01ELF/JNI parcial via feature native (x86_64/ARM64/ARMv7); não é NDK/Android completo nem adaptador do registro.
LANG-03lang-03LANG-02Rust NDK reutiliza a fronteira ELF/JNI.
LANG-04lang-04LANG-02Flutter: Dart AOT e engine/render próprio pendentes.
LANG-05lang-05LANG-02JS/RN/NativeScript: engine JS e bridges pendentes.
LANG-06lang-06LANG-01WebView/bridges Android; não baixa páginas na detecção.
LANG-07lang-07LANG-02Mono/IL e render de MAUI/Avalonia pendentes.
LANG-08lang-08LANG-07União das rotas Unity Mono e IL2CPP; não implica suporte gráfico.
LANG-09lang-09LANG-02Pontes independentes de engines; não embute engines no registro.
LANG-10lang-10LANG-01Shared DEX é possível; render Compose MP exige trabalho adicional.
LANG-11lang-11LANG-01Java gerado; só o subconjunto DEX já disponível.
LANG-12lang-12LANG-01WASM in-app; bridge JNI/JS escolhida na implementação futura.

Exemplo: cargo build -p rd-cli --no-default-features --features lang-04 seleciona LANG-04 → LANG-02 → LANG-01. O campo feature_enabled confirma seleção, enquanto registry_adapter_status continua NOT_IMPLEMENTED. LANG-08 representa a união Mono/IL2CPP; selecionar o módulo inclui LANG-07. A VM já renderiza um subconjunto Compose Android; a feature native executa ELF/JNI limitados em x86_64/ARM64/ARMv7. native-engines acrescenta os adapters c-ndk, cpp-ndk, rust-ndk sobre essa rota. Não implementa Compose Multiplatform, NDK/Android completo nem bridges WebView. Essas rotas existentes e seus limites estão nos ADRs 004, 006 e 007. runtime_status descreve cobertura existente, não disponibilidade neste build; feature_enabled informa somente os contratos LANG. native/jit são seleções independentes. AVAILABLE_BOUNDED informa existência do adapter, não execução observada. Metadados mantêm execution_claimed=false; o relatório do runtime mede instruções reais.

Regras de detecção e rotas

all exige todas as pistas; any exige pelo menos uma quando não vazio. Regras só usam nomes ZIP canônicos (case-sensitive) e classes/metadados de componentes do manifest. Bibliotecas nativas exigem exatamente lib/<abi>/<arquivo>.so; DEX exige classes.dex ou classesN.dex (N ≥ 2). Nenhum asset/lib é descomprimido, extraído, carregado ou executado.

1 — java

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-vm
  • Runtime: DEX parcial (rd-vm); adaptador do registro ausente
  • Limite: DEX tem suporte parcial, não execução universal de Java.
  • candidate: all=[root-dex]; any=[] — DEX é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem.

2 — kotlin

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-vm
  • Runtime: DEX parcial (rd-vm); adaptador do registro ausente
  • Limite: Dependências Kotlin não provam que o app foi escrito em Kotlin.
  • candidate: all=[root-dex]; any=[] — DEX é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem.

3 — kotlin-multiplatform

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-compose-mp
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Não é possível distinguir KMP/Compose MP apenas pela presença de DEX.
  • candidate: all=[root-dex]; any=[] — DEX é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem.
  • candidate: all=[suffix:.klib]; any=[] — klib é pista, não prova render Compose Multiplatform.

4 — jvm-dynamic

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-vm
  • Runtime: DEX parcial (rd-vm); adaptador do registro ausente
  • Limite: invoke-custom/method handles e runtimes dinâmicos não são declarados completos.
  • candidate: all=[root-dex]; any=[] — DEX é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem.

5 — c-ndk

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-ndk/rd-jni
  • Runtime: ELF/JNI parcial; disponibilidade do adaptador depende da engine/feature
  • Limite: C não pode ser atribuído a uma .so genérica. Adapter c-ndk real e limitado exige native-engines; fonte/compilador auditáveis atribuem o idioma.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.

6 — cpp-ndk

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-ndk/rd-jni
  • Runtime: ELF/JNI parcial; disponibilidade do adaptador depende da engine/feature
  • Limite: Adapter cpp-ndk real e limitado exige native-engines. O APK de prova compila C++20 com std::array e sem libc++_shared; não implementa exceções nem STL/NDK completos.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.

7 — rust-ndk

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-ndk/rd-jni
  • Runtime: ELF/JNI parcial; disponibilidade do adaptador depende da engine/feature
  • Limite: Nome .so e símbolos removidos não provam Rust. Adapter rust-ndk real com native-engines, validado por APK Android no_std source-built; não implica std/async.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.

8 — go-mobile

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-gomobile
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Marcador gojni é uma assinatura heurística, não análise de símbolos.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.
  • signature: all=[native:libgojni.so]; any=[] — Marcador de bind gomobile.

9 — objective-c-ndk

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-ndk/rd-jni
  • Runtime: ELF/JNI parcial; disponibilidade do adaptador depende da engine/feature
  • Limite: Somente a rota ELF/JNI é parcial; runtime Objective-C não é implementado. Uma .so genérica só produz candidato.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.

10 — zig-llvm

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-ndk/rd-jni
  • Runtime: ELF/JNI parcial; disponibilidade do adaptador depende da engine/feature
  • Limite: ELF não preserva necessariamente a linguagem do compilador.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.

11 — flutter

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-flutter
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Não interpreta Dart AOT nem converte widgets nesta entrega.
  • signature: all=[native:libflutter.so, prefix:assets/flutter_assets/]; any=[] — Engine Flutter acompanhado de assets.
  • candidate: all=[native:libapp.so]; any=[] — libapp.so isolada não prova Flutter.

12 — react-native

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-react-native
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED

  • candidate: all=[path:assets/index.android.bundle]; any=[] — Bundle convencional isolado é apenas candidato.

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-webview

  • signature: all=[prefix:assets/public/, path:assets/capacitor.config.json]; any=[] — Assets web com configuração Capacitor.
  • candidate: all=[prefix:assets/www/]; any=[] — Assets HTML compatíveis com engines web.
  • candidate: all=[prefix:assets/public/]; any=[] — Assets HTML compatíveis com engines web.

14 — twa-pwa

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-webview
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Ausência de payload local não descarta TWA/PWA.

17 — dotnet-maui

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-mono

  • Limite: PCK isolado é candidato; C# demanda Mono além de Godot.
  • signature: all=[suffix:.pck]; any=[native:libgodot_android.so, native:libgodot.so] — Biblioteca Godot e pacote/descritor do projeto.
  • signature: all=[path:assets/project.binary]; any=[native:libgodot_android.so, native:libgodot.so] — Biblioteca Godot e project.binary.
  • candidate: all=[suffix:.pck]; any=[] — Pacote .pck isolado não prova Godot.

22 — lua-engines

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-lua
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Bytecode/containers podem ser comprimidos; .lua é apenas candidato.
  • signature: all=[]; any=[native:libcorona.so, native:libdmengine.so] — Marcador de engine Lua (Solar2D libcorona; Defold real embarca libdmengine.so — libdefold.so nunca existiu na build oficial).
  • candidate: all=[suffix:.lua]; any=[] — Payload Lua não distingue Defold/Solar2D/Cocos2d-x.
  • candidate: all=[suffix:.luac]; any=[] — Bytecode Lua apenas por extensão; conteúdo não validado.
  • candidate: all=[native:libcocos2dcpp.so]; any=[] — Cocos2d-x não implica uso de Lua.

23 — python-engines

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-python
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Não descompacta private.mp3/stdlib.zip nem executa Python.
  • signature: all=[prefix:assets/chaquopy/]; any=[] — Marcador de payload Chaquopy.
  • candidate: all=[]; any=[suffix:.py, suffix:.pyc] — Payload Python identificável por extensão.
  • candidate: all=[path:assets/private.mp3]; any=[] — Container convencional python-for-android; conteúdo não verificado.

24 — haxe

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-haxe
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Formato DEX/ELF não identifica Haxe; ambas as rotas são candidatos.
  • candidate: all=[root-dex]; any=[] — DEX é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem.
  • candidate: all=[native-so]; any=[] — ELF é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem nem valida ABI/payload.

25 — qt-qml

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-qt
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: QML pode estar em recursos compilados, fora de assets visíveis.
  • signature: all=[suffix:.qml]; any=[native-prefix:libQt5Core, native-prefix:libQt6Core] — Runtime Qt e payload QML.
  • candidate: all=[]; any=[native-prefix:libQt5Core, native-prefix:libQt6Core] — Runtime Qt por nome de lib.
  • candidate: all=[suffix:.qml]; any=[] — QML isolado é candidato.

26 — avalonia

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-avalonia
  • Runtime: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
  • Limite: Assemblies em stores opacos podem não ser identificáveis.
  • signature: all=[]; any=[path:assemblies/Avalonia.Android.dll, path:assemblies/Avalonia.Base.dll] — Assembly Avalonia embarcada.
  • candidate: all=[prefix:assemblies/]; any=[] — Payload managed genérico não prova Avalonia.

27 — generated-java

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-vm
  • Runtime: DEX parcial (rd-vm); adaptador do registro ausente
  • Limite: Java gerado não é distinguível de Java escrito à mão apenas pelo formato.
  • candidate: all=[root-dex]; any=[] — DEX é compartilhado: não identifica a linguagem de origem.

28 — wasm

  • Rota existente/futura: rd-engine-wasm
  • Runtime: WASM hospedado pelo RustyDroid via bridge documentada (WasmBridge, i32 MVP); adaptador depende da feature wasm-execution
  • Limite: WASM hospedado pelo RustyDroid via bridge documentada: APK com DEX + assets/*.wasm roda pela VM e pelo WasmBridge (feature wasm-execution, M11 S1c): i32, fuel por chamada, sem WASI, threads, JS/JNI bridge nem loader .wasm standalone. Extensão .wasm sozinha não prova execução.
  • candidate: all=[suffix:.wasm]; any=[] — Arquivo com extensão WASM; payload não validado.

Contrato e erros

EngineAdapter define parse(Artifact) -> Process, event(process, event) e syscall(process, call). Os 28 adaptadores do registro são indisponíveis: toda operação retorna {code, cause, suggestion, module_id} com code: NOT_IMPLEMENTED e module_id: LANG-xx. Nenhum processo fictício é retornado, mesmo com --all-features. A cobertura DEX existente pertence a rd-vm, pelas rotas rd vm/rd app, não a estes adaptadores.

CódigoSituação
NOT_IMPLEMENTEDOperação de runtime/contrato ainda ausente (CLI exit 2)
UNKNOWN_ENGINEID não registrado (exit 1)
INVALID_ENGINE_CATALOGSchema, IDs, módulos, ciclos, regras ou status inválidos
CATALOG_TOO_LARGECatálogo maior que 1 MiB
DETECTION_LIMITMais de 100.000 entradas ZIP
IO_ERRORArquivo de catálogo/APK inacessível

Ao exceder o limite de entradas, rd engine detect continua falhando com DETECTION_LIMIT. inspect --json e MCP app_info preservam os dados básicos; engines contém analysis_status: not_analyzed e error tipado, não uma lista vazia que fingiria ausência de assinaturas. Catálogo explícito inválido continua sendo erro, nunca fallback silencioso.

Diagnósticos do relatório: DUPLICATE_ZIP_ENTRY, NON_CANONICAL_ARTIFACT_PATH, UNKNOWN_ABI, AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE_LANGUAGE. Nomes duplicados contam uma vez. Evidências/diagnósticos contêm no máximo 4 amostras por predicado/diagnóstico, mantendo a contagem total. Todos os 28 IDs aparecem, inclusive not_detected; ordem e amostras são determinísticas. execution_claimed: false e artifact_validation: not-performed são contratos explícitos.

Testes e definição de conclusão

  • tests/engines/signatures.json: exatamente 28 casos golden de DETECÇÃO, um por ID. Fixtures APK/AXML/ZIP são geradas em memória; nenhum binário é commitado. Testes cobrem híbridos, pistas incompletas, ambiguidades, paths hostis, duplicatas, teto de entradas e amostragem.
  • Tests de contrato exercitam parse/event/syscall para os 28 itens: sempre erro tipado. Builds mínimo, features individuais e todas são independentes.
  • cargo xtask engine-report regenera este arquivo; cargo xtask engine-spec regenera apenas a tabela marcada no Apêndice G; cargo xtask compat-report atualiza o placar oficial. Testes barram drift.
  • Integração OSS explícita: baixe um APK com golden-apks/fetch.sh e rode RD_TEST_APK=/caminho/app.apk cargo test -p rd-engine-registry --test registry real_oss_apk_inventory -- --ignored. Sem a variável/arquivo, o teste falha; não há falso sucesso por pular a fixture. No teste normal ele é ignored.

Registro/detecção concluídos ≠ runtime concluído. Uma engine só pode mudar de NOT_IMPLEMENTED após crate/adaptador real feature-gated, ADR, parse/event/syscall funcionais, golden flow com APK OSS e gate Moto E5. As capacidades parciais de M9 já existentes não equivalem às engines de M11. Veja ADR 003 e ROADMAP.

Ferramentas do Agente MCP (M5)

Servidor rustydroid-agent v0.9.0 · protocolo 2024-11-05 · transporte stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0, uma mensagem por linha).

Total: 52 tools. Este catálogo é gerado de rd_agent::mcp::tool_defs() — o MESMO registro respondido em tools/list e impresso por rd mcp --describe-tools.

Controles de segurança

  • Sandbox de caminhos: install/screenshot só acessam arquivos dentro das raízes RD_MCP_SANDBOX (default: cwd + temp do sistema); .. e URLs são recusados (PATH_OUTSIDE_SANDBOX/URL_NOT_ALLOWED).
  • APK excessivo: teto de tamanho RD_MCP_MAX_APK_MB (default 256 MB) — checado antes de ler (APK_TOO_LARGE).
  • Tempo ilimitado: wait/swipe/wait_for têm teto RD_MCP_MAX_WAIT_MS (default 60 000 ms) (LIMIT_EXCEEDED).
  • Batch: teto de passos RD_MCP_MAX_BATCH (default 64); sem aninhamento; retomada idempotente via resume_from.
  • Estado consistente: install/remove/clear são transacionais (validam tudo antes de mutar); app em execução é encerrado antes de remove/clear/reinstall do mesmo package.

Erros

Falhas de tool voltam com isError: true e o contrato estável {code, cause, suggestion?, module_id}. Erros de PROTOCOLO são JSON-RPC (-32601 método, -32700 parse).

Catálogo

session_open

ADR 023 (sessões): abre outra sessão de app no processo, com estado isolado (engine, disco virtual, logs, permissões e tela). Devolve engine_id; passe-o em engine_id das demais tools para atuar nela. Limite padrão 2 (env RD_MCP_MAX_SESSIONS, máximo 8). Erro SESSION_LIMIT ao passar do teto.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

session_list

ADR 023 (sessões): lista as sessões abertas no processo, com engine_id, se é a padrão, o app instalado ativo e o app em execução. A sessão padrão (sem engine_id) vem primeiro.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

session_close

ADR 023 (sessões): fecha uma sessão aberta com session_open e libera o slot. A sessão padrão não fecha (erro INVALID_ARG). Erro SESSION_NOT_FOUND para engine_id desconhecido.

  • Parâmetros: engine_id · obrigatórios: engine_id

install

Instala um APK na sessão (abre, valida o piso API 9 e prepara o estado de permissões). Caminho PRECISA estar dentro do sandbox (RD_MCP_SANDBOX); URL é recusada; APK acima de RD_MCP_MAX_APK_MB (default 256) é recusado. Reinstalar o package EM EXECUÇÃO o encerra (sem estado inconsistente). Não executa o app.

  • Parâmetros: apk, instant · obrigatórios: apk

launch

Executa o app instalado: cria a activity (LAUNCHER ou activity) e roda o lifecycle até o onCreate completar. activity precisa estar declarada como / no AndroidManifest.xml E existir no DEX (issues #82/#83) — o Android recusa o que não está declarado; um lança a sua targetActivity (issue #109). Se o MESMO package já está em execução, o relançamento reutiliza o processo (warm start: sem re-parse do DEX; o resultado traz warm=true) (M7). Com package lança outro app do registro (multi-app); sem, o app ativo (último install/launch).

  • Parâmetros: activity, engine, observe, package

tap

Toque simulado nas coordenadas (px do viewport ativo: 720×1440 retrato, 1440×720 paisagem). Retorna se algum listener foi acionado.

  • Parâmetros: observe, x, y · obrigatórios: x, y

swipe

Gesto de arraste determinístico (x1,y1)→(x2,y2) em ms (cap RD_MCP_MAX_WAIT_MS). Reporta as views atravessadas em ordem; down+up na MESMA view vira clique (listener disparado) — semântica Android tap vs scroll.

  • Parâmetros: ms, observe, x1, x2, y1, y2 · obrigatórios: x1, y1, x2, y2

type_text

Digita texto: na EditText focada/primeira visível; sem EditText (Jetpack Compose, editores custom) usa o caminho do IME da plataforma — a view focada cria o InputConnection (onCreateInputConnection) e recebe commitText; toque no campo antes. replace=true substitui; default anexa. Devolve o texto final lido do editor.

  • Parâmetros: observe, replace, text · obrigatórios: text

key

Evento de tecla: BACK (finaliza a activity corrente), DEL (apaga último caractere da EditText), ENTER (no editor do IME — Compose — executa a IME action do EditorInfo via performEditorAction; senão entregue sem efeito). Outras teclas: erro tipado NOT_IMPLEMENTED com a lista suportada.

  • Parâmetros: key, observe · obrigatórios: key

wait

Avança o clock virtual (ms) e executa os runnables do Looper com deadline vencida. Retorna quantos rodaram. Cap RD_MCP_MAX_WAIT_MS (default 60_000) — contra tempo ilimitado.

  • Parâmetros: ms, observe · obrigatórios: ms

wait_for

Espera CONDICIONAL: avança o clock virtual em passos de step_ms (default 100) até a view (resource_id/text/class) existir ou timeout_ms vencer (cap RD_MCP_MAX_WAIT_MS). class casa o nome completo ou o nome simples exato (issue #78). found=false é resposta honesta (não é erro) — o agente decide.

  • Parâmetros: class, observe, resource_id, step_ms, text, timeout_ms · obrigatórios: timeout_ms

ui_tree

Dump da UI corrente: xml (uiautomator, formato dos seletores) ou text (árvore textual). Views GONE não aparecem.

  • Parâmetros: format

screenshot

Screenshot PNG determinístico do viewport ativo (720×1440 retrato, 1440×720 paisagem). Com path escreve o arquivo (DENTRO do sandbox — RD_MCP_SANDBOX; symlink no destino é recusado: SYMLINK_NOT_ALLOWED, issue #67); sem, devolve o PNG em base64 (conteúdo image).

  • Parâmetros: path

logs

Saída do app (System.out/System.err) acumulada na sessão. clear=true limpa após ler.

  • Parâmetros: clear

invoke

Invoca um método static no app em execução (sonda de estado geral — o ‘eval’ do agente). Exceções Java voltam tipadas.

  • Parâmetros: args, class, method, sig · obrigatórios: class, method, sig

assert_view

Asserção de existência: procura view por resource-id (ex.: com.app:id/btn), trecho de texto ou classe. class casa o nome COMPLETO (android.widget.TextView) ou o nome SIMPLES exato (TextView) — View NÃO casa TextView. Retorna matches.

  • Parâmetros: class, resource_id, text

assert_text

Asserção de conteúdo: o texto da view com resource_id é igual a expected (ou contém, com contains=true).

  • Parâmetros: contains, expected, resource_id · obrigatórios: resource_id, expected

assert_activity

Asserção: a activity corrente é activity (com.ex.Main ou Lcom/ex/Main;).

  • Parâmetros: activity · obrigatórios: activity

assert_finished

Asserção: a activity corrente terminou (finish() chamado).

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

app_info

Identidade do app ATIVO: package, versão, SDKs, floor e componentes do manifest. engines registra os 28 itens do Apêndice G e detecta assinaturas/candidatos por nomes ZIP/manifest; não valida payload nem promete execução. Features selecionam contratos, não runtimes.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

package_list

Lista os packages instalados NO REGISTRO da sessão (multi-app), marcando o ativo.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

package_remove

Desinstala um package do registro. Se estiver EM EXECUÇÃO, o app é encerrado antes (nunca estado inconsistente). Se era o ativo, o ativo vira o último remanescente.

  • Parâmetros: package · obrigatórios: package

package_clear

Limpa os DADOS de um package (Android clear data): permissões runtime voltam ao estado de instalação e o app em execução é encerrado. Permanece instalado.

  • Parâmetros: package · obrigatórios: package

permissions_list

Permissões declaradas pelo app com o estado atual (granted/denied/runtime-pending/special).

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

permissions_grant

Concede uma permissão (runtime/special) na sessão.

  • Parâmetros: permission · obrigatórios: permission

permissions_revoke

Revoga uma permissão na sessão.

  • Parâmetros: permission · obrigatórios: permission

permissions_role

Torna o app holder de um role do Android (ex.: SMS, Apêndice B6) ou tira o role. Enquanto é holder, as permissões ligadas ao role ficam concedidas; ao sair, voltam ao estado inicial.

  • Parâmetros: held, role · obrigatórios: role

permissions_auto_revoke

Revoga permissões runtime sem uso (Apêndice B6). Exige targetSdk ≥ 30 e dias sem uso ≥ limiar (padrão 90).

  • Parâmetros: days_unused, threshold_days · obrigatórios: days_unused

permissions_audit

Auditoria estática do manifest (exported sem guarda, debuggable, cleartext, permissões desconhecidas).

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

device_profile

Perfil de device corrente (piso contratual moto-e5, budgets e snapshot de periféricos virtuais M10) e controle determinístico AG-10 via action opcional (get, location, sensor, battery, network, telephony, sms_receive, ble_advertisement, nfc_tag, camera_frame, biometric, audio_input, media_action, dark_mode, locale, font_scale, orientation, clipboard) + Apêndice E programável (gms: availability, conta/Sign-In fake, token/mensagem FCM, catálogo/resultado Billing, falha Ads, Integrity/SafetyNet, Fit, Cast; gms_state: snapshot capturado — analytics, compras, ads, crashes, maps). Sem rede: modo no-gms-honest.

  • Parâmetros: accuracy, action, address, ads_clear_failure, ads_failure_code, airplane_mode, altitude, attestation_jws, bearing, billing_error_code, billing_outcome, billing_sku, bytes_hex, call_state, camera_id, carrier_name, cast_device, cast_disconnect, charging, command, enabled, enrolled, fcm_body, fcm_data, fcm_from, fcm_title, fcm_token, firebase_strict_init, fit_steps, format, gms_account_email, gms_account_name, gms_availability, gms_signin, hardware_present, height, id_hex, integrity_token, label, latitude, level, locale, longitude, metered, name, network_type, online, orientation, outcome, payload_hex, pcm_hex, persist, plugged, power_save_mode, roaming, route, rssi, scale, seek_ms, sender, sensor, sensor_type, sim_state, speed, step_route, temperature_tenths_c, text, transport, uri, values, width

behavior_switches

Comutadores de comportamento targetSdk 26→36 ativos para o app instalado (PRF-07).

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

runtime_health

Saúde do runtime: sessão, app em execução, activity, finished, clock virtual, heap, fuel, fila do Looper, bytes de log e tamanho do registro — sem exigir app (reporta o que existe). Inclui gc (gerações minor/major, chaves fracas, pausas), heap peak e jit quando compilado com a feature jit. gc=true força coleta major. Fuel é cumulativo; cada tool inicia uma janela de execução limitada nova.

  • Parâmetros: gc

compat_gaps

Catálogo HONESTO das lacunas de compatibilidade do runtime v1 (notificações M9, args String/array na sonda, foco, teclas, gestures, intent implícito, transporte HTTP) + sumários executáveis dos Apêndices C (data/api-coverage.toml), D (data/jetpack.toml: AndroidX/Jetpack) e E (data/gms.toml: GMS/Firebase sem rede) + superfícies stub/not_implemented referenciadas pelo app activo (app_library_gaps) — o agente consulta antes de planejar.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

batch

Executa uma lista de chamadas [{name, arguments}] EM ORDEM, uma vez cada, com resultados por passo. stop_on_error (default true) para no 1º erro; resume_from pula os N primeiros passos já executados — retomada idempotente. Cap RD_MCP_MAX_BATCH (default 64). batch não aninha. Validação de formato (name obrigatório/não vazio, sem batch aninhado, arguments objeto) rola sobre o lote INTEIRO antes de executar: passo inválido ⇒ NADA é executado (issue #80).

  • Parâmetros: calls, resume_from, stop_on_error · obrigatórios: calls

get_api_usage

AG-09 (metade estática): quais APIs android.* o app instalado REFERENCIA nos DEX — tipos (method_ids/field_ids/superclass/interfaces), métodos por classe, contagem por pacote e classificação Apêndice C (api_coverage: domínio funcional/status/gaps via data/api-coverage.toml), mais os tipos androidx.* contra o Apêndice D (jetpack, data/jetpack.toml) e com.google.android.gms./com.google.firebase. contra o Apêndice E (gms, data/gms.toml, modo no-gms-honest: registro ≠ backend). É análise ESTÁTICA do DEX; para coverage de EXECUÇÃO use get_coverage. Com package consulta outro app instalado; sem, o app ativo.

  • Parâmetros: package

get_coverage

AG-09 (metade dinâmica): cobertura de EXECUÇÃO do app em uso, nível de MÉTODO — instrumentação no interpretador registra cada corpo DEX executado. Requer app lançado (senão NOT_RUNNING); a contagem é do processo atual (reiniciar o app zera). Denominador: métodos com corpo nos DEX do app (abstract/native e classes host ficam fora).

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

component_service

M9: enable an APK-declared IME, accessibility, notification listener or widget provider. Runs its DEX lifecycle; returns the component object handle.

  • Parâmetros: class, role · obrigatórios: class, role

widgets

M9: list/allocate/bind/delete widgets or click a RemoteViews PendingIntent. Provider is an object handle returned by component_service.

  • Parâmetros: action, host, id, provider, view_id

widget_screenshot

M9: render the current RemoteViews widget through the normal deterministic PNG renderer.

  • Parâmetros: id · obrigatórios: id

ime

M9: inspect/focus the editor, select UTF-16 range, commit/compose text, delete surrounding code units or finish composition.

  • Parâmetros: action, after, before, codepoints, cursor, end, start, text, view

accessibility

M9: inspect visible accessibility nodes/events or perform a node action by object id. Action 16 click, 1 focus, 64 accessibility focus, 2097152 set text.

  • Parâmetros: action, action_id, node, text

shortcuts

M9: list current dynamic/pinned shortcuts or launch an enabled shortcut by id.

  • Parâmetros: action, id

native_state

M9: native feature availability, ABI, loaded ELF libraries and guest instruction/memory accounting. Never claims a library ran merely because it was loaded.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

notifications

M9: list active notifications/channels or click/cancel a notification (tag/id and optional action index). Uses the app NotificationManager state.

  • Parâmetros: action, action_index, id, tag

observe

See the screen WITHOUT a screenshot: semantic model of the current frame derived from the recorded display list (works for Views, Compose and custom canvases) merged with the host view tree. Returns visible texts with bounds, probable tap targets (label + center x,y; source frame|view), images and a frame version that only changes when visible content changes, plus a diff (+added/-removed texts) since the previous observe. format=text (default, compact, LLM-friendly) or json (structured; boxes=true adds drawn boxes). ~10-100x cheaper than screenshot (no rasterize/PNG). Also available as subscribable MCP resources rustydroid://screen and rustydroid://screen.txt.

  • Parâmetros: boxes, diff, format

tap_text

Tap by visible label instead of coordinates: finds the tap target (or text) whose label matches text on the current frame (case/space-insensitive substring; exact=true for equality; nth picks among matches in reading order) and taps its center. Error VIEW_NOT_FOUND lists the visible texts. Works on Compose UIs (labels come from the drawn frame).

  • Parâmetros: exact, nth, observe, text · obrigatórios: text

find_views

Find structured host views by AND-combined selectors. Text is exact by default; contains=true opts into substring. Reports bounded matches, total, truncation, xywh bounds and an opaque session/revision token. Snapshots visit at most 10000 nodes; returned text is a UTF-8 prefix of at most 4096 bytes with explicit text_bytes/text_truncated. Tokens expire after potentially mutating tools, including waits and failed attempts. Not a Canvas/Compose query: use observe for those.

  • Parâmetros: class, clickable, contains, enabled, limit, resource_id, text, visible

tap_view

Tap a uniquely matched visible enabled host view, rejecting ambiguity, incomplete trees, stale expected_token and occluded centers before injecting input. Coordinates are clipped to the 720x1440 viewport. Does not claim listener success when none fired.

  • Parâmetros: class, clickable, contains, enabled, expected_token, observe, resource_id, text, visible

wait_for_view

Wait for a host selector to become present or absent, polling virtual time under existing wait/fuel budgets. A timeout is condition_met=false, never a successful assertion. Limited to 1000 time steps. Incomplete trees cannot prove absence.

  • Parâmetros: class, clickable, contains, enabled, observe, resource_id, state, step_ms, text, timeout_ms, visible

session_info

Inspect session identity, active versus running package, compiled capabilities and policy limits without launching an app or collecting garbage. Sandbox roots are reported only as a count, never paths. This complements runtime_health; compiled capability flags do not promise runtime availability.

  • Parâmetros: nenhum

logs_tail

Read at most max_bytes raw log bytes (default 4096, cap 65536). Without cursor, returns the newest bytes; next_cursor supports lossless incremental reads. Cursors bind this session, a clear-generation and byte offset; logs(clear=true) invalidates old cursors even after the buffer regrows. data_b64 is authoritative across UTF-8 boundaries; text is explicitly lossy when needed. Read-only; does not clear or cap the underlying legacy log buffer.

  • Parâmetros: cursor, max_bytes

last_error

Inspect the latest typed tool failure, including early validation failures, batch child failures and isolated runtime panics. Retains bounded UTF-8 error context, not input arguments; does not separately capture logs or stack traces. Original error messages may contain app-provided text. Successful tools do not erase it. clear=true clears only the snapshot, not the cumulative error count. Protocol parse/method errors are not tool failures.

  • Parâmetros: clear

Seeing the screen without screenshots (observe, resources, live viewer)

RustyDroid renders every frame itself (tiny-skia-style software raster of the display list the app records through android.graphics.Canvas / RenderNode). That means the runtime already knows what is on screen as data, before any pixel exists. Round 6 exposes that knowledge to agents and humans:

SurfaceForWhat it givesCost (Comprix, release, 720×1440)
observe toolagentsvisible texts with bounds, tap targets (label + centre), icons, frame version, diff since last observe45 ms when a new frame must be recorded · 0.1–0.4 ms when nothing changed
tap_text toolagentstap by visible label ("Continuar", "Ajustes") instead of coordinates25–180 ms (tap + app work)
observe: true on launch/tap/tap_text/swipe/type_text/key/wait/wait_foragentsthe action result carries the new screen summary → 1 round-trip per step+45 ms
MCP resources rustydroid://screen (JSON), rustydroid://screen.txt, rustydroid://screen.png, rustydroid://logsMCP clientsresources/read + resources/subscribe → notifications/resources/updated whenever visible content changes—
rd mcp --live 0.0.0.0:7878 (or RD_MCP_LIVE)humansbrowser page with the RustyDroid-rendered frame, the screen text, tap-target overlay (checkbox “tap targets”), package/activity, last tool + latency, frame version; long-poll push (/state.json?since=N, ≤20 s)PNG served from /frame.png (see the routes below)
screenshotbothPNG, now cached per frame version and deflate-compressed (adaptive row filters; ~190 KB instead of ~3.1 MB)~75 ms fresh · 1.4 ms repeated

Before round 6, the only way to see a Compose app was screenshot (0.3–1.6 s, ~3 MB base64 per call) — ui_tree shows one opaque AndroidComposeView node.

How the screen model is built (rd-vm/src/screen_model.rs)

  1. The host draw pass (draw_frame) records the window display list (it runs anyway for screenshots).
  2. Engine::screen_model() walks it with exactly the rasterizer’s rules — matrix concatenation, clip intersection (op clip, clipToBounds, outlines), layer alpha, render nodes and bitmaps — but collects items instead of pixels:
    • Text ops → text runs with glyph-box bounds (measure, ascent/descent of the same glyph atlas the rasterizer uses); runs mostly clipped away or nearly transparent are dropped;
    • filled/stroked rects, rounded rects, ovals, paths, colour fills → boxes;
    • bitmaps (incl. Compose’s vector-icon caches) → images.
  3. Post-processing: painter’s-order occlusion (an item fully under an opaque box drawn later is hidden — sheets and dialogs hide the screen behind them), merge of runs on one baseline, reading order, background detection, targets = smallest box (< 40 % of the screen) enclosing a label, except containers (a box with labels side by side on one row — navigation bars, toolbars) where each label is tapped at its own position.
  4. A content fingerprint drives the frame version: it only changes when the visible content changes, so agents can poll cheaply and subscriptions fire only on real changes.
  5. rd-agent merges the host view tree: clickable host views become targets (source: "view"), host-painted texts (TextView, Button…) are added.

It is toolkit-agnostic (Views, Compose, custom onDraw) because it reads what the app drew, not an accessibility tree the app may not populate.

Caching and invalidation

Any tool that can run app code (everything except observe, ui_tree, screenshot, logs, asserts, info tools) marks the screen dirty. The next observer records one frame; the PNG is cached per version. A finished activity reports finished: true and an empty screen — never a stale frame.

Robustness

  • A runtime panic during a tool no longer kills rd mcp: the release profile unwinds (panic = "unwind"; there are no extern "C" frames — native code runs out of process) and call_tool_isolated turns the panic into an INTERNAL_PANIC tool error, ends the app and keeps the session.
  • A failing draw pass is reported in observe (draw_error), in the screenshot result (warning text) and once in logs.

Example (Comprix v1.6.0, after “Criar e adicionar itens”)

frame v7 · Lbr/com/comprix/presentation/MainActivity; · 25 texts · 5 targets · 13 images
y51    [x113] Compras de janeiro
y233   [x34] Adição rápida
y466   [x30] Ex.: “2 kg de arroz, meia dúzia de ovos, 3 leite”
y542   [x76] Anotando preços em:   [x384] Escolher loja
y1074  [x166] Lista vazia por enquanto.
y1303  [x30] 0 itens   [x128] •   [x158] Total: R$ 0,00   [x529] 0/0 no carrinho
y1377  [x200] Comparar estabelecimentos
-- targets (label @ center x,y):
  "Escolher loja" @ 435,542
  "Adicionar loja" @ 546,704
  "Comparar estabelecimentos" @ 360,1377
-- changed since v6: +["Adição rápida", …] -["Minhas listas", …]

Accessibility labels (round 8)

With advanced-components (enabled by default), the refresh path also calls saved standard View accessibility delegates/providers. It executes the app’s real DEX createAccessibilityNodeInfo and traverses virtual child IDs; no Comprix class names or icon positions are hardcoded. Mutable node text, contentDescription, screen bounds, child IDs and actions support Compose’s provider. Described nodes with bounds augment the frame targets. For example, Comprix exposes Buscar listas, Minhas lojas, and Voltar; tapping Minhas lojas by name opens that screen.

Traversal is bounded at 2,048 nodes. It executes guest code and can be much more expensive than the historical round-6 draw-only timings above; heavy navigation can take seconds. Provider errors are surfaced in the screen’s error/warning field (currently labelled draw_error), not silently ignored. Dialogs use the same provider path, including ContextThemeWrapper base-context delegation and bounded rectilinear Region clipping.

Limits (honest)

  • Images with no drawn text or accessibility description still appear only as icon centres (-- icons @ center). This is not OCR or icon recognition.
  • This is provider-node traversal, not a complete Android accessibility service framework or complete Region API. Boolean Region operations have rectangle/work limits and return structured errors on exhaustion.
  • The virtual clock only advances inside tools (wait, actions): the live viewer shows the latest frame between calls; it does not animate on its own (determinism is a feature for agents).
  • Text inside images rasterized from fonts at runtime is found; text baked into PNG assets is not (no OCR).

Live viewer: routes and page (rd mcp --live)

Served by live_serve_conn in crates/rd-agent/src/observe.rs (std-only HTTP, one thread per connection, Connection: close). The address comes from rd mcp --live <addr> (handled in crates/rd-cli/src/main.rs) or RD_MCP_LIVE (read in crates/rd-agent/src/mcp.rs). The viewer is started in serve_stdio_with (crates/rd-agent/src/mcp.rs) and logs [rd mcp] live viewer: http://<addr>/ to stderr.

RouteResponseNotes
/ or /index.htmlHTML page (LIVE_HTML, observe.rs:765-796)Self-contained page: frame canvas, tap-target overlay, screen text, status pills
/state.jsonJSON stateLong-poll: ?since=N blocks until the frame version passes N, up to 20 s (observe.rs:720-742). Without since it returns at once
/frame.pngimage/png204 No Content while no frame has been recorded yet (observe.rs:744-749)
any other path404 Not FoundEmpty body

The page’s header shows the package and activity, the frame version (frame vN), and the last tool with its latency (last: <tool> <ms> ms, observe.rs:791). It shows the screen text and a draw pass failed message when the host draw fails. The overlay is a checkbox labelled “tap targets” (observe.rs:779).

Successful (200) responses send Cache-Control: no-store. All responses close the connection.

Reliable MCP automation and diagnostics

The generated tool catalog remains the source of truth for all 52 registered tools (catálogo de 2026-11-11). The original 41 tool definitions are preserved; the six additions below complement, rather than replace, the existing tools.

Structured host-view automation

  • find_views returns leaf metadata for AND-combined resource_id, text and/or class selectors. At least one nonblank selector is required. Text is exact by default; contains: true explicitly opts into substring matching. Class names match the full name or exact simple name, not a suffix or subclass.
  • Optional enabled, clickable and visible filters are booleans. Visibility inherits through parents within each window, but not from activity content into a separate dialog window. Enabled state follows actual per-view host hit testing, not an invented parent-enabled rule.
  • Default discovery is visible views, with 50 returned matches; limit is 1–200. Snapshot construction and traversal are capped at 10,000 nodes. A result-count limit is not tree truncation: total_is_exact and truncated distinguish these cases, while has_more is conservative.
  • Returned text is a UTF-8-safe prefix of at most 4,096 bytes. text_bytes and text_truncated disclose this explicitly. Matching and tap identity checks still use the full original text; output clipping never changes which view matches.
  • tap_view requires exactly one matching, visible, enabled target in a complete snapshot. It clips the target center to the 720×1440 viewport and verifies the actual foreground-window hit before injecting input. This includes clickable/visibility/enabled identity, not merely equal labels and bounds. An open dialog cannot accidentally be dismissed by targeting a view behind it. listener_acionado: false honestly means no listener fired; it is not promoted to application-level success.
  • find_views.tree_token can be supplied as tap_view.expected_token. Tokens bind session, package, revision and observed host state. They are optimistic concurrency guards, not authentication tokens. Potentially mutating calls, including waits and failed action attempts, can invalidate them; re-discover immediately before a guarded tap. Read-only diagnostics do not invalidate them. A stale token produces STALE_VIEW before input.
  • wait_for_view polls for state: "present" or "absent" using virtual time, with an immediate initial check. Defaults are 5,000 ms timeout and 100 ms steps. timeout_ms: 0 checks immediately, even under a zero-wait policy. The last step never overshoots the timeout. Existing policy/fuel limits apply, plus at most 1,000 virtual-time steps. polls counts checks, including the initial check. condition_met is the condition result; present separately reports whether a matching view exists. A timeout is not a successful assertion. Incomplete trees cannot prove absence or authorize a unique tap.

Queries target the running engine, which can differ from the active installed package; session_info reports both. Dialog-only activities are supported even without activity content.

These tools inspect the host view hierarchy, not labels painted by Canvas or Compose. Continue to use observe / tap_text for display-list labels and screenshot for visual inspection. Existing assertion tools are unchanged.

Example using the genuine C workbench fixture (the helper call sends a normal MCP tools/call and decodes its text JSON):

selector = {"resource_id": "org.rustydroid.demo.c:id/compute", "clickable": True}
found = call("find_views", selector)
assert found["total"] == 1 and found["total_is_exact"]
result = call("tap_view", {**selector, "expected_token": found["tree_token"]})
assert result["listener_acionado"]  # Application-specific expectation.
ready = call("wait_for_view", {
    "resource_id": "org.rustydroid.demo.c:id/result", "timeout_ms": 0,
})
assert ready["condition_met"]

Runtime diagnostics

  • session_info works before install/launch and after an isolated runtime failure. It distinguishes active from running package, reports compiled capability flags and policy limits, and reports sandbox roots only as a count. Compiled native/JIT support does not promise that a runtime dependency is installed or an application is compatible. Use runtime_health and native_state for detailed runtime accounting. It does not execute guest code, reset its fuel window, force or trigger GC, or mutate the UI revision.
  • logs_tail reads at most max_bytes raw bytes (default 4,096; maximum 65,536). Without a cursor it returns the newest bytes. Save next_cursor and pass it back for subsequent incremental reads; has_more indicates backlog. Cursors bind session identity, clear generation and byte offset. A different session or logs(clear=true) makes an old cursor stale, even if the buffer subsequently grows past the old offset. A future offset is invalid rather than silently clamped. data_b64 is authoritative: decode and concatenate bytes before decoding UTF-8. text is only a convenience view, with text_lossy disclosing invalid/split UTF-8. Reads never clear the buffer or deadlock on a multibyte character split. The legacy log buffer remains session-wide and unbounded; this tool bounds reads, not retention.
  • last_error retains the latest typed tool failure, including early validation returns, failed batch children, and isolated runtime panics. Successful calls do not erase it. clear: true returns then clears the snapshot without clearing logs or resetting the cumulative error-event count. Each retained message field is byte-bounded and UTF-8-safe; truncated and cause_bytes disclose clipping. Original tool results are unchanged. Input arguments are not retained, but the original error message can itself contain app-provided text or paths; this is not secret redaction. Protocol parse/method errors are outside this tool-failure snapshot.

All three diagnostic additions are read-only with respect to the guest, clock, fuel window, GC and UI revision. Clearing an error snapshot only changes its diagnostic bookkeeping.

Validation and reproducible acceptance

Malformed optional values no longer silently become different actions: tap_text (exact, nth), type_text (replace), observe (diff, boxes, format), logs (clear), and runtime_health (gc) reject types outside their existing schemas before app code runs. Valid legacy requests retain their behavior and schemas. New tools reject unknown fields and null/wrong-type options; limits cannot be bypassed by negative, fractional or huge integers.

The genuine native MCP gate requires positive coverage of every registered tool for C, C++ and Rust, on x86_64, arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a, with JIT off/on:

bash golden/native-languages/gate.sh

For longer functional testing, after building the genuine fixtures and a native/JIT-enabled CLI:

python scripts/mcp-session-soak.py --rd target/debug/rd --apks target/native-languages/apks --seconds 600 --out target/mcp-soak

The soak pins its executable, exercises 18 persistent language/ABI/JIT sessions, checks independently computed JNI results, stale-token rejection, presence and absence semantics, repeated PNG equality, warm restarts and forced GC. When available, it also checks diagnostic error context and incremental logs. It stores bounded summaries and response-stream hashes instead of unbounded image transcripts. It is functional endurance evidence, not a performance benchmark.

Compatibility note: numeric visibility

The host now accepts Android setVisibility values 4 (INVISIBLE) and 8 (GONE), alongside the pre-existing 0/1/2 ordinal inputs. The legacy numeric getVisibility convention (0/1/2) is deliberately unchanged in this MCP-focused change; fully aligning that numeric getter with Android needs a separate compatibility decision. Structured selectors use the actual visibility state, not that numeric getter.

Suítes de teste — formato e execução (rd test)

M6 — TST-01 do checklist: rd test suite.json → resumo humano + JUnit XML + exit code. Implementação: crates/rd-agent/src/suite.rs (núcleo) e rd test em crates/rd-cli.

Uso

rd test tests/suites/contract-no-app.json                 # resumo humano
rd test suite.json --junit out/junit.xml                  # + relatório JUnit XML
rd test suite.json --json                                 # resumo em JSON (stdout)

Códigos de saída

exitsignificado
0todos os cenários passaram
1pelo menos um cenário falhou (o JUnit traz o detalhe)
64suíte inválida ou arquivo ilegível — nenhum passo foi executado

Formato

{
  "name": "smoke",
  "scenarios": [
    {
      "name": "abre o app e confere o texto",
      "steps": [
        { "name": "install", "arguments": { "apk": "apps/app.apk" } },
        { "name": "launch",  "arguments": {} },
        { "name": "wait",    "arguments": { "ms": 50 } },
        { "name": "assert_text",
          "arguments": { "resource_id": "com.test:id/tv", "expected": "Olá" } }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "lançar sem APK responde NO_APP",
      "steps": [
        { "name": "launch", "arguments": {}, "expect": "error:NO_APP" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "com hooks e retry (AG-07)",
      "setup": [
        { "name": "install", "arguments": { "apk": "apps/app.apk" } }
      ],
      "steps": [
        { "name": "launch", "arguments": {}, "retries": 2 },
        { "name": "assert_activity", "arguments": { "expected": "com.test/.Main" }, "timeout_ms": 5000 }
      ],
      "teardown": [
        { "name": "package_clear", "arguments": {} }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • name (suíte): obrigatório, não vazio.
  • scenarios: lista obrigatória, com pelo menos um cenário.
  • Cenário: name e steps (pelo menos um passo); hooks opcionais setup e teardown (listas de passos com a mesma gramática — podem ser vazias).
  • Passo: name = nome de uma tool MCP (ver docs/mcp-tools.md); arguments = objeto (opcional, padrão {}); expect (opcional, padrão "ok"); timeout_ms (opcional, inteiro > 0 — orçamento de wall-clock do passo); retries (opcional, inteiro ≥ 0, padrão 0 — tentativas extras após falha).

Regras de execução

  1. Validação antes de executar. Qualquer erro de formato (campo ausente, arguments não objeto, expect inválido, batch dentro de suíte) aborta com INVALID_SUITE e exit 64. Nenhum passo roda.
  2. Isolamento. Cada cenário roda em uma sessão nova do agente (um app por sessão — ADR 001). Um cenário não herda o APK instalado por outro.
  3. Passo ok (padrão) passa quando a tool completa e o resultado não diz que a condição falhou:
    • isError = true → falha, com o código e a causa devolvidos pela tool.
    • "ok": false ou "found": false no resultado → falha.
    • assert_finished devolve {"finished": bool}: "finished": false → falha. As asserções do MCP (assert_text, assert_view, assert_activity, wait_for…) devolvem sucesso na chamada com ok:false quando a condição não se confirma; o executor trata isso como falha. Sem essa regra, toda asserção errada passaria em verde.
  4. Passo "expect": "error:CODIGO" passa somente quando a tool falha com exatamente aquele código estável (ex.: NO_APP, NOT_RUNNING, INVALID_FORMAT). Se a tool completar, ou falhar com outro código, o passo falha.
  5. Primeira falha encerra o cenário. Os passos seguintes são marcados SKIP no JUnit. Os outros cenários continuam.
  6. Caminhos relativos. install.apk relativo é resolvido a partir da pasta do arquivo de suíte, não do diretório atual. Caminhos com .. não são reescritos (a policy de sandbox do agente decide).
  7. timeout_ms por passo. Se presente, o passo tem orçamento de wall-clock: a chamada da tool roda até o fim (não há preempção) e, se o tempo medido exceder o teto, o passo falha com o código estável STEP_TIMEOUT e os passos seguintes são pulados. Vale mesmo com expect: "error:…" — o orçamento é contrato do passo, não da tool. timeout_ms: 0, negativo ou não numérico é INVALID_SUITE (validação antes de executar).
  8. Hooks (AG-07). setup roda antes dos passos; falha no setup aborta o cenário (passos e teardown são marcados SKIP). teardown roda depois dos passos mesmo se eles falharem (limpeza garantida, best-effort: um passo de teardown falho não pula os demais) e falha no teardown reprova o cenário. Hooks aceitam expect, timeout_ms e retries como qualquer passo; no JUnit aparecem com prefixo de fase ([setup 0], [teardown 1]).
  9. Retries (AG-07). retries: N dá N tentativas extras ao passo após falha (qualquer modo: erro inesperado, asserção, STEP_TIMEOUT). A primeira tentativa que passa encerra o retry; cada tentativa é julgada de novo pelo expect/timeout_ms. O tempo reportado é a soma das tentativas; o resultado/log é o da última. attempts aparece no log do JUnit (N tentativas). Retry não muda a regra 5: esgotadas as tentativas, a falha encerra a fase.

Saída

Resumo humano

Suíte: smoke (2 cenário(s))
  PASS  abre o app e confere o texto (4 passo(s), 41 ms)
  FAIL  lançar sem APK responde NO_APP (1 passo(s), 3 ms)
        → passo 0 (launch): esperado erro NO_APP, mas a tool completou sem erro
Resultado: 1 passou, 1 falhou — 46 ms

JUnit XML — um <testcase> por cenário. Falha vira <failure message="…">. O <system-out> traz cada passo com status, tempo e o resultado cru da tool, para auditoria (a mesma filosofia de “saída literal” do projeto).

<testsuites name="rustydroid" tests="2" failures="1" errors="0" time="0.046">
  <testsuite name="smoke" tests="2" failures="1" ...>
    <testcase classname="smoke" name="abre o app e confere o texto" time="0.041">
      <system-out>[0] install PASS (…) …</system-out>
    </testcase>
    <testcase classname="smoke" name="lançar sem APK responde NO_APP" time="0.003">
      <failure message="passo 0 (launch): …" type="ScenarioFailed">…</failure>
      <system-out>…</system-out>
    </testcase>
  </testsuite>
</testsuites>

Limites atuais (M6)

  • Não há coverage (get_coverage, AG-09) — fica para as próximas rodadas.
  • Suítes que exigem APK precisam que o APK esteja no disco no momento da execução (ex.: baixado por golden-apks/fetch.sh, que não é versionado — GH-05).
  • A suíte é executada pelo binário rd; não há driver em outra linguagem.

Arquivos versionados

  • tests/suites/contract-no-app.json — contratos de erro e de estado que rodam sem APK (o CI executa esta suíte).
  • docs/compat-matrix.md lista as suítes em tests/suites/ automaticamente (cargo xtask compat-report).

M9 — Advanced components and NDK

Status: ✅ implemented; human review approved (2026-10-21). The user reviewed and approved the full M9 deliverable in this session. Every M9 capability below is implemented and covered by tests. In all five real F-Droid APKs, the DEX code calls a JNI method and the native code returns a result that is checked independently. The same check passes for each APK’s x86_64, arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a libraries (15/15 runs). See Gate evidence and Known limits for exactly what was and was not verified.

Design decision record: ADR 004.

Architecture

 DEX (rd-vm interpreter)
   │  native method / System.loadLibrary
   ▼
 rd-vm::native  ── JNI function table (JNIEnv*, JavaVM*), local/global refs (rd-jni)
   │  typed calls, no raw pointers into the VM heap
   ▼
 rd-ndk::runtime ── ELF loader (rd-ndk::elf), relocation, imports, libc shim,
   │                arena allocator, watchdog / fuel accounting
   │  line-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout
   ▼
 native_worker.py ── Unicorn 2.1.4 CPU emulator in a separate process
                     (x86_64, AArch64, ARM/Thumb); syscalls/SVC blocked
  • No host dlopen and no new unsafe. Guest code never runs on the host CPU. The Rust side only parses bytes and exchanges IPC messages.
  • GPL isolation. Unicorn is GPL-2.0. It runs in a separate interpreter process launched at runtime. It is never linked into the MIT/Apache binary.
  • Determinism and limits. Every call has an instruction budget (fuel) and a wall-clock watchdog, plus memory and arena caps. Fuel is the deterministic limit: instruction counts are identical across machines, including GitHub runners. The per-call wall-clock net defaults to 30 s (RD_NATIVE_CALL_SECS, 1–120). An earlier 5 s net made armv7 binaryeye flaky under load. JNI arrays and strings are capped at 1,000,000 elements. A failure surfaces as a typed VmExit/Error, never a host crash.
  • Fail-closed libc. Libc imports that are not implemented return a typed NOT_IMPLEMENTED that names the symbol. The fd layer exposes only stdio. Any other descriptor returns EBADF. Lock and condition-variable signalling calls are uncontended successes because the guest is single-threaded. pthread_cond_wait would block forever, so it stays unimplemented.

Crates

CrateRole
rd-ndk (src/elf.rs)Bounded ELF32/ELF64 parser. Supports x86_64, AArch64 and ARM; REL/RELA/JMPREL/RELR; DT_HASH/GNU hash; symbol kinds; DT_INIT/DT_INIT_ARRAY. Errors on any truncation or overflow.
rd-ndk (src/runtime.rs, feature native)Worker client. Handles segment mapping, relocation, lazy function imports and data imports (__stack_chk_guard, __sF, …), and the libc shim. The shim covers the printf family (including %f/%e/%g) with va_list for all three ABIs, string/memory functions, malloc/realloc/free/posix_memalign, a libm subset (hard-float and armeabi-v7a softfp), locale, rlimits, futex, pthread TLS keys, __system_property_get and Android log.
rd-ndk (worker/native_worker.py)Unicorn worker. Sets up the TLS page and stack canary (FS_BASE / TPIDR_EL0 / TPIDRURO), enables VFP on ARM and reports fault PC and address.
rd-jniJNI name mangling (short and overloaded), descriptor parsing, modified UTF-8 and local/global reference frames.
rd-vm (src/native.rs)JNI bridge. Covers FindClass, Get[Static]MethodID/FieldID, Call*Method[V|A] (the V form decodes the guest va_list with each ABI’s rules), New*, strings (including Get/StringRegion, GetStringUTFRegion and GetStringCritical), primitive arrays (Get/Release/Region/Critical), weak globals, monitors, exceptions, RegisterNatives and JNI_OnLoad. Also provides Engine::native_report, Engine::new_instance and Engine::invoke_instance.
rd-vm (src/m9/)Notifications, IME, widgets, accessibility and shortcuts. They share one state model, which app calls and agent tools both see.
rd-agent (src/m9_tools.rs)MCP tools: component_service, widgets, widget_screenshot, ime, accessibility, shortcuts, native_state; notifications is now functional.

Feature flags

CrateFeatureDefaultEffect
rd-vmadvanced-componentsonM9 framework components (src/m9/)
rd-vmnativeoffJNI bridge and System.loadLibrary via rd-ndk
rd-ndknativeoffWorker runtime (without it, only the ELF parser is built)
rd-agent, rd-clinative, advanced-componentsfollows rd-vmforwarded

When native is off, System.loadLibrary and native methods fail with a typed NOT_IMPLEMENTED that points here.

Installing the native worker

pip install unicorn==2.1.4          # or into a private prefix
export RD_NATIVE_PYTHON=python3     # interpreter that can `import unicorn`
cargo build -p rd-cli --features native

RD_NATIVE_PYTHON defaults to python3. The worker script is embedded in the binary (include_str!) and passed to the interpreter with -c, so nothing is written to disk.

ABI fixtures for the tests are built from golden/native/fixture.c with bash golden/native/build.sh. This needs gcc, gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu and gcc-arm-linux-gnueabihf. The artifacts are gitignored.

Supported surface

SYS-09 — notifications, IME, widgets

  • Notifications. Covers channels and groups, NotificationChannel getters/setters (importance cannot change after registration), and Notification.Builder and NotificationCompat.Builder. The builder supports title, text, subtext, channel, group/summary, category, small icon, ongoing, auto-cancel, only-alert-once, visibility, priority, number, progress, content and delete intents, setTimeoutAfter, actions and BigTextStyle. Also covered: notify/cancel/cancelAll and the targetSdk 33+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission gate (denied by default for targetSdk ≥ 33; agents grant it explicitly). PendingIntent (getActivity/getBroadcast/getService/getForegroundService) is dispatched into the DEX. On targetSdk ≥ 31 it requires a mutability flag, as on Android. Clicking a notification fires its intent and applies auto-cancel. Timeouts expire notifications, and NotificationListenerService posted/removed callbacks are delivered.
  • IME. Covers focus and keyboard visibility on EditText, InputConnection (commitText, setComposingText, finishComposingText, deleteSurroundingText, setSelection, performEditorAction), and the InputMethodService lifecycle (onCreate, onStartInput, onFinishInput). Text and selection handling are Unicode-correct.
  • Widgets (RemoteViews). Covers AppWidgetManager/AppWidgetHost allocate, bind and delete, and the AppWidgetProvider DEX lifecycle (onEnabled, onUpdate, onDeleted, onDisabled). RemoteViews supports setTextViewText, setViewVisibility, setOnClickPendingIntent and setBoolean(id, "setEnabled", …). Other RemoteViews setters are not intercepted; other setBoolean targets fail with NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Widgets render into the same UiNode tree as activities, and widget_screenshot captures them. Clicking a widget dispatches its PendingIntent.

SYS-10 — accessibility and shortcuts

  • Accessibility. Builds a node tree from the live view hierarchy, including content descriptions. AccessibilityEvent objects are delivered to registered AccessibilityService DEX callbacks. Supported actions are focus, click and set text, and set text goes through the same editor model as the IME.
  • Shortcuts. Covers ShortcutManager: set/add/update/remove/ removeAll dynamic shortcuts, enable/disable, requestPinShortcut, getDynamicShortcuts/getPinnedShortcuts, ShortcutInfo.Builder (labels, intent, rank) and launch through intent dispatch. ShortcutManagerCompat is not intercepted; it falls through to the APK’s androidx DEX.

LANG-02 — NDK

  • ELF loading and relocation for x86_64, AArch64 and ARM (EABI5, hard-float).
  • JNI_OnLoad, static symbol lookup by mangled name, and RegisterNatives.
  • Primitive, wide and float/double arguments and returns. Up to 8 integer-class arguments have been tested, plus stack spill.
  • Strings (modified UTF-8), primitive arrays (get/release/region), callbacks into Java, and exceptions in both directions. A native Throw becomes a VM exception.
  • Repeated loadLibrary calls do not re-run constructors.

Known limits

These are deliberately unsupported and fail typed rather than silently:

  • No threads. pthread_create and pthread_cond_wait are not implemented. de.jurihock.voicesmith’s libvoicesmith is driven through JNA (libjnidispatch, see below), not JNI, so it is not part of the gate.
  • Nested native reentrancy is refused. This means native code calling Java that then calls another native method.
  • Syscalls and SVC are blocked in the worker. The fd layer only exposes stdio, and everything else returns EBADF.
  • Large arrays. JNI arrays are capped at 1,000,000 elements. termux-bootstrap’s roughly 30 MB getZip array exceeds that.
  • JNA libjnidispatch. JNI_OnLoad returns 0 because its java.lang reflection lookups are not implemented.
  • RemoteViews ProgressBar, image/colour setters and collection widgets (RemoteViewsService) are not implemented.
  • No real text shaping in widget screenshots. They use the M4 bitmap font.
  • Components were verified on fixture APKs. Notifications, IME, widgets, accessibility and shortcuts were tested with rd-testsupport’s test.m9 fixture and the agent tools, not with a third-party app.
  • TFLite inference. Model loading needs direct ByteBuffers (NewDirectByteBuffer/GetDirectBufferAddress), which are not implemented.
  • Performance. Emulation through Unicorn plus IPC is orders of magnitude slower than native code. That is acceptable for testing and agent work, not for running heavy native workloads.

Gate evidence

Fixture tests (all three ABIs):

  • cargo test -p rd-ndk --features native: load, relocate, initialize and execute; fuel-bounded infinite loop; every truncated prefix of an ELF fails cleanly.
  • cargo test -p rd-vm --features native --test native: Dalvik → JNI round-trips on x86_64, arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a (softfp). Covers add, wide, float, 8 arguments, strings, echo, arrays, mutate, callback, RegisterNatives, throw, snprintf integer formatting, GetStringUTFRegion/GetStringRegion, ExceptionCheck, floating varargs (%.3f %g %.2e) with fmodf/floor, and a missing import (getaddrinfo) reported as NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
  • cargo test -p rd-ndk --features native --lib: %f/%e/%g rendering checked against C printf (18 cases, including round-half-even).
  • cargo test -p rd-vm --test m9: 7 component tests (IME, InputConnection and IME lifecycle, notifications, channels, RemoteViews/widget provider, accessibility, and unknown APIs failing typed).
  • ELF parser mutation campaign (crates/rd-ndk/examples/elf_campaign.rs): over 164M mutated inputs (about 130M of them accepted as structurally valid) ran in 12 minutes with no panic.

Real APKs: bash golden-apks/native-gate.sh (pinned by SHA-256, cached under golden-apks/cache/, output in target/m9-native-gate.json). Every APK must make at least one JNI method call from its real DEX, and the script checks each result. RD_NATIVE_ABI=arm64-v8a or RD_NATIVE_ABI=armeabi-v7a runs the same APKs’ ARM libraries; the output goes to target/m9-native-gate-<abi>.json. The CI native job runs the gate on all three ABIs, with the APKs cached by script hash.

Several fixes and additions came out of this work:

  • JNI table bug. Slots 226–228 were off by two; per the JNI spec, ExceptionCheck is 228. This is now fixed.
  • Instruction accounting bug. The worker reports a running per-call total with every event, and the client used to add each report again. That inflated the counts; for example, an earlier note said the QR call took about 1.09 billion instructions. Only the increments are counted now. The 5M per-call fuel cap was always enforced by the worker itself.
  • ARM fixes.
    • The SVC detector tested Thumb-2 32-bit encodings as ARM-mode SVCs. It now checks the CPSR T bit, which removes false positives.
    • Unused jvalue bytes and r1 are dropped for 32-bit values.
    • Variadic J/D/F arguments now use aligned register pairs, with float promoted to double.
    • getauxval returns the HWCAPs Unicorn emulates.
  • New JNI functions. GetStringRegion, GetStringUTFRegion, Get/ReleasePrimitiveArrayCritical, Get/ReleaseStringCritical and MonitorEnter/Exit.
  • New libc/libm shims. memchr, wmemchr, wcslen, strncmp, strstr, __strchr_chk, posix_memalign, the libm subset and C-exact %f/%e/%g (unit-tested against C printf, including round-half-even).

Limite conhecido: instruções AVX (VEX/EVEX) no worker (issue #400)

O Unicorn 2.1.4 executa código VEX/EVEX de forma errada: floor(5.5)+0.25 virava 0.25 numa biblioteca compilada para x86-64-v3. Por isso o worker rejeita essas codificações com NOT_IMPLEMENTED antes de executar a instrução, em vez de devolver um valor errado em silêncio.

  • Fixtures de referência usam -march=x86-64 (baseline SSE2). golden/native/build.sh também gera x86_64-avx2.so (-march=x86-64-v3) como fixture negativa.
  • Teste: avx_encoded_guest_code_is_rejected_fail_closed_400 (crates/rd-ndk/tests/native.rs).
  • Bibliotecas reais compiladas com AVX não rodam neste worker. Esse é o limite documentado, não um suporte. A correção definitiva depende de um Unicorn com VEX correto ou de outro emulador.

Real C, C++, and Rust APK execution

What is implemented

The opt-in native-engines feature supplies executing c-ndk, cpp-ndk, and rust-ndk registry adapters. They share the existing bounded Android DEX → JNI → ELF → isolated Unicorn worker route; they are not new language interpreters. MCP launch.engine explicitly prepares the VM through the same native adapter parser. native_state.selected_engine identifies that selection. A filename or ELF signature never identifies a source language or authorizes execution.

The other 25 registered adapters remain NOT_IMPLEMENTED. LANG features alone still select contracts. Default advanced-components and the independent native and JIT feature gates remain supported. Detection/listing is static and always reports execution_claimed=false, even when an adapter is AVAILABLE_BOUNDED. Only runtime evidence with positive machine-instruction counts claims execution.

Source-built Android applications

golden/native-languages/ contains three project-owned demonstration APKs, not third-party applications. Each has a real binary Android manifest, compiled resources, Java-to-DEX UI glue, and Android-targeted JNI native cores for x86_64, arm64-v8a, and armeabi-v7a:

  • C: Android NDK r27c clang, C11.
  • C++: NDK r27c clang++, C++20 templates and std::array headers; exceptions and RTTI disabled, no dynamically linked C++ runtime.
  • Rust: rustc Android targets, no_std, panic=abort, with the NDK linker; not an x86 Linux .so renamed as an Android library.

digest(int,int) consumes two signed integers as eight little-endian bytes, using FNV-1a seeded by a language tag and returning the low 31 bits. nativeFlavor() returns the language tag. There is no Java implementation of these native methods or fallback arithmetic. The independent Python/Rust test oracles are outside the APKs. Java provides the Android UI and component glue, as in an ordinary JNI Android app; the native cores are the three languages being demonstrated.

Each APK has inputs, compute/persisted result, notification, pinned shortcut, detail activity, finish control, widget provider, accessibility service, input method service, and notification listener. They are signed with a generated development-only certificate; never use that key/password in production.

Reproduce

Build prerequisites: Linux x86_64, JDK (java, javac, keytool), aapt, apksigner, zipalign, unzip, Python 3, and Rust with these targets:

rustup target add x86_64-linux-android aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi
python golden/native-languages/build.py --out /tmp/native-language-apks
python -m pip install unicorn==2.1.4
cargo build -p rd-cli --features native-engines
./target/debug/rd engine check rust-ndk --json
./target/debug/rd engine run rust-ndk /tmp/native-language-apks/native-rust.apk --json

The builder downloads SHA-256-pinned official platform 26, NDK r27c, and R8 8.5.35 inputs. It compiles with minSdk 26/targetSdk 34, verifies APK v2/v3 signatures with apksigner, and emits provenance.json containing source, compiler, APK, library, and ELF-machine evidence. Downloads, private debug key, classes, .so files, and APKs remain outside Git under cache/target/output. The runtime’s MSRV remains Rust 1.76; the builder records the actual compiler.

Run every MCP tool positively for each APK and each guest ABI:

for abi in x86_64 arm64-v8a armeabi-v7a; do
  python scripts/native-languages-mcp.py \
    --rd target/debug/rd --apks /tmp/native-language-apks \
    --out /tmp/native-language-evidence/$abi --abi $abi
done

This is a real newline-delimited JSON-RPC MCP stdio client, not direct handler calls. It obtains the server’s tool catalog, requires exactly 52 tools (the catalog of rd mcp, see docs/mcp-tools.md), checks argument names/required fields, rejects unsuccessful assertions, and requires positive coverage of all 50 for every language/ABI. Expected negative errors are counted separately and cannot satisfy positive coverage. Outputs include raw request/response JSONL, per-tool positive/negative counts, native instruction counters/ABI, APK SHA-256, PNG screenshots, and machine-readable summaries.

The campaign independently checks signed integer extremes, input through keyboard/IME/accessibility, actual compute callbacks and logs, screenshots, service activation, widget bind/render/delete, notification post/click/cancel, shortcut publication/launch, detail navigation, forced major GC while Main is suspended, BACK restoration, another native computation after restoration, warm launch with persisted result, finish, package clear/remove, permissions, coverage, batching, and diagnostics. Unsupported engines, invalid arguments, missing methods/views, and sandbox escape fail with typed errors. A failed method lookup must not increment native instruction counts.

The public adapter parse/event/syscall contract has a separate real-APK gate:

RD_NATIVE_LANGUAGE_APKS=/tmp/native-language-apks \
  cargo test -p rd-engine-registry --features native-execution \
  --test native_execution -- --ignored --nocapture

Run it once per ABI using RD_NATIVE_ABI, or use the MCP matrix above. The external-APK test is explicitly ignored by ordinary offline unit tests; the availability/metadata tests and VM history/dispatch tests run without the SDK.

The gate also runs the public engine run --json CLI regression test for all three languages on each ABI. It requires one clean JSON artifact on stdout, guest output captured in logs, an executing native report, and the expected UI text. Missing source APK fixtures fail the explicitly requested test rather than silently skipping it. Ordinary unit tests independently cover invocation validation at the unchanged 16 KiB payload and 16 signed-integer argument boundaries, including malformed JSON, duplicate/unknown fields and overflow.

MCP selection

After install, call:

{"name":"launch","arguments":{"engine":"rust-ndk"}}

Use c-ndk or cpp-ndk for the other source-built packages. No selection means the existing generic Android route. A warm launch preserves a selected backend for the same running package; switching explicit backend rebuilds the process. Unsupported adapters and builds without native-engines return NOT_IMPLEMENTED; unknown IDs return UNKNOWN_ENGINE. They never fall back to another language adapter. native_state is diagnostic; invoke performs method calls. runtime_health with gc=true forces major collection.

Runtime fixes supporting the proof

  • D8-inherited Android method owners resolve through bounded/cycle-checked platform ancestors after DEX override resolution. Concrete View/TextView/ Context handlers precede generic property storage, preserving IDs and text. Direct VM invocation shares that host ancestor resolver.
  • Context navigation has bounded (64 suspended entries) single-task history, strong GC roots, lifecycle dispatch, focus/IME restoration, failed-launch recovery, and idempotent finish/BACK. Explicit MCP root relaunch replaces old history. Actual heap activity class drives MCP activity/health metadata.
  • Snapshot and widget screenshots now use the VM Canvas embedded antialiased glyph atlas instead of checkerboard pseudo-text. They remain headless snapshots, not pixel-perfect Android theme rendering.
  • CLI native forwards to the agent too. The previous missing forwarding could make an executing native VM appear disabled through MCP diagnostics.
  • engine run --json captures app stdout instead of corrupting the JSON output; APK input is bounded to 256 MiB, including a growing-file read bound.
  • Deliberately corrupted native payloads fail closed in all nine language/ABI combinations; a launch error cannot print success JSON or fallback output.

Explicit limits

This demonstrates bounded real execution, not universal C/C++/Rust Android compatibility. It is not a complete Android OS, NDK/libc/JNI implementation, complete STL/C++ exception runtime, Rust std/async runtime, arbitrary host syscall bridge, or graphical GPU implementation. The Java UI/components run in the project’s headless Android model. Guest machine code runs in Unicorn on this host, not on a physical Android phone. Task history is single-task and does not implement all Android launch modes, tasks, process restoration, or services. Actual hardware installation and device testing are separate from this gate. The explicit native adapter launcher currently rejects activity aliases; use the generic MCP route for those APKs. The GitHub Actions job is added here; local execution is not evidence that remote CI has run or passed.

Source attribution comes from the committed source/build provenance, not from guessing a language from ELF. A successful demonstration APK does not establish compatibility with every third-party APK written in that language.

M10 — Virtual devices, sensors, media, connectivity, and dynamic system config

Status: ✅ implemented (MEDIA-01..08, NET-05..06, SYS-07, AG-10). Every M10 subsystem runs deterministically in pure safe Rust per Engine instance with zero host OS hardware access, zero unsafe in rd-vm / rd-agent, and full integration with Dalvik DEX callbacks, permission checks, and the MCP agent surface.

Design decision record: ADR 011.

Architecture

 MCP client / rd test
   │  device_profile({ "action": "location" | "sensor" | "battery" | ... })
   ▼
 rd-agent::m10_tools ── validates arguments, materializes Engine, bumps ui_epoch
   │
   ▼
 rd-vm::m10 (per-Engine State)
   ├── sensors.rs       MEDIA-01  SensorManager, 8 Moto E5 sensors, SensorEventListener
   ├── location.rs      MEDIA-02  LocationManager, FusedLocationProviderClient, Haversine, routes
   ├── camera.rs        MEDIA-03  Camera2, CameraCaptureSession, ImageReader RGBA8888/JPEG
   ├── biometrics.rs    MEDIA-04  Framework + AndroidX BiometricPrompt, FingerprintManager
   ├── media.rs         MEDIA-05..08  AudioManager/Record/Track, MediaPlayer, MediaSession, MediaProjection
   ├── connectivity.rs  NET-05..06  Connectivity/Telephony/SMS, Bluetooth LE scan+GATT, NFC NDEF
   └── sysconfig.rs     SYS-07    Battery/PowerManager WakeLock, dark mode/locale/scale/orientation, Clipboard
  • Per-Engine isolation (Law 2 & Law 9). All virtual peripheral state lives in Engine.fw.m10 (crates/rd-vm/src/m10/mod.rs). No thread_local!, global singletons, or host OS hardware calls exist anywhere in M10.
  • GC-safe transient payloads. High-frequency callback objects (SensorEvent, Location, ImageReader planes, ScanResult, NdefMessage, ClipData) store payloads directly in VM heap fields and primitive arrays so the mark-compact GC collects them automatically without unbounded host maps.
  • Coexistence with Appendix C absent-hardware defaults. Raw Engine::new() starts with m10.virtual_hardware_enabled = false so Appendix C’s sensorless / camera-less / radio-less unit-test profile stays intact. Launching an app through rd-agent (AgentSession), calling Engine::m10_enable_virtual_devices(), or invoking any AG-10 mutation enables virtual peripherals ahead of the absent-hardware stubs in crates/rd-vm/src/intrinsics.rs.
  • Stable 47-tool MCP catalog. AG-10 multiplexes 18 action modes onto device_profile (crates/rd-agent/src/m10_tools.rs), preserving the locked 52-tool MCP contract (docs/mcp-tools.md) and the no-app Moto E5 floor response when action is omitted or "get".

Feature flags

Opt-in na compilação: virtual-devices não está em default (Cargo.toml). A ativação por execução (rd app run --virtual-devices) existe no branch do Zoom (PR #626) e ainda não está em main; ver a emenda da ADR 011.

CrateFeatureDefaultEffect
rd-vmvirtual-devicesoff (implies advanced-components)Enables crates/rd-vm/src/m10/ and interpreter/intrinsic dispatch
rd-agentvirtual-devicesoffEnables AG-10 device_profile mutations and live virtual_devices snapshot
rd-clivirtual-devicesoffForwards virtual-devices to rd-vm and rd-agent

When compiled with --no-default-features, device_profile still serves the read-only Moto E5 profile (virtual_devices: null) and returns typed NOT_IMPLEMENTED on mutating actions.

Supported surface

MEDIA-01Virtual sensorsSensorManager (getDefaultSensor, getSensorList, registerListener, unregisterListener), Sensor, SensorEvent (values, accuracy, timestamp) for accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, light, proximity, pressure, gravity, step counter
MEDIA-02Virtual GPS & routesLocationManager (getLastKnownLocation, requestLocationUpdates, removeUpdates, isProviderEnabled), Location (distanceBetween / distanceTo / bearingTo Haversine), LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient (getLastLocation, requestLocationUpdates, removeLocationUpdates)

Gate evidence

  • cargo test -p rd-vm --test m10 — 9 end-to-end Dalvik DEX callback, interpreter dispatch, GC compaction, and SecurityException tests.
  • cargo test -p rd-agent --test m10_mcp — 47-tool catalog lock, no-app contract, and all 17 mutating AG-10 actions against a live AgentSession.
