M11 — Engine WASM (slices S1, S1b, S1c)

Decisão e critério de “rodar”: ADR 013. Este documento descreve o que já executa e o que ainda não executa.

Status

Parcial (S1 + S1b + S1c: VM, APK e registro/CLI). O núcleo está em crates/rd-engine-wasm: parser, validador, interpretador do subconjunto MVP i32/i64, limites, fuel e harness de fuzzing. A bridge io.rustydroid.wasm.WasmBridge está em crates/rd-vm/src/wasm_bridge.rs, atrás da feature wasm-engine (desligada por padrão). Dois goldens de VM a exercitam:

  • crates/rd-vm/tests/wasm_bridge.rs: DEX e módulo montados no teste, Activity chama a bridge em onCreate via launch_app.
  • crates/rd-vm/tests/wasm_demo_golden.rs + golden/engines/wasm/: APK de demonstração de verdade (rd_testsupport::wasm_demo), com classes.dex e assets/demo.wasm lidos do ZIP. O TextView tem de mostrar 5 (add(2, 3)).

A suíte rd test golden/engines/wasm/suite.json roda sobre esse APK (install → launch → assert_text, PASS com 5). Ela entra no CI no job Rust (stable), com --features wasm-engine.

S1c (registro e CLI). O adaptador wasm (engine #28) existe em crates/rd-engine-registry/src/wasm_execution.rs, atrás da feature wasm-execution (que liga LANG-12, rd-vm/wasm-engine e o parser DEX). Em data/engines.toml o estado é partial_wasm, com a frase “WASM hospedado pelo RustyDroid via bridge documentada”. Com a feature ligada:

  • rd engine check wasm --json responde AVAILABLE_BOUNDED com execution_claimed: false. Isso informa existência do adaptador, não execução.
  • rd engine run wasm <apk> --json faz parse do APK, roda launch (a Activity executa onCreate e a bridge é chamada) e devolve o relatório com a árvore de UI. No APK de demonstração, o TextView result mostra 5.
  • Sem a feature, wasm continua NOT_IMPLEMENTED, como antes.
  • Para APK inválido, o erro vem do parser compartilhado (rd-apk). APK sem assets/*.wasm, sem launcher ou abaixo de minSdk 26 falha com erro tipado.

A execução é limitada ao subconjunto da bridge. Não há loader standalone de .wasm, WASI, threads, JS/JNI bridge nem chamadas de invoke pelo registro. Por isso o M11 não está concluído no ROADMAP: faltam S2 (React Native), S3 (Mono) e S4 (Flutter).

Contrato da bridge (S1b, congelado)

package io.rustydroid.wasm;
public final class WasmBridge {
    public static int call(String asset, String export, int a, int b);
}
  • asset: caminho relativo a assets/ do APK. Caminhos absolutos, vazios, com .., . ou barra invertida são rejeitados como FileNotFoundException, antes de qualquer leitura do ZIP.
  • export: função exportada com tipo (i32, i32) -> i32. Os dois inteiros são os argumentos; o resultado é o único i32 devolvido.
  • Cada chamada instancia o módulo do zero. Nenhum estado persiste entre chamadas. Orçamento de fuel por chamada: limits::MAX_FUEL (10 M).
  • Qualquer falha vira java.lang.IllegalStateException cuja mensagem começa pelo código estável do rd-engine-wasm (PARSE_ERROR, INVALID_FORMAT, NOT_FOUND, FUEL_EXHAUSTED, TRAP, …). Export com assinatura diferente de i32 único também é IllegalStateException (INVALID_ARG).
  • Sem System.loadLibrary. Sem threads, sem memória compartilhada com o host.

Testes (cargo test -p rd-vm --features wasm-engine --test wasm_bridge, 8/8): retorno correto, aritmética i32 com wrap, asset ausente, caminho hostil, export ausente, bytes inválidos, laço infinito esgotando o fuel e o ciclo de vida completo de Activity. Os módulos são montados byte a byte no próprio teste; nenhum .wasm binário é commitado.

Escopo do que executa

Interpretador do subconjunto MVP (ADR 013 §4), em Rust puro sem dependências, com unsafe proibido pelos lints do workspace:

  • tipos i32 e i64; constantes, aritmética, comparações, conversões (i32.wrap_i64, i64.extend_i32_s/u) e os operadores de extensão de sinal (i32.extend8_s etc.), que o LLVM emite por padrão;
  • controle estruturado: block, loop, if/else, br, br_if, br_table, return, unreachable, nop;
  • chamadas diretas call; drop, select;
  • variáveis locais, globais mutáveis e imutáveis (inicializadas por constante);
  • memória linear única: load/store de 8, 16, 32 e 64 bits com extensão, memory.size, memory.grow;
  • seções de dados ativas (offset constante), exportações de função/memória/global, função start; seções customizadas são ignoradas.

Fora do subconjunto, com NOT_IMPLEMENTED (nunca um stub silencioso): ponto flutuante (tipos, constantes, operadores), SIMD, tabelas e call_indirect, imports de módulo, multi-valor, element e segmentos passivos, instruções 0xFC (bulk memory e conversões saturadas), atômicas e múltiplas memórias.

Excesso ou falta gera RdError-like WasmError com código estável: PARSE_ERROR, INVALID_FORMAT, NOT_IMPLEMENTED, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, INSTANTIATION_FAILED, NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARG, TRAP, FUEL_EXHAUSTED, STACK_EXHAUSTED. Nenhum caminho entra em pânico (Lei 1).

Determinismo e isolamento

  • Fuel é debitado uma vez por instrução executada; fuel_used é a contagem real (Lei 4). Mesma entrada, mesmo resultado e mesmo fuel_used (execution_is_deterministic).
  • Sem relógio, sem aleatoriedade, sem rede, sem imports e sem I/O no convidado.
  • O módulo é validado por completo antes da instanciação: tipos de operandos, altura da pilha (incluindo código inalcançável), índices, alinhamento de memória, imutabilidade de globais e nomes de exportação.

Próximos passos (S1b restante)

  2. Suíte rd test sobre o APK de demonstração (feito: golden/engines/wasm/suite.json, feature wasm-engine em rd-agent e rd-cli, passo de CI no job Rust (stable)).

  4. Só depois do merge do S1c começam S2 (React Native), S3 (Mono) e S4 (Flutter).

Garbage collector

RustyDroid’s app heap (rd-vm Heap, default budget 256 MB) uses a non-moving, stop-the-world generational mark/sweep collector. ObjRef slots stay stable and freed slots are recycled. See ADR 006. This is a generational implementation, not incremental or concurrent marking.

Safe points and scheduling

  • Between MCP tool calls and between 512 ms slices of long waits.
  • Inside a single Java invocation: the interpreter checks allocation pressure before instructions. Frames publish roots before nested calls, class initialization and collection; suspended callers remain rooted.
  • Minor collections trace young objects, remembered old heap writes and old host/module side state. Survivors are promoted. A major collection normally runs every eighth cycle, under byte/object-slot pressure, or after a minor leaves the heap above half its byte budget.
  • The byte watermark grows from the last live size: max(live × 2, live + 16 MiB), capped at half the budget while live is small and halfway through remaining headroom when live is larger. Object-slot pressure starts at 75% of the 2^20-slot cap. Inside a live frame it backs off through remaining slot headroom if a pinned/live heap cannot shrink; an unchanged heap is not recollected at every instruction. Tool boundaries can collect again after temporary pins have been released. Hard allocation budgets still report OOM; collection is not a promise that every workload fits.
  • RD_GC=off (or 0) disables automatic collection. Explicit Engine::gc() and MCP runtime_health {"gc": true} still request a full collection.

runtime_health reports minor/major counts, last kind, traced/live/freed objects, weak references/keys cleared, before/after bytes, pause and totals. RD_GC_TRACE=1 logs phase timing. Interpreter-internal cycles appear in these counters; only cycles initiated by the agent’s tool-boundary path produce its I/RdGc app-log message.

Roots and barriers

  • Precise Java roots: instance fields, arrays, register ObjRefs, last-result and pending-exception references.
  • Host temporaries: a host-dispatch scope pins its allocations. Guest re-entry suspends allocation pinning for guest allocations but preserves earlier host temporaries. Nested host calls propagate their pins to an enclosing host callback, never through an intervening Java frame. Object/exception results returned to a host scope are pinned until that scope exits. Top-level Java entries conservatively pin pre-existing objects, since Rust callers may hold otherwise untracked local references. Scope cleanup covers normal and error returns; direct consumers that catch runtime panics should discard the engine (MCP does).
  • Engine side state — conservative: statics, framework state, looper, callbacks, insets/back dispatch, content, native/JNI state and similar tables are rendered with Debug; integer tokens matching valid ObjRefs are roots. The parsed APK is excluded because it has no heap references. Scalar/id collisions can retain extra objects.
  • Heap mutation access (get_mut, including fields and arrays) remembers old objects. Old host/module side states are scanned conservatively on minors because not all their mutation APIs have barriers.
  • The host halves (fw.objects, gfx.objs, Matcher/Spannable/Reader state, etc.) are traced only for reachable key objects. Old side states are also examined during a minor. Dead side-table keys are purged before slot reuse.

External Rust callers of explicit GC must put local references in engine state (e.g. statics) before collecting. An arbitrary Rust local is not a GC handle.

Weak references and WeakHashMap

WeakReference and PhantomReference referents are cleared when otherwise unreachable; registered queues are populated using GC-visible heap fields. SoftReference currently remains strong. ReferenceQueue polling/removal is non-blocking in this headless runtime.

WeakHashMap keys are weak, values strong. Dead object-key entries are pruned by collection; null and scalar keys remain strong. A value that points back to its key keeps that key alive, as on Java WeakHashMap; this is not an ephemeron map. Old dead weak keys/referents can survive until a major cycle.

Limits and validation

Minor marking avoids walking unchanged old Java graphs, but still scans old host state. Marking, slot initialization/sweep and conservative roots still have live-set/arena-size costs; long pauses are possible. This does not establish a Moto E5 pause budget or ARM device performance result.

Regression tests cover old-to-young fields/arrays/host lists, one Java call allocating roughly a GiB under a 4 MiB heap budget, guest-returned host references, weak keys and an above-watermark pinned heap that must not enter a collection storm. Real-APK runs and their limitations are recorded in Comprix end-to-end notes.

versãoRSS (KB)

A imagem de saída é idêntica em todas as versões. O heap contabilizado no fim do quadro é de cerca de 19 MB (109 639 objetos). A maior parte do RSS está fora do heap do app: DEX descompactados (cerca de 20 MB), código decodificado (19 653 corpos, 261 327 instruções) e o malloc. Para diagnosticar, use RD_MEM_REPORT=1 rd app shot ... (imprime os contadores no stderr). Para reduzir a fragmentação do malloc em execuções longas, defina MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 no ambiente: a VM roda numa thread só.

Composição da memória viva em malloc no mesmo quadro (amostrador LD_PRELOAD, fora do repositório; bytes pedidos, não residentes): buffers de DEX ~20 MB, instruções decodificadas ~11 MB, APK inteiro ~12 MB, campos e objetos ~20 MB, Vec<Value> ~6 MB, resolve cache ~5 MB, regex ~3 MB. Total ~123 MB (com folga de capacidade). O GC não aparece como custo relevante no quadro: 2 ciclos, de 33 a 37 ms cada. Detalhes, opções e ordem dos próximos passos: ADR 029.

Fuzzing — RustyDroid

Os parsers de formato não-confiável (ZIP, AXML, ARSC, DEX) são fuzz-hardened: toda leitura é bounds-checked, todo loop tem guarda de avanço e a Lei nº 1 proíbe pânico — falhas são sempre RdError { code, cause, suggestion, module_id }.

Layout

  • crates/rd-apk/fuzz/ — targets zip, axml, arsc, apk_full
  • crates/rd-dex/fuzz/ — target dex (parse + render das primeiras classes)
  • crates/rd-engine-wasm/fuzz/ — target wasm_module (parser + validador + interpretador WASM, M11 S1). Entra na campanha noturna fuzz.yml e no job fuzz-build. scripts/fuzz-campaign.sh ainda não o inclui; essa ampliação fica para uma campanha própria.

Os crates de fuzz ficam FORA do workspace principal (padrão cargo-fuzz) para não contaminar o MSRV nem o lockfile de produção.

Rodando

cargo install cargo-fuzz
cargo +nightly fuzz build -p rd-apk-fuzz          # valida que os targets compilam
cargo +nightly fuzz run zip -- -max_total_time=60 # smoke de 60 s
cargo +nightly fuzz run dex -- -max_total_time=60

Política

  • O DoD do M1 pede fuzz 24 h sem crash antes de declarar o parser “estável”. O script recomendado: rodar os 5 targets por 24 h paralelos em uma noite e arquivar os crashes (se houver) como issues com o input minimizado.
  • O CI roda cargo fuzz build (compilação em nightly, sem execução) para garantir que os targets não apodrecem entre milestones.
  • Qualquer crash de fuzz é bug P0 — Lei nº 1 violada.

Comprix v1.6.0 end-to-end via MCP: status, latency, and blockers

This document covers running Comprix v1.6.0 (br.com.comprix, x86_64) end to end, driven entirely through rd mcp.

  • App: Jetpack Compose, Room, androidx.startup, ML Kit OCR and barcode.
  • Target: minSdk 26, target 35, a single DEX.
  • Harness: mcp_run.py, which sends JSON-RPC over stdio and times each call from request write to parsed response with a monotonic clock.

Status

Round 2 (current): launch no longer hangs. It runs the whole startup plus the first Compose composition and returns in 0.28–0.45 s with a typed error. Before round 2 it exceeded the 60 s per-call deadline. The activity still dies before the first frame, so no app screenshot is available yet.

How far the launch gets now:

  1. Application.onCreate, the androidx.startup initializers, and MainActivity.onCreate run, then setContentView(ComposeView).
  2. The window is attached and the Recomposer and coroutine dispatchers run.
  3. AndroidComposeView is created, with its accessibility, autofill, content-capture, ViewConfiguration, text-input and focus owners.
  4. The Room database is built: ComprixDatabase_Impl is found by reflection, the InvalidationTracker is set up with locks, and the SQLiteOpenHelper is configured.
  5. The first composition of the app UI runs: Scaffold/Surface, java.time date formatting, and Material vector icons parsed from binary XML (painterResource) and tinted with a BlendModeColorFilter.
  6. The side effects run: WindowInsetsController system-bar appearance and the permission-result callback.
  7. The Room open helper is constructed as DEX:
    • process lock: File, FileOutputStream, FileChannel.lock;
    • getWritableDatabase;
    • Room’s onCreate, which creates the schema.
  8. It stops here: Room’s first query uses SQLiteDatabase.rawQueryWithFactory with a CursorFactory (SQLiteCursor/SQLiteQuery bind path). The in-memory m8 SQL subset does not model it yet. This is the next work item: a SQLite engine able to run Room’s generated SQL (PRAGMA, sqlite_master, INSERT OR REPLACE, bound statements).

Round-2 launch progress chain. Each item is a failure found and fixed in general form:

CAS identity → addAll → getHandler → getResources → Canvas → AccessibilityDelegate → AccessibilityManager → SparseLongArray → Autofill → VibratorManager → TreeSet(Comparator) → ViewConfiguration → CursorAnchorInfo$Builder → DEX TreeSet subclass contains → AutofillCallback → JDK interface closure (Set→Collection CCE) → content capture → Object[] ArrayStore → ClassLoader.loadClass → Method.getAnnotations → ActivityManager.isLowRamDevice → Class.getPackage → ReentrantLock → host ListIterator via the Iterator mref → DateTimeFormatter → Resources.getXml → Xml.asAttributeSet → BlendModeColorFilter → Window.getInsetsController → host panic in permission delivery → Activity.onRequestPermissionsResult → SQLiteOpenHelper.setWriteAheadLoggingEnabled → Class.getAnnotation → NPE (diagnosed with the new guest-stack trace: the m8 SQLiteOpenHelper hook swallowed the DEX subclass’s own constructor) → Context.getCacheDir → ReentrantLock→Lock check-cast → FileOutputStream/FileChannel.lock → (open) rawQueryWithFactory.

Round 1 (history).

  • Blocker 1: the Dex::find_class linear scan, now an O(1) index.
  • Blocker 2: the runBlocking spin, resolved in round 2 by the CAS identity and collection fixes.

The raw rows are in comprix/mcp-delays.jsonl, outside this repository.

What to improve, from these measurements

  1. launch has no wall-clock or fuel bound that covers host loops.
    • A single MCP call can block the server forever.
    • Add a wall-clock watchdog to launch, tap and the other tools that run app code (for example RD_MCP_MAX_CALL_MS). On expiry, return a structured VM_TIMEOUT with the guest stack.
  2. MCP errors carry no guest stack. The CLI --trace stack was what located every root cause in this run. Add a trace argument to launch.
  3. runtime_health should report threads, the pending Looper queue, and frames pumped, so a stalled launch can be diagnosed from MCP alone.
  4. Unmodelled host static fields silently read as null or 0, which hides root causes. boxes and android_build mitigate this.
  5. Traces carry no dex pc.
  6. The session tools are fast: install takes about 15 ms and the metadata tools under 1 ms. The cost is concentrated in launch.
  7. Post-mortem inspection. After a launch crash, every interactive tool (screenshot, ui_tree, widgets, accessibility, get_coverage, native_state) returns NOT_RUNNING. Keeping the dead activity’s last frame, view tree and coverage readable would make crash triage possible from MCP alone.
  8. Host-raised exceptions need guest frames.
    • Guest-constructed Throwables now record the guest stack under --trace; the uncaught-exception log prints it.
    • An NPE raised by the interpreter on a null dereference, once caught and rethrown by guest code, still has no frames. That is exactly the current blocker.
  9. Throwable toString without a message printed Class@id. Fixed in the shared host-object fallback: throwables now print Class or Class: message using getLocalizedMessage(), and DEX message/toString overrides still dispatch to app code.
  10. Error messages should name both declarer and receiver. The ListIterator.hasNext failure was really an Iterator.hasNext mref on a host ListIterator. NOT_FOUND should print both the resolved declarer and the receiver class.
  11. launch latency is now dominated by guest work, not the VM: about 0.3–0.45 s for roughly 2,200 distinct DEX methods. install is 22–32 ms with the larger round-2 classpath, and get_api_usage is 66 ms (a full DEX scan, worth caching per install).

Documented deviations

  • Regex: backreferences and lookaround raise PatternSyntaxException (the engine is the Rust regex crate).
  • String.format: a subset of conversions is supported.
  • Reflection:
    • lookup resolves signatures from the dex method_ids, so it covers app-defined methods and referenced platform APIs;
    • getMethods()/getDeclaredMethods() enumeration is not provided;
    • access checks are not enforced.
  • Throwables: no guest stack frames are captured. getStackTrace() returns the last setStackTrace value, else an empty array.
  • Collections.newSetFromMap: returns an independent set rather than a view backed by the map. This is equivalent for the usual idiom, which passes an empty, freshly created map.
  • IdentityHashMap: compares DEX objects by identity but strings and boxes by value.
  • Character classification: approximated with Rust Unicode tables.
  • Collections: subList returns a copy; host ListIterators iterate a snapshot; TreeMap/TreeSet views are snapshots.
  • Resources: ?attr in android:background is resolved through the context’s theme (the manifest application android:theme, then the style item): a color or a drawable reference is applied; an attribute the theme does not define keeps a transparent stand-in. Theme drawables are not rasterized (base Drawable, no pixels). Other ?attr references in XML are still reported as absent, and default styles are ignored. TypedArray getValue reports ints as colors when the attribute name contains “color” or “tint”. getBaseContext returns the receiver.
  • Device: moto-e5, 720×1440 at 280 dpi, locale en-US (RD_LOCALE overrides). ActivityManager models a 2 GB, non-low-RAM device. ViewConfiguration uses AOSP 14 constants.
  • Graphics:
    • not implemented: shaders, mask filters, blend modes, shadows, and applying color filters (they are recorded only);
    • clips are rectangular and Path.op is approximate;
    • Bitmaps are display lists, with no text shaping or bidi;
    • the draw pass paints DEX views only.
  • Platform services: base classes return defaults. Accessibility reports no services; Autofill and content capture are absent (null). Vibrator calls are logged as I/RdVibrator, insets calls as I/RdInsets. Services are per-class singletons; value builders are inert.
  • Reflection: Classes, Methods and Constructors expose no runtime-visible annotations. There is a single app ClassLoader, whose parent is null.
  • Locks: hold counters under cooperative green threads. Holding a lock across a park does not block other threads; Condition.await returns as a spurious wakeup.
  • java.time: the device zone is UTC. The current time is the deterministic virtual wall clock (RD_EPOCH_MS). Pattern letters supported: y M d H h m s S a E and quotes.
  • SQLite: real SQLite in a child process (ADR 005). The in-memory SQL subset remains as a fallback.
  • Filesystem: virtual and in memory per VM; the host disk is never touched. File locks always succeed (single process); FileChannel.map is unsupported.
  • Unsupported: ML Kit OCR and barcode, which need pthread_create and direct ByteBuffers (accepted M9 limitations).

Open items and what to improve next

  1. Garbage collector. RustyDroid never frees memory. A long session (create a list, then all tabs, about 18 s of virtual time) reaches the 256 MB heap ceiling. A collector that runs at safe points between looper messages (roots: statics, host objects, looper queue, frame callbacks and side maps) is the top item.
  2. type_text for Compose text fields. Today it only types into host EditTexts; Compose fields need the InputConnection/IME path.
  3. Sheet animation speed. The Material sheet settles about 3× slower in virtual time than on a device (exponential approach; still under investigation).
  4. Scanner tab. It returns to Listas (camera/ML Kit not modelled).
  5. Screenshots. Cache the frame until something is invalidated, and use cheaper PNG encoding (deflate level, or a delta frame).
  6. Faster cold launch. Use a warm start or snapshot.
  7. Make NOT_FOUND catchable, and cache negative method resolution.

Round 6: seeing the app in real time without screenshots

Question from the round: can the agent see the full APK in real time via MCP without screenshots? Before this round, no — ui_tree showed a single opaque AndroidComposeView node and the only way to see Comprix was a ~3 MB screenshot (0.3–1.6 s). Now yes, see mcp-observe.md:

  • observe (text/json): visible texts with bounds, tap targets, icon centres, frame version and diff — derived from the recorded display list, so it works on Compose;
  • tap_text: tap by label; observe: true on action tools;
  • MCP resources rustydroid://screen, screen.txt, screen.png, logs with resources/subscribe → notifications/resources/updated (the live demo got 13 notifications for 13 real screen changes, none for unchanged frames);
  • rd mcp --live 0.0.0.0:7878: a browser page with the RustyDroid-rendered frame, screen text, tap-target overlay and last tool latency (long-poll);
  • screenshot cached per frame version; runtime panics isolated (INTERNAL_PANIC, session survives).

Focus check (project goals vs. this round)

All additions are Rust-native and stay inside the project’s shape: no VM, no emulator, no new dependencies (the HTTP viewer is std::net, the PNG encoder is the existing one), the model is computed from RustyDroid’s own display list (tiny-skia-style raster path), and everything is exposed through the in-house JSON-RPC MCP (ADR 001) first. Gaps against the stated goals that remain the top priorities: Cranelift JIT not started (the GC landed — see docs/gc.md), regex look-around (above), Compose semantics (contentDescription) for icon labels. Compose type_text is done (fixes 89–92).

Historical round-6 blockers above are superseded by round 8 below.

Garbage collector (round 7)

The app heap used to be an arena: nothing was freed until the app exited, so a long session headed for the 256 MB budget (the main risk for the Moto E5 / 2 GB floor). It now has a mark-sweep collector; design in docs/gc.md.

Same scenarios, same results with GC on and off (identical OK/ERR steps), heap measured by runtime_health:

ScenarioGC off: heap at endGC on: heap at endGC on: peakCyclesFreedPause
s12-gc tab cycling (65 steps)44.8 MB (step 49)14.5 MB (step 49)22.8 MB437.4 MB19–65 ms
s14-long label navigation (131 steps)40.0 MB18.1 MB26.3 MB121.8 MB36 ms
s08-observe full flow (30 steps)not measured16.9 MB27.9 MB355.7 MB52 ms
s11-type Compose input (19 steps)41.2 MB (round 6, r6k)11.3 MB23.7 MB231.8 MB43 ms

The first cycle went from ~600 ms to ~55 ms once the parsed APK was excluded from the root scan (it holds no heap references). Note: Comprix’s repeated tab navigation trips a pre-existing host-iterator bug (Iterator.remove on a snapshot iterator, also present with RD_GC=off), which limits how far the end-to-end stress can push; the unit test long_session_stays_under_budget covers the long-session property directly (8 MB budget, ~25× the budget allocated across 200 tool calls, live set intact; the arena OOMs before call 20).

Weak references (same round). WeakReference/PhantomReference referents are now cleared when nothing else reaches them (SoftReference stays strong). Re-running the flows: identical OK/ERR outcomes; real Compose weak references were cleared (42 in an s08-observe cycle, 13 in s11-type, 30 per cycle in s12-gc) and s12-gc ends at 6.8 MB (was 7.6 MB with strong weak refs).

Pause tuning (same round). RD_GC_TRACE=1 phase timings showed roots <2 ms and marking ~11 ms dominant. A per-cycle side-table bitmap (one Vec<u8> check per object instead of ~5 hash lookups) plus precise tracing of host List/Map/Iter cut marking to 5–9 ms; steady-state forced cycle 14 → 8 ms (live 38.6 k, identical live set), last automatic cycle per flow: s08 46 → 37 ms, s11 42 → 35 ms, s12 20 → 12 ms — same bytes freed to the byte (the collector is deterministic).

Runtime completion and strict regression (round 8, 2026-10-20)

AI-assisted changes address the runtime blockers before integrating the feature branch. Historical round-6/7 numbers above remain historical, not new-device measurements.

  • Iterator.remove now writes through to mutable lists/sets/map-view backing maps, with next/previous cursor adjustment and IllegalStateException rules. COW/immutable iterators remain unsupported for removal. Traversal is still a deterministic snapshot, not a complete fail-fast/live JDK collection model.
  • WeakHashMap keys are weak (strong values, permanent null keys). Minors retain old dead keys until a major collection.
  • Non-moving generations, remembered old writes, live/suspended frame roots and host-temporary scopes permit collection inside one Java invocation. Adaptive object-slot pressure avoids hitting the slot cap before the byte budget and backs off when pinned live objects cannot be reclaimed.
  • Pattern/Matcher/String regex entry points share fancy-regex 0.13 lookaround and backreferences. Backtracking is bounded at 100,000; exhaustion reports REGEX_RUNTIME, never a false match. Source length (64 KiB), delegated regex size/DFA (1 MiB each) and retained cache (128 patterns) are bounded. This is still a documented Java-regex subset, not a complete replacement for Java.
  • Generic saved View delegate/provider traversal supplies Compose virtual node descriptions. Bounded rectilinear Region operations and wrapper-context delegation support the actual provider path, without obfuscated-class hooks.
  • Optional Cranelift 0.104 integer leaf JIT is implemented and off by default. Warmup threshold 32, cache 8,192 entries, native function cap 256; unsupported code falls back to the interpreter. See ADR 007 for safety and architecture.
  • Fuel remains a lifetime counter, but each MCP tool starts a fresh bounded execution window. This avoids exhausting a healthy session’s entire fuel allowance merely through a long sequence of ordinary actions.

Observed real-APK evidence

Comprix 1.6.0 x86_64 release APK, release RustyDroid, desktop Linux sandbox (2 GiB RAM); not a Moto E5 measurement:

  1. Create a list, type 2 kg de arroz, submit via ENTER: Arroz / 2 x kg / 1 item. This goes through the actual app’s parser, Compose input and Room insert, not a mocked fixture.
  2. observe exposes Buscar listas, Minhas lojas, Voltar. Tapping Minhas lojas by name opens the correct screen. Dialog nodes use the same generic path.
  3. With GC disabled, two full Listas → Ajustes → Histórico → Comparar → Listas cycles complete without Iterator.remove failure (17 MCP steps including install/onboarding/provider checks; 32.65 seconds).
  4. Strict populated-list stress treats provider warnings as failures. It uncovered a ContextThemeWrapper inherited-query gap and then a slot-pressure collection storm above 786,432 pinned objects. Both have dedicated regression tests; the long campaign is rerun after these fixes. Final outcome is recorded in the validation report when available; do not infer a completed soak here.

No physical camera/Scanner campaign, ARMv7 native JIT, Moto E5 latency or full Java/Android compatibility claim is made. Human review is required before merge by CONTRIBUTING.md.

Scripts em tools/comprix/:

  • gerar_rotulos.py: gera EAN-13 válidos (dígito verificador pela função dv_ean13, não digitado à mão), tabela nutricional, selo ALTO EM, etiqueta de preço e gabarito.json.
  • validar_fixtures.py: compara os rótulos com o gabarito. EAN via zbarimg; selo, tabela e preço via RapidOCR. Comparação sem acento e por palavra, porque a ordem de leitura do OCR não é garantida. Resultado em validacao_fixtures.json.

Limites desta validação:

  • Não é teste ponta a ponta do Scanner no VM. A leitura de código de barras e de texto pelo ML Kit no VM é stub (host_stub em interp.rs devolve lista vazia, decisão do usuário; gms.rs marca ML Kit como not_implemented). Trocar esse comportamento exige confirmação explícita.
  • O VM não injeta imagem PNG na câmera CameraX. m10/camera.rs cobre só Camera2 e frames sintéticos (RD-CAM…).
  • RapidOCR e zbar não são o ML Kit real. Isso é um desvio de fidelidade e deve ser revisto antes de qualquer alegação de compatibilidade.

Intrínsecos: inclusivo × exclusivo por classe

A telemetria v3 (LaunchTrace::intrinsic_by_class) separa o tempo inclusivo (inclui intrínsecos aninhados) do exclusivo (sem os intrínsecos filhos diretos). O exclusivo ainda inclui o trabalho guest que o intrínseco executa (interpretação, <clinit>, resolução), porque esses contadores são outra categoria.

Ljava/util/concurrent/Executor;238,4301,725

Landroid/database/Cursor;10,210,22.549
Ljava/util/concurrent/atomic/AtomicReferenceFieldUpdater;10,110,13.467

Leitura: quase metade do intrínseco está em Executor (25 chamadas). Ele roda os runnables postados, então o exclusivo dele é o trabalho guest desses runnables (primeira composição e o caminho do Room). Não é custo de despacho de host. Os outros intrínsecos somam poucos ms cada.

Perfil de CPU (perf report --comm rd, plano)

O perfil é plano: nenhum símbolo passa de ~4,5% das amostras. Os primeiros:

Interpretação: o custo está espalhado pelo despacho e pelas buscas por chave String (hash, comparação, malloc/free, is_subtype, method_ref, field_ref) em cada instrução ou chamada, e não em um único ponto. Não há um gargalo isolado para corrigir com um patch pequeno. Com mais 30% de corte necessário (de 640 para 450 ms), é preciso trabalho estrutural no interpretador.

Próximos passos (ordem sugerida)

  1. Eliminar String nas chaves de lookup do caminho quente: resolver method_ref/ field_ref/is_subtype uma vez por site de invoke (cache por índice, não por nome).
  2. Remover alocações por chamada de intrínseco (instance_intrinsic_dispatch_full e a cadeia if class == ... de call_static_intrinsic_rooted).
  3. Inspecionar o que o Executor executa no lançamento (runnables postados): esse exclusivo de 238 ms é o maior bloco isolado.
  4. Medir de novo com perf record --call-graph dwarf para ter a visão inclusiva por função.
  5. Medir com perfil release numa máquina com mais de 2 GB (não é possível nesta sandbox).

Nenhuma destas mudanças foi aplicada. Esta página só registra o perfil e a telemetria.

Os maiores: exec_frame 6,7%, exec_leaf_insn 5,1%, instance_intrinsic_dispatch_full 2,6%, resolve_or_run_host_invoke 2,3%, malloc 2,3%, Classpath::is_subtype 2,0%, call_static_intrinsic_rooted 2,0%, free 1,6%, Classpath::field_ref_shared 1,6%, Heap::gc_host_enter 1,5%.

Correção à leitura anterior: o grupo “malloc/free” de 14,6% estava inflado, porque também contava funções Rust monomorfizadas com alloc no nome. O malloc da libc, sozinho, fica em torno de 4%.

Observações de código (cada uma ~1%, sem alavanca única):

  • Heap::gc_due cai em gc_due_slow por instrução sempre que gc_frames está vazio, porque o caminho rápido exige !gc_frames.is_empty().
  • Heap::gc_host_enter roda por chamada de host e empilha um Vec e um corte em existing_cutoffs.

Conclusão: o custo é difuso. Não há um gargalo que, sozinho, leve as ferramentas MCP de ~1,2 s para perto de 345 ms. Atacar isso exige mudanças estruturais no interpretador ou no despacho de intrínsecos, e não ajustes pontuais.

Causa do clinit no ENTER (uma vez por processo, na primeira vez que o item é processado):

  • Lm2/A; (catálogo de unidades): 240 ms inclusivo.
  • Lm2/n; (catálogo de hortifruti, aninhado em m2/A): 227 ms inclusivo.
  • Ambos são <clinit> com ~1.400 e ~3.900 linhas de smali, montados com listOf, Pair, mapOf e Lm2/n;->c/e/a (cerca de 300 entradas). O custo é execução de bytecode no interpretador (~2 M de instruções a ~250 ns), não uma operação cara isolada.

Decisões e limites:

  • Mover esses <clinit> para o launch reduziria o passo ENTER, mas é uma troca de onde o custo cai na medição, e não uma redução de trabalho. Não foi feito; depende de decisão sobre a métrica.
  • Acelerar listOf/Pair/mapOf com intrínsecos do stdlib do Kotlin: no <clinit> do m2/n, listOf e Ls0/c;->L são ~317 dos ~650 sites de invoke estáticos (contagem estática, não execução). Exige cuidado com a semântica das listas; o ganho real não foi medido.
  • O ganho grande exige reduzir o custo por instrução do interpretador, o que segue difuso (ver a seção de categorias acima).

RD Sentinel — anti-regression bot operator guide

RD Sentinel is RustyDroid’s dedicated Dependabot-like guardian. Normal CI remains the fast, bounded pull-request gate. Sentinel handles the evidence CI cannot afford or cannot express at one revision: differential comparisons, long campaigns, historic budgets, environment drift, evidence shrinkage, and deduplicated GitHub triage.

The architecture and rationale are recorded in ADR 010.

What changed in v1.1

  • Risk is now explainable: every report lists the factors and points behind its 0–100 score instead of asking reviewers to trust one opaque number.
  • Targeted package selection follows reverse workspace dependencies, so a parser change also exercises the workspace consumers above it.
  • Public-API checks compare crate-level item inventories, reducing false alarms for same-crate moves while still blocking removals/signature changes.
  • Workflow changes are linted for mutable action refs, shell template injection, persisted checkout credentials, missing permissions, and dangerous-trigger candidate checkouts.
  • Dependency evidence now includes duplicate/mass-update analysis, reachable workspace blast radius, cargo-deny, optional cargo-machete, an OSV batch query when network is allowed, and a deterministic CycloneDX SBOM artifact.
  • Reports are also emitted as SARIF 2.1.0. The fingerprinted JSON remains the authoritative completeness/verdict record.
  • A mutants profile runs cargo mutants --in-diff on committed Rust changes, asking whether the tests actually catch injected faults.
  • Cold26 A/B comparisons include sample counts and median absolute deviation; relative deltas must clear a noise-aware floor, while absolute <26 ms budgets remain strict.

What changed in v1.2

  • Evidence no-shrink checks are named, not only counted: Rust test identities are compared by (scope, test name) with duplicate-name counts, and fuzz targets are compared by crate-qualified target name. Deleting a meaningful test/target and adding an unrelated one no longer looks neutral.
  • OSV querybatch pagination is completed per unfinished query (bounded by campaigns.osv_max_pages), preserving the package-to-advisory mapping and reporting page/pending/truncated metrics instead of silently stopping at the first page.
  • The trusted publisher now also creates the rd-sentinel/gate Check Run with up to GitHub’s per-request annotation batches for findings that carry a file and line, and uploads the SARIF rendering to code scanning when a PR report has findings. These are presentation layers over the same verified JSON report; API rejection there does not replace or weaken the trusted comment, labels, or commit status.
  • The CLI can consume a raw merge_group event file directly for merge-queue reproduction, using the group base/head SHAs without inventing a PR number from the queue ref.

What runs where

Bot partTriggerPermissionsPurpose
Dependabotweekly/monthly scheduleGitHub-managedproposes Cargo, fuzz-crate, and Actions updates
RD SentinelPR, merge queue, manual dispatchcontents/pull-requests readtrusted-base policy audit plus risk-selected campaigns
RD Sentinel Deepnightly, weekly, manual dispatchcontents/pull-requests readlong and broad campaigns on main
RD Sentinel Publishworkflow_run completionissues/PR/statuses/checks/security-events writeverifies the artifact against GitHub, comments, labels, issues, verified status, annotated gate Check Run, code-scanning SARIF upload
RD Sentinel Commandissue commentactions/issues/PR write, contents readmaintainer-only campaign dispatch

Candidate-executing analysis jobs never receive a publishing token.

The strict rules

Sentinel fails closed:

  • P0/P1 findings block. Examples: forged/stale report identity, protected Sentinel paths without approval, secrets, unsafe outside approved crates, fuzz crashes, nondeterministic frames, cold-start median at/above 26 ms, incompatible dependency sources.
  • Required skipped evidence is not a pass. In GitHub campaigns it blocks; locally it produces incomplete unless --strict-skips is also set.
  • Evidence cannot shrink silently. Test attributes, named Rust tests, JVM golden vectors, named fuzz targets, and MCP tool count are compared to both the base revision and .github/rd-sentinel/baseline.json.
  • Performance budgets cannot be relaxed to hide a regression. The 1,500 ms real-execution startup budget and the <26 ms process-cold snapshot presentation budget are separate contracts and must stay separate.
  • A/B regressions block even when absolute budgets still pass. The bot compares base and candidate inspect, rd perf, snapshot cold start, frame hashes, binary size, and paired efficiency workloads.
  • Exceptions expire. Every exception in .github/rd-sentinel/policy.json needs an owner, precise scope, reason, and expiry date. Expired or incomplete exceptions block.
  • The trusted policy and baseline validate themselves. Weakened blocking severities, malformed numeric limits, invalid deep-dependency regexes, missing protection for Sentinel’s own policy/baseline/workflow/code, duplicate or over-broad exceptions, and malformed corpus contracts are findings rather than silent configuration drift.
  • Workflow privilege cannot drift quietly. Sentinel workflow actions are pinned to full commit SHAs, and changed workflows are checked for unpinned actions, user-controlled expressions in run: scripts, credential persistence, and missing explicit permissions.

Campaigns

PR risk audit (auto)

The diff is classified into parsers, VM core, native/security, agent/protocol, render/UI, CLI contract, dependencies/build, CI security, performance, fuzz, tests, docs, and Sentinel itself. That classification selects:

  • tests for directly changed packages plus their downstream workspace dependents;
  • relevant Cargo feature combinations derived from the checked-out manifests (with the v1.0 matrix retained as an unreadable-manifest fallback);
  • repeated tests with named flaky-test extraction and real-APK byte-stability probes;
  • actual bounded fuzz execution for parser changes;
  • rd perf and scripts/cold26.py for performance-sensitive changes;
  • full A/B and real-APK campaigns for high-risk diffs or sentinel:deep.

Draft PRs receive the static report without executing expensive campaigns. The verdict stays incomplete until a ready/synchronized revision executes the plan.

Use --profile mutants or the sentinel:mutants label to add changed-code mutation testing to a PR. Deep runs include it as a required component. A test-only diff or an uncommitted worktree cannot provide a trustworthy mutation result and is reported as such.

Nightly deep

Runs Monday-Saturday on main:

  • cargo test --workspace --all-features;
  • broad feature matrix for VM/agent/CLI/registry/JNI/NDK;
  • repeated determinism/flaky hunts;
  • resolved dependency license/source/MSRV audit, cargo audit, cargo-deny, changed-dependency blast-radius analysis, an OSV query when network is enabled, and a CycloneDX SBOM artifact;
  • beta Rust and Rust 1.76 trials;
  • release binary size, rd perf, process-cold snapshot, and real-APK probes;
  • all five fuzz targets for the configured bounded duration;
  • isolated semver-compatible dependency-update trial in the weekly core job.

Weekly campaign

Runs Sunday on main and adds:

  • a longer hosted fuzz campaign;
  • base-versus-head A/B performance/efficiency/frame comparisons;
  • application-neutral persistent-session MCP endurance on pinned launchable APKs (install/launch, observe, UI tree, screenshots, virtual time, app info, and runtime health), plus scripts/comprix-regression.py only when a real Comprix APK is explicitly supplied;
  • scripts/mcp-session-soak.py over the signed native-language APK matrix;
  • three repetitions of the JVM golden comparison;
  • changed-code mutation testing for the weekly base/head range;
  • an isolated cargo update trial.

GitHub-hosted jobs have a six-hour ceiling. Therefore the weekly hosted fuzz run is not called a 24-hour campaign. For an actual 24-hour run, dispatch or run scripts/fuzz-campaign.sh 86400 on a self-hosted/read-only runner or a maintainer machine and retain the artifacts.

Maintainer commands

Only GitHub author associations OWNER, MEMBER, and COLLABORATOR may use:

/rd-sentinel rerun
/rd-sentinel deep
/rd-sentinel perf
/rd-sentinel fuzz 900
/rd-sentinel deps
/rd-sentinel determinism
/rd-sentinel mutants 45
/rd-sentinel baseline propose
/rd-sentinel status
/rd-sentinel help

Commands only dispatch evidence campaigns. They cannot approve policy, change a baseline, push, dismiss reviews, or merge. status links the newest report comment authored by github-actions[bot]; a marker planted by another account is ignored.

Approval is deliberately label-based and human-applied:

LabelMeaning
sentinel:policy-approvedmaintainer reviewed bot code/policy/workflow changes
sentinel:baseline-approvedmaintainer reviewed before/after evidence for a baseline change
sentinel:deepforce the deep PR campaign
sentinel:mutantsforce changed-code mutation testing

The publisher applies only result/risk labels such as sentinel:pass, sentinel:blocked, sentinel:P0, sentinel:perf-risk, sentinel:security-risk, sentinel:dependency-risk, sentinel:test-gap, sentinel:risk-high, and sentinel:risk-critical. It removes stale Sentinel result/risk labels when publishing a newer report.

A live PR that moved on while the audit ran is not an integrity failure (issue #233). If the artifact’s head is no longer the PR head, the publisher treats it as superseded and does not write anything to the PR: the live head’s own run owns the comment, labels and gate. If only the base branch advanced and the report claims pass, the verdict becomes stale. In that case the gate is pending, no result label is set (a previous sentinel:pass is removed), and the comment asks for /rd-sentinel rerun. A stale report is never a pass. Real findings in a non-pass report are published unchanged, and any other verification mismatch (changed files, artifact head vs workflow_run, unapproved protected paths) is still a P0.

Dependabot PR vetting

Dependabot groups Cargo minor/patch updates, separates majors, checks the two fuzz workspaces monthly, and updates GitHub Actions weekly. Version updates use explicit release-age cooldowns (14 days for Cargo majors, 7 for minors and GitHub Actions, and 3 for Cargo patches); security updates are not delayed by those cooldowns. Sentinel then:

  1. parses the exact Cargo.lock delta;
  2. blocks non-dependency files in a Dependabot PR;
  3. classifies major/minor/patch/prerelease and 0.x minor-as-major movement;
  4. checks licenses, crates.io-only sources, and dependency Rust versions against MSRV 1.76;
  5. reports duplicate-version growth and mass updates, then runs feature, determinism, and A/B evidence for those wider movements;
  6. computes direct/reachable workspace consumers and flags changed build, proc-macro, build-script, native-link, and widely consumed crates;
  7. runs cargo-deny, cargo audit, and (with network) OSV, and writes a CycloneDX SBOM;
  8. requires the major-approval label for major movement; and
  9. never auto-merges.

If an update only fails on Rust beta or future dependencies, do not ignore it: that is tomorrow’s red main. Either pin deliberately in the product PR or prepare the migration before the stable release arrives.

Local use

Static plan (no campaigns executed, therefore not a passing audit):

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py plan \
  --base origin/main --head HEAD

Executable risk-selected audit:

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py audit \
  --base origin/main --head HEAD --execute --strict-skips

Audit uncommitted work against the current commit:

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py audit \
  --base HEAD --head WORKTREE --execute

Bounded fuzz only:

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py audit \
  --base origin/main --head HEAD --profile fuzz \
  --component static --component fuzz --Fuzz_SECONDS 600 --execute

Changed-code mutation testing only (requires a clean committed range and cargo-mutants):

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py audit \
  --base origin/main --head HEAD --profile mutants \
  --component static --component mutation \
  --mutation-minutes 45 --execute --strict-skips

Validate/render an artifact:

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py validate \
  --report target/rd-sentinel/rd-sentinel-report.json
python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py render \
  --report target/rd-sentinel/rd-sentinel-report.json
python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py sarif \
  --report target/rd-sentinel/rd-sentinel-report.json \
  --out target/rd-sentinel/rd-sentinel-report.sarif

Generate baseline evidence without modifying the baseline:

python3 tools/rd-sentinel/rd_sentinel.py baseline-proposal \
  --base origin/main --head HEAD --execute

Exit codes are 0=pass, 1=blocked, 2=bot/config error, and 3=incomplete. An incomplete local run still writes JSON, Markdown, and SARIF reports, but it must not be quoted as a pass.

Corpus policy

The pinned launchable corpus currently contains Primftpd 71 (org.primftpd_71.apk) with its SHA-256 in the baseline. The public F-Droid client download is a moving latest build, so Sentinel treats it as a structured-behavior/determinism probe, not a pinned launch baseline.

For the 100 MB+ process-cold gate, set:

RD_SENTINEL_HEAVY_APK=/path/to/launchable-heavy.apk

A missing heavy corpus is reported as missing evidence. Sentinel does not manufacture or imply a heavyweight pass. Never commit the heavy APK.

The Comprix journey is application-specific, so it is never run against Primftpd or another unrelated APK. To include it in a real-APK campaign, set RD_SENTINEL_COMPRIX_APK=/path/to/comprix.apk; Sentinel then runs the existing Portuguese UI script only against that explicit corpus.

Responding to findings

Fuzz crash

  1. Preserve the uploaded artifact before rerunning.
  2. Reproduce and minimize with the command printed by fuzz-campaign.sh.
  3. Add the minimized case as a unit/integration/fuzz seed regression.
  4. Fix the parser without adding a production panic path.

Flaky or nondeterministic output

Treat process/thread globals, time, random seeds, filesystem ordering, and shared stdout routing as prime suspects. A retry that turns green is evidence of the bug, not evidence that it disappeared. Sentinel names tests that both passed and failed across repetitions; start with those tests rather than the last failing command alone.

Surviving mutant

A surviving mutant means the changed behavior can be altered without any test noticing. Add an assertion for the public behavior, not a test that merely mirrors a private implementation detail. If the mutant is truly equivalent, record why in a dated, narrowly scoped exception. A mutation timeout is not a kill and needs its slow/pathological path investigated.

Performance

Separate three numbers:

  • rd perf: real guest execution against the emulated Moto E5 budget;
  • cold26: new live process presenting a previously captured deterministic snapshot frame;
  • first interaction/materialization: reported separately from first frame.

Do not use snapshot timing to claim the first-ever guest launch is <26 ms, and never raise a budget in the same PR that introduces the slowdown.

Baseline change

  1. Run the same campaign on base and candidate.
  2. Open a PR that changes only the baseline/ADR evidence, or clearly isolate that commit.
  3. Link both reports and explain why the new behavior is correct.
  4. Apply sentinel:baseline-approved after maintainer review.

Required repository settings

Files alone cannot make a check required. After this bot lands, configure branch protection or a repository ruleset for main to require at least:

  • the existing CI jobs;
  • RD Sentinel / audit;
  • optionally the publisher’s rd-sentinel/gate commit status;
  • conversation resolution and no force-pushes.

Also restrict who can apply the Sentinel approval labels. The bot honors those labels as maintainer decisions, so label permission is security-sensitive.

.github/CODEOWNERS routes Sentinel, supply-chain, native-boundary, and cold-start-evidence changes to the repository owner. Do not enable “Require review from Code Owners” while that owner is also the sole PR author: GitHub does not let authors approve their own PRs, so the rule would deadlock merges. Enable it when a second maintainer or team exists.

Known limits

  • Hosted performance runners are noisy. Sentinel therefore pairs absolute budgets with A/B ratios and absolute deltas, but a human still reviews borderline evidence.
  • Static diff heuristics are intentionally conservative and can produce P2 review findings. P0/P1 rules are reserved for contracts, security, determinism, evidence loss, and measured regressions.
  • cargo audit, cargo-deny, cargo-machete, and cargo-mutants are installed by workflows that need them. On a local runner without one, the report marks that evidence skipped/incomplete rather than inventing it.
  • OSV is queried only when network is explicitly allowed. Sentinel follows per-query querybatch pagination up to campaigns.osv_max_pages, reports the number of pages and any still-pending queries, and still keeps cargo audit/RustSec as separate evidence.
  • Check Run annotations and code-scanning SARIF are GitHub presentation layers. A fork head, disabled code-scanning surface, or missing Checks API acceptance is recorded as a publisher-side error for that layer; it never turns a blocked fingerprinted report into a pass.
  • The public-API inventory is a conservative source-level comparison, not a rustdoc/semver proof. It intentionally ignores same-crate file moves; associated items, re-exports, trait implementations, and generic bounds can still require human review or future cargo-semver-checks adoption.
  • The named-test inventory is also source-level. Macro-generated tests without a visible following fn still rely on the #[test] attribute count and on compiled test evidence from campaigns.
  • Diff-scoped mutation testing gives fast changed-code evidence. It does not prove the unchanged workspace has a high global mutation score.
  • Sentinel workflows use reviewed full-SHA action pins. GitHub’s newer workflow dependency lockfile remains a separate adoption decision; Sentinel does not fabricate an actions.lock file.
  • The bot does not prove Android compatibility beyond the pinned real-APK, native, contract, and golden evidence it actually executes.

Reproduce

cargo build --release -p rd-cli --features jit

The harness does not download APKs. It writes summary.json, full JSON-RPC transcripts, stderr, and a typed-item screenshot under target/comprix-campaigns/<name>/. Each operation has a 120-second watchdog; tool errors, provider/frame warnings and wrong screen titles fail the run.

Issues found and corrected during strict real-APK validation

  1. Missing Region/AccessibilityAction APIs prevented the standard Compose provider from initializing. Implemented bounded platform models and tests.
  2. Dialog accessibility queries inherited Context.getPackageName through ContextThemeWrapper. Delegation now honors real base DEX overrides and inherited Activity/Application host methods; cyclic wrapper chains fail.
  3. A high pinned live object count caused a collection at every instruction above the fixed 75% slot watermark. Adaptive headroom/backoff and a dedicated

    786k-object regression prevent this collection storm.

  4. A negative integer immediate needed zero-extended i32 bits in Cranelift IR. Differential literal/narrowing tests now pass.
  5. Host temporaries returned from a guest callback need protection before a second callback can collect. The return-root regression now passes.

Explicit limits / merge gates

  • The collector is generational and stop-the-world, not incremental/concurrent. Some measured desktop major pauses exceed 100 ms, especially under concurrent compilation. No Moto E5 latency or memory budget certification is claimed.
  • JIT is off by default and restricted to integer leaves. ARMv7 is not a native JIT target; ARM64 execution still needs device validation.
  • Provider traversal, Java regex, Region and collection views remain bounded subsets; see ADRs 006/007 and Comprix notes. Camera/Scanner is not covered.
  • GitHub CI for the final pushed commit, completed endurance result and human review must be checked separately. A repository-protection API request was denied by token permissions; protection requirements are unknown, not assumed absent. Do not bypass them or fabricate review approval.

GC and runtime efficiency verification — 2026-10-20

Scope and quality constraints

This change integrates the Appendix G registry and source-built C/C++/Rust native-language work with measured GC/runtime improvements. The repository’s main at verification was 7ce8ba3a9849cdef09fee988a381dac591f5b8c4; registry work also overlaps the still-open PR #158. This PR does not close or merge that PR. The other 25 adapters remain unimplemented; this is not full NDK or physical-Android conformance.

The optimization-only baseline is imported delivered source 6fdfaaf47b60f93d2aba5f499a2b7fa1a198008c. Measurements used the Rust source subsequently delivered in f119cbd8143374f5de89053074502fbf5ba03d72. PR-publication follow-ups extend CI and shell-gate coverage, document evidence, and scope CLI report serialization to its feature configuration so default and native builds both pass strict Clippy. The CLI JSON behavior is preserved; these follow-ups add no new VM/GC optimization.

No quality-damaging shortcut is accepted. Heap storage/API/limits, fuel, safepoints, parser/ELF validation, barriers, pinning and the optimization baseline’s rendering/native/JIT algorithms are unchanged. The cumulative PR also includes the earlier native UI/inheritance fixes documented in the native language delivery; do not confuse the optimization-only diff with the full main-to-PR diff.

Retained changes

  • Scan the exact conservative Debug root byte stream without temporary Strings. Preserve cross-write numeric tokens, saturation, order and byte counts.
  • Remove a redundant minor-GC uniqueness set over unique arena indices.
  • Borrow weak-class descriptors and only query WeakHashMap ancestry for Maps.
  • Borrow method names instead of allocating per comparison.
  • Use a checked sequential instruction cursor with checked binary fallback for branches, handlers and invalid PCs. Fuel and root publication remain intact.
  • Borrow static built-in hierarchy/interface slices with preserved keys/edges.
  • Avoid temporary String/UTF-16 allocations in length/hash/charAt paths; preserve surrogate units, invalid indices, messages and validation order.
  • Resolve each subtype-walk class once, without a persistent mutable-DEX cache.

A compact vacant-slot representation passed tests but regressed sweep throughput by about 40%; it was reverted. There is no optimization-only heap.rs change. A slower scanner and a stale shared-Cargo-cache baseline attempt were also rejected, not selectively reported as wins.

Assertion-bearing paired measurements

25 seeded randomized-order pairs for each of nine workloads: 450 runs, matching checksums and iteration counts. Original used a separate empty target directory; final runtime dependencies were cleaned/rebuilt. No competing build/benchmark was active. Linux GNU time measured child peak RSS.

Confidence bounds are a descriptive 10,000-resample percentile bootstrap of the median paired ratio, not of the ratio of medians. They are not multiplicity adjusted and cannot model all host noise. The fetch workload intentionally has long sequential instruction runs; these are not whole-app multipliers.

The initial JIT row has different ratio-of-medians and paired estimates because of noisy/mixed timing populations. Both the raw row and slower point estimate remain included. An additional 100 unpinned and 100 fixed-vCPU pairs gave median paired ratios 1.030 [1.022, 1.036] and 1.027 [1.025, 1.030]. No JIT algorithm was changed and no JIT-specific speedup is a headline claim.

Raw pairs, generated summary, hierarchy proof and supplemental JIT summary are in the performance evidence directory.

Real-app and quality evidence

These are one sequential replay per binary/mode, not a statistical app-wide speedup guarantee. APK SHA-256 is 39a4930c89f1a3670eca03cc6eb37114a0467c52687bf028dd633a6b60c6d6f4. The final typed item/quantity survived cycling and final collection. Six app milestone PNG pairs and 36 native UI/widget pairs were byte-identical.

Original GC-on JIT-off runs already vary in non-time health metrics. The final 21-sample trace exactly matched the earlier original trace, while a second original run differed. JIT-on matched its contemporaneous original trace. Do not claim every paired intermediate fuel/GC counter was identical. No fuel metering or safepoint was removed. GC root-phase timing now includes tokenization; phase attribution before/after is not directly comparable.

A one-cycle GC-off typed control passed. Both versions separately reached the same typed 256 MiB OOM at step 28 of the requested three-cycle GC-off boundary control, after two cycles. Heap/fuel/clock samples matched before OOM. The budget was not raised and GC was not secretly enabled.

Recorded gates: 570 all-feature / 558 default tests; strict Clippy/fmt; minimal checks; Rust 1.76 minimal-native check and actual build; 150 JVM golden vectors; 18 native APK cases with all 41 tools positively covered in each, 1,683 calls; nine malformed-ELF rejections; 15 legacy APK/ABI checks. Normally ignored real source/OSS APK tests were explicitly exercised. Fresh PR verification and GitHub checks are separately reported on the PR, not inferred from these earlier logs.

The JVM oracle is the repository CI’s Temurin 21, compiling target 17. JVM 17 has two legacy float-string spellings; all 150 original/final raw VM records were identical there. No comparator or runtime formatting was weakened.

Reproduce

Use separate target directories for original/final source restores: restored old mtimes can make a shared Cargo target reuse an unrelated optimized library. Copy the identical final efficiency_bench.rs example into the baseline tree. Build each with release/all-features/locked and one build job on a 2 GiB host.

python scripts/efficiency-benchmark.py --baseline /absolute/original-bench --candidate /absolute/final-bench --out /tmp/rd-perf/final-original-nine-paired.json --repetitions 25 --workloads roots host sweep minor resolve interp strings subtype jit
python scripts/summarize-efficiency-benchmarks.py --evidence /tmp/rd-perf

The checked instruction cursor has differential random-walk/bad-PC coverage; UTF-16 has Unicode/surrogate/index differentials; the GC graph oracle uses 64 seeds with 192 objects each and independent buffered roots/manual marking. These are regression evidence, not a proof over every APK or of a universal performance optimum. Headless emulation is not physical-device validation.

The mandatory source-language CI gate rebuilds SHA-pinned signed APKs, executes all three ABIs with JIT off/on, requires positive coverage of every MCP tool, and rejects nine corrupted ELF inputs. It uploads provenance/evidence but not the generated private debug signing key. See native languages.
