ADR 001 — Servidor MCP do rd-agent sem rmcp (JSON-RPC 2.0 próprio, zero deps)

  • Status: aceito e implementado; revisto pelo ADR 023 (múltiplas sessões por processo)
  • Data: data de aceite não registrada no ADR original

Contexto

A spec (RustyDroid.md, “DECISÕES TÉCNICAS JÁ TOMADAS”) fixa rmcp p/ MCP; tokio só no rd-agent. O M5 exige um servidor MCP v1 com ~20 tools.

Fato novo verificado em 2026-10: todas as versões publicadas do rmcp (até a 3.5.1) declaram MSRV 1.88; o workspace é MSRV 1.76 (decisão também vinculante da spec, guardada pelo job rust-msrv do CI). Adotar rmcp hoje quebraria o MSRV — violação de contrato, não escolha.

Opções

  1. rmcp + subir MSRV para 1.88 — viola decisão vinculante + exclui contribuidores/CI de toolchains mais velhas; o piso é produto.
  2. rmcp 0.x antigo — versões sem rust_version declarado, APIs instáveis pré-1.0; mesmo assim puxa tokio full + tower para o que, no v1 stdio, é um envelope JSON-RPC.
  3. JSON-RPC 2.0 sobre stdio implementado no rd-agent (serde_json já é dependência) — o MCP em transporte stdio É newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list, tools/call, ping); envelope pequeno e testável; mantém o padrão do projeto (ZIP/AXML/ARSC/PNG/zlib próprios, zero deps externas).

Escolha

Opção 3. O protocolo na fio é idêntico ao MCP (clientes oficiais — Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, MCP Inspector — conectam sem saber a diferença); o envelope de sessão v1 é ~200 linhas testadas; zero deps novas; MSRV 1.76 intacto.

Consequências

  • Quando o MSRV do workspace subir para ≥1.88 (M7+ plausível), re-avaliar rmcp; o contrato das tools (nomes/args/resultados) não muda — só o envelope.
  • Features de MCP que o v1 não usa (resources, prompts, sampling, streaming SSE/HTTP) ficam fora do envelope até demandarem — mesmas respostas de erro tipado do resto do projeto.
  • tokio segue FORA do workspace (a fila do agente é single-thread determinística — decisão M3); o servidor stdio é um loop de leitura bloqueante, uma sessão por processo.

ADR 002 — Entradas ZIP duplicadas: aceitar, sinalizar e contar por nome único

Issue: #84 · Status: aceito · Data: 2026-10-11

Contexto

O leitor de ZIP (crates/rd-apk/src/zip.rs) monta a lista de entradas a partir do central directory sem verificar nomes repetidos. Um APK com duas entradas classes.dex era descrito como se fossem dois arquivos distintos: o resumo do rd inspect contava 4 dex num APK com 3 DEX reais e uma duplicata — sem nenhum aviso. As buscas por nome (Zip::find) devolviam a primeira ocorrência, silenciosamente.

Princípios envolvidos: “Sem falha silenciosa” (RustyDroid.md) e “never a silent failure” (README.md). O inspect é a base das decisões de compatibilidade do projeto, então descrever o APK com contagem errada tem impacto alto.

Limitação conhecida: não foi verificado neste ambiente como o instalador Android resolve nomes duplicados (não há emulador nem dispositivo). Esta ADR trata do comportamento do rd e não afirma qual decisão o sistema toma.

Opções

  1. Rejeitar o APK (INVALID_FORMAT no parse, com o nome duplicado). Simples e “seguro”, mas impede justamente a análise do caso ambíguo: nomes duplicados são um artifício conhecido de empacotadores/obfuscadores para que leitores ingênuos vejam um arquivo diferente do que o runtime vê. Uma ferramenta de análise que se recusa a abrir esse APK entrega menos informação exatamente onde ela importa.
  2. Aceitar e sinalizar (escolhida): o ZIP continua parseando, o nome repetido é exposto em Zip::duplicates()/Apk.zip_duplicates, o inventário passa a contar por nome único e o inspect imprime uma linha de aviso (e o JSON ganha a chave zip_duplicates).
  3. Aceitar em silêncio, só corrigir a contagem: remove a distorção, mas mantém a escolha invisível — viola “sem falha silenciosa”.

Escolha

Opção 2. Aceitar e sinalizar.

  • Zip::parse detecta repetições (ordem de aparição no central directory) e guarda em Zip::duplicates();
  • Apk::parse monta o inventário (dex, lib/*.so, assets/*, res/*) pulando nomes já vistos — a contagem de DEX no inspect deixa de inflar;
  • rd inspect imprime zip duplicates ⚠ N nome(s) repetido(s) no ZIP: <nomes> — rd usa a 1ª ocorrência e, no --json, a chave zip_duplicates (omitida quando vazia);
  • Leitura por nome continua na 1ª ocorrência (Zip::find/Zip::read). É a decisão conservadora: mantém o comportamento atual de todos os consumidores (rd dex, rd vm, assinatura) em vez de adotar “última ocorrência” sem evidência do que o Android faz.

Consequências

  • APKs sem duplicatas — a imensa maioria — não mudam: nenhuma linha nova na saída humana, nenhuma chave nova no JSON.
  • Um APK ambíguo passa a ser descrito como ambíguo em vez de descrito como se tivesse mais arquivos do que tem.
  • Se futuramente ficar estabelecido (com evidência) qual ocorrência o Android usa, a política de leitura pode mudar num único ponto (Zip::find) — a sinalização e a contagem por nome único permanecem.

ADR 003 — Registro de engines separado de execução

  • Status: aceito para registro/detecção; novos runtimes continuam pendentes
  • Data: 2026-10-14
  • Escopo: Apêndice G, 28 entradas e LANG-01…LANG-12

Contexto

O Apêndice G mistura linguagens de origem, formatos compartilhados (DEX/ELF) e frameworks. Um classes.dex não prova Java em vez de Kotlin/Scala; uma .so não prova C em vez de Rust/Zig. Na origem desta decisão (2026-10-14), JNI/NDK eram stubs. Atualização de integração (2026-10-20): a rota native já executa um subconjunto ELF/JNI em x86_64/ARM64/ARMv7 (ADR 004), e há render Compose Android parcial. Isso não implementa adaptadores LANG, Compose Multiplatform nem Android/NDK completo; M11 segue pendente. O dono do repositório escolheu completar registro e detecção, não anunciar execução dos 28 ecossistemas.

Decisão

  1. data/engines.toml é o catálogo versionado das 28 entradas, módulos, dependências, estratégias, assinaturas e estado REAL de runtime.
  2. A crate segura rd-engine-registry valida o catálogo e analisa nomes de entradas ZIP e declarações do manifest. Não extrai arquivos, carrega .so, executa código, consulta rede nem descomprime assets. O payload dos artefatos NÃO é validado; nomes/declarações podem ser falsificados.
  3. A detecção separa signature (marcadores de framework), candidate (formato compatível/ambíguo) e not_detected (sem evidência, não exclusão). Um APK híbrido pode ter várias assinaturas; nenhuma delas prova execução.
  4. O catálogo está sempre disponível, mesmo no build mínimo. Features Cargo lang-01…lang-12 expressam seleção e transitividade para os contratos; não baixam nem implementam engines. Seleção de runtimes no manifest e checkboxes do spec permanece inalterada nesta entrega.
  5. O contrato público é EngineAdapter::parse(artifact) -> Process, event(process, event) e syscall(process, call). Os adaptadores do registro são indisponíveis e SEMPRE respondem NOT_IMPLEMENTED(LANG-xx), com ou sem feature. Não retornam um processo fictício. A VM DEX existente continua acessível pelas rotas rd vm/rd app, com cobertura parcial documentada.
  6. rd engine list|detect|check, rd inspect --json e a tool MCP app_info expõem o mesmo catálogo/relatório. Não há nova tool MCP nem alteração no protocolo/contagem. --data explícito nunca cai silenciosamente no embedded.
  7. Relatórios/spec gerados e testes travam IDs, 28 casos golden de assinaturas, features/dependências e isolamento (mínimo, individual e all-features). Evidências e diagnósticos têm amostras limitadas; excesso de entradas é erro tipado, não alocação ilimitada.

Consequências

  • Todo o Apêndice G é consultável e auditável agora, sem promessas falsas.
  • TWA/PWA podem não ter payload local; ausência de assinatura não as descarta. DEX/ELF comuns continuam candidatos, nunca atribuição da linguagem original.
  • Registro/detecção não requer novas dependências nativas ou unsafe; os budgets de execução E5 não foram certificados por esta mudança.
  • Uma engine futura precisa de sua própria crate rd-engine-<nome>, ADR, feature, adaptador real e golden flow com APK OSS antes de mudar o estado de runtime. Testes de detecção NÃO satisfazem esse critério de execução.

Alternativas rejeitadas

  • Marcar todas as linguagens como executáveis ao reconhecer um nome de arquivo.
  • Criar dezenas de crates vazias ou embutir Flutter/Mono/CPython/wasmtime só para registrar metadados: mais peso, sem ganho funcional e fora do escopo aprovado.
  • Inferir linguagem de origem a partir de uma .so genérica ou bibliotecas de dependências Kotlin presentes no APK.

ADR 003 — M8 compat host: interceptação seletiva + estado real consultável

  • Status: aceito e implementado (M8 concluído, 2026-10)
  • Data: data de aceite não registrada no ADR original

Contexto

M8 (spec PARTE 4): “Compat real — app OSS médio navega funcional; v0.9”. Os subsistemas pedidos (RecyclerView, Fragments, Dialogs, OkHttp, SQLite/Room, Services/broadcasts/deep links, WorkManager) são, na maioria, bibliotecas que viajam no DEX do APK (androidx/okhttp), não classes android.*. A VM só despachava Landroid/ para o host; o resto executava DEX.

Opções

  1. Implementar cada biblioteca inteira em Rust — duplicar AndroidX/OkHttp.
  2. Deixar todo o DEX rodar e só preencher android.*/java.* — RecyclerView real exige Canvas/MeasureSpec/etc. demais para o headless atual.
  3. Interceptação seletiva: o dispatch (interp) consulta crate::m8 antes da resolução DEX, mas só para métodos explicitamente listados; None cai para o DEX real da biblioteca. O host implementa esses métodos com estado real consultável (Engine::m8_*), chamando de volta o DEX do app onde o Android chamaria (Adapter.getItemCount/onCreate/onBind, SQLiteOpenHelper.onCreate, BroadcastReceiver.onReceive, DialogInterface.OnClickListener, OkHttp Callback).

Escolha

Opção 3. É a única que entrega comportamento observável de ponta a ponta sem reescrever bibliotecas: a RecyclerView pergunta a contagem ao adapter do app e anexa os itemViews reais; o SQLite guarda linhas e responde cursores; o OkHttp devolve a resposta registrada sem fingir rede.

Desvios documentados (nunca silenciosos)

  • Single-thread determinístico: Call.enqueue, broadcasts e commits de fragment são síncronos; WorkManager registra o pedido mas não roda Worker.doWork() em background (harness conclui via m8_complete_work).
  • SQLite: desde a ADR 005 o backend padrão é SQLite real (processo filho Python sqlite3, jsqlite.rs). O subconjunto SQL em memória (CREATE/DROP TABLE, SELECT … FROM, insert/update/delete com col=literal|?; sem arquivo, sem JOIN/ORDER) continua como fallback (RD_SQLITE=subset, Engine::use_sqlite_subset, ou quando não há Python).
  • OkHttp é shim offline: nenhuma rede; resposta vem de Engine::m8_set_http_response (default 200 vazio) e toda URL é registrada.
  • RecyclerView popula no máximo 20 itens (viewport headless).
  • SharedPreferences vivem na VM (sem arquivo); fragments sem animações.

Consequências

  • Apps médios navegam: lista (RecyclerView) → detalhe (fragment/dialog) → dados (SQLite/Room) → rede (OkHttp shim) → background (Service/WorkManager) é exercitável por testes (crates/rd-vm/tests/m8.rs) e pelo agente via compat_gaps (ids m8-*).
  • Métodos não listados continuam NOT_FOUND tipados (Lei 1) — a superfície cresce por sondagem real, como nos 45 gaps do primftpd.

ADR 004 — M9 isolated native execution and advanced components

Status

Accepted for implementation; acceptance remains subject to the M9 evidence gate.

Context

APK native libraries are untrusted ELF, commonly ARM rather than the host ISA. Calling arbitrary guest code through host dlopen violates isolation, exposes the host libc ABI instead of Android bionic, and makes deterministic fuel impossible. The workspace forbids unsafe Rust outside the two native crates. Full CPU emulation is not a reasonable home-grown instruction subset. Unicorn supports x86-64, AArch64 and ARM/Thumb, but its GPL licensing must not silently change the licensing of the MIT/Apache Rust binary.

Decision

Use a separately installed, optional Python/Unicorn worker process, controlled by bounded JSON-lines messages over private stdin/stdout. No host function pointers, no executable guest mappings in the Rust process and no new unsafe Rust. The worker receives only explicitly mapped guest memory; guest syscalls and unimplemented imports fail closed. It is a CPU emulator, not a guest Android OS. Native support is opt-in (native Cargo feature); minimal builds retain typed errors. The worker requires Python 3 and unicorn==2.1.4; it is not linked into the Rust binary. Unicorn retains its own license. Process separation is an engineering boundary, not a claim of legal advice or a hardened OS sandbox: Python/Unicorn vulnerabilities still require an external container/seccomp policy for hostile APKs.

ELF metadata and relocation processing live in safe Rust (rd-ndk), JNI identity, modified UTF-8, descriptors and local-reference rules in rd-jni, and Java heap / callback translation in rd-vm. Unsupported relocation/import/JNI operations must return structured errors rather than fabricated success. Instruction and memory budgets bound guest execution. The worker watchdog also bounds wall-clock time.

Advanced components use per-Engine deterministic state and the existing virtual clock. Notifications are keyed by tag/id with channels, actions and listeners; widgets retain RemoteViews operations; IME edits the focused view with UTF-16 selection semantics; accessibility operates on the existing view tree. Agent tools use the same state, not a second mock implementation. Missing platform services remain explicit compatibility gaps.

Consequences

Native execution requires an extra optional runtime dependency and IPC has overhead. No claim of complete Android bionic, C++ runtime, JNI or five real APK compatibility is made without reproducible tests. Generated native fixtures prove ABI behavior; they do not substitute for the five-real-APK exit gate. Golden evidence records APK hashes, source/license and the native functions actually executed.

ADR 005 — Real SQLite through an isolated child process

Status: accepted (Comprix e2e, round 3)

Context

Room apps (Comprix, and most modern apps) issue real SQL: JOINs, ORDER BY, aggregates, sqlite_master and pragma queries, triggers, and rawQueryWithFactory with bind args. The M8 in-memory SQL subset (ADR 003) cannot run them. Comprix died on its first Room query.

The options considered were:

  1. extending the hand-written subset;
  2. linking rusqlite with bundled SQLite (C code, unsafe FFI, a C toolchain in every build, and MSRV churn);
  3. a child process that owns a real SQLite.

Decision

Option 3. crates/rd-vm/src/jsqlite.rs runs python3 -u with a small sqlite3 server script and speaks JSON lines with it (open, exec, query, transaction, close). SQLiteDatabase, SQLiteStatement, Cursor and SQLiteOpenHelper are served on top of it.

  • Database files live in a per-session temporary directory that mirrors /data/user/0/<pkg>/databases/.
  • The interpreter is configurable with RD_SQLITE_PYTHON.
  • RD_SQLITE=subset, Engine::use_sqlite_subset() or a missing Python falls back to the M8 subset, which stays deterministic and dependency-free.

Consequences

  • No unsafe and no C build in rd-vm; the workspace policy and MSRV 1.76 hold. A crash in SQLite cannot take the VM down. This mirrors the ADR 004 isolation choice for native code.
  • Each call costs an IPC round trip, which is microseconds and well below DEX interpretation cost.
  • Python 3 is a runtime dependency only for apps that use SQLite. CI images already have it.
  • Tests that inspect the subset model (Engine::m8_database) must opt into the subset with use_sqlite_subset().

ADR 006 — non-moving generations and live-frame GC roots

Status: implemented; differential/regression and real-APK validation in progress.

Context

Tool-boundary full GC cannot reclaim allocations in a long Java invocation. Precise suspended-frame roots and protection of Rust host temporaries are required before collection can run with an interpreter frame live. Moto E5 also benefits from tracing young objects rather than the entire old heap.

Decision

Keep stable ObjRef slots and stop-the-world collection, with a young generation and periodic full collections. Heap mutation access (get_mut, including field and array writes) records old objects in a remembered set. Minor collections retain old objects, trace remembered old heap objects, and conservatively scan all old host/module side states, whose mutation APIs are not write-barriered. Surviving young objects are promoted after each minor. A full collection runs periodically and under pressure; explicit gc() remains a full collection. Slot pressure starts at 75% of the slot cap and backs off through remaining headroom when a live/pinned heap cannot shrink. Unchanged heaps are not recollected on every instruction; a tool boundary can retry after pins release. No concurrent marker, moving heap or guest Android runtime is introduced.

Interpreter frames publish only ObjRef roots before calls/class initialization and when collecting. The current frame additionally publishes last-result and pending-exception references. Suspended callers retain their published roots. Host-dispatch scopes pin allocations made in Rust host code; guest re-entry suspends allocation pinning while preserving earlier host temporaries. Guest object/exception return values are pinned into the surrounding host scope. Nested host calls transfer temporary pins to the enclosing host callback, but not through an intervening Java frame. Pins are released when that callback returns. Top-level Java entries conservatively pin pre-existing objects because their Rust caller may hold references not yet stored in engine state. Scope cleanup occurs on normal and error returns. This deliberately favors over-retention over dangling references. Public explicit GC outside a Java entry still requires callers to root local references in engine state.

Consequences

Minor pauses avoid traversing unchanged old Java graphs. Old host side state is still scanned, so pause improvements depend on the workload; do not claim Moto E5 measurements from desktop results. Unreachable old objects and weak old keys can persist until the next major collection. WeakHashMap values remain strong, not ephemerons (values that reference keys retain them, matching Java).

Cranelift/JIT GC integration is not implied: compiled execution must publish roots or use interpreter fallback before allocating/calling out.

ADR 007 — opt-in Cranelift integer & control-flow JIT (MethodJit)

Status: accepted and upgraded from straight-line leaf prototype to full verified multi-block integer/long/switch/array JIT; opt-in (RD_JIT=on or Engine::enable_jit).

Context and Evolution

The initial ADR 007 prototype (LeafJit) compiled only straight-line static 32-bit int leaves (<= 128 instructions, no branches, no loops, no 64-bit long, no switch, no primitive arrays, opt_level="none", and per-call heap allocations in the dispatch path). Real Android compute hotspots — checksums, hashes, PRNGs, parsers, state machines, sorting/searching, and pixel/byte-buffer loops — all rely on control flow, 64-bit long arithmetic, switch tables, or primitive arrays, causing the prototype to reject them (unsupported).

MethodJit graduates ADR 007 into a complete, RustyDroid-adapted integer and control-flow JIT while preserving every safety, determinism, MSRV, and GC invariant of the original boundary (LeafJit remains available for backward compatibility).

Architecture and Safety Invariants

  1. Dual-stage verification (rd-vm + rd-jni):
    • crates/rd-vm/src/jit.rs (#![forbid(unsafe_code)]) discovers basic-block leaders across CodeItem.instructions, prunes unreachable dead blocks and trailing switch payloads via BFS from PC 0, propagates Dalvik register types across CFG joins, and lowers 82 Dalvik opcodes into JitProgram.
    • crates/rd-jni/src/jit.rs independently re-verifies structural bounds (<= 256 registers, <= 32 parameters, <= 256 reachable blocks, <= 4,096 total IR ops, <= 4,096 cached functions) and runs a monotone fixed-point dataflow verifier over the lattice {Zero, Int32, LongLo, LongHi, Ref, ArrI32, ArrI64, Uninit} before Cranelift (opt_level="speed") emits machine code.
  2. Full Dalvik control flow and exact per-block fuel accounting:
    • Supports goto/goto/16/goto/32, if-eq..if-le (both int and reference identity), if-eqz..if-lez (including null checks), packed-switch (Cranelift JumpTableData), and sparse-switch (Cranelift Switch search tree / jump tables, including negative keys).
    • Every basic block header adds its exact Dalvik instruction count to an SSA fuel accumulator and branches to a dedicated FuelExhausted exit if the window budget (Engine::fuel_remaining()) would be exceeded. Hostile infinite loops terminate deterministically with VM_FUEL, and normal returns advance Engine::fuel_used by the exact instruction count of the interpreter.
  3. 64-bit long lane, void/instance methods, and safe literal division:
    • Supports const-wide/*, move-wide/*, add/sub/mul/and/or/xor-long (3-reg and /2addr), shl/shr/ushr-long (32-bit int shift count masked with & 63 per Dalvik specification), neg/not-long, int-to-long, long-to-int, cmp-long, return-void, and return-wide.
    • Supports non-zero literal div-int/lit16, rem-int/lit16, div-int/lit8, and rem-int/lit8, guarding lit == ±1 in IR so i32::MIN / -1 wraps to i32::MIN and i32::MIN % -1 == 0 without hardware #DE traps. Variable register division/remainder (div-int, rem-int, div-long, rem-long) and lit == 0 continue to fall back to the interpreter to materialize ArithmeticException.
  4. Opaque-handle transactional primitive arrays (zero raw guest pointers):
    • Primitive array parameters ([Z, [B, [S, [C, [I, [J) never pass heap addresses into guest registers. Instead, guest registers hold 1-based opaque handles (0 = null, 1..=K = verified host slice table slot), deduplicated by ObjRef so aliased arguments (f(a, a)) share the same transactional buffer and preserve a == b reference identity.
    • Every array-length, aget*, and aput* checks 1 <= handle <= K and (idx as u32) < len in hardware before indexing. On normal return, mutated buffers commit back to Engine.heap. On NullPointerException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, or mid-array VM_FUEL, uncommitted scratch buffers are dropped and Engine::call replays in the interpreter to produce exact partial writes and exception traces.
  5. Loop-aware tiering and zero-allocation hot dispatch:
    • Methods containing backward branch edges (loops) compile immediately on their first invocation (threshold = 1), accelerating cold single-call compute kernels; straight-line leaves retain threshold = 32.
    • Engine::invoke_static maintains an inline cache (StaticIcSlot) and marshals scalar arguments onto a stack [u64; 32] buffer, eliminating per-call String/Vec allocations and DEX table scans.

Feature and Floor

Cargo feature jit remains OFF by default. Enable an engine explicitly via Engine::enable_jit() or RD_JIT=on. cranelift-* =0.104.3 preserves the workspace Rust 1.76.0 MSRV. Native execution targets 64-bit Cranelift hosts (validated on x86_64); the portable interpreter remains the Moto E5 baseline.

Paired Benchmark Results (--release --features jit, 5-run medians)

All five workloads assert bit-identical return checksums and instruction-exact Engine::fuel_used() parity between interpreter and MethodJit (compilation time is included inside the MethodJit wall-clock numbers for loop kernels):

WorkloadDalvik FuelInterpreter (RD_JIT=off)Prototype LeafJit (main)MethodJit (RD_JIT=on)Speedup vs main
efficiency_bench jit (100k sum(II)I calls)200,128103.78 ms91.92 ms7.10 ms12.95x (14.62x vs interp)
IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 (byte[4096] x 40, nested loops)11,796,760212.45 ms212.45 ms (unsupported)2.64 ms80.46x
SplitMix64 long stream (409,600 64-bit rounds)3,277,30059.17 ms59.17 ms (unsupported)1.28 ms46.37x
Bounded Collatz CFG (4,000 calls, if-* + div/rem)3,016,75043.98 ms43.98 ms (unsupported)2.45 ms17.94x
packed-switch VM state machine (409,600 steps)2,867,50040.28 ms40.28 ms (unsupported)1.19 ms33.71x

Remaining Interpreter-Only Scope

Floating-point (float/double) lanes, heap object allocation, field access (iget/iput/sget/sput), nested method calls (invoke-* inside a JITted body), and methods with try/catch handlers remain in the interpreter.

ADR 008 — 15 GB APK support with ≤ 1,500 ms cold start on the Moto E5 floor

  • Status: Accepted (design); Stage 1 (partial) + Stage 2 (prototype) implemented in the landing PR; Stages 1b/3/4/5 specified for follow-up PRs.
  • Date: 2026-10-21 · Scope: rd-apk, rd-dex, rd-vm, rd-agent, rd-render, rd-cli, rd-ndk, rd-engine-registry, workspace Cargo.toml.
  • Identity (non-negotiable): Rust-native runtime, no VM/KVM/guest kernel, no boot; Moto E5 floor (data/devices.toml: Snapdragon 425, cpu_single_thread_factor=0.25, cpu_quota_cores=1.0, ram_process_cap_mb=512, ram_app_heap_mb=256, 720×1440@280dpi, minSdk 26); MCP plane (47 tools, ADR 001) contract unchanged; determinism (execution, GC, PNG); MSRV 1.76; unsafe_code="forbid" except rd-ndk/rd-jni (deny + local allow + ADR).
  • Laws: Law 1 structured RdError{code,cause,suggestion,module_id}; Law 2 raw offsets preserved (rd inspect/rd dex); Law 4 deterministic output.

1. Problem & measured root causes

rd perf (crates/rd-cli/src/perf.rs:183 timed_launch_frame) times launch+screenshot on a fresh AgentSession after install; emulated = host/0.25 = host×4.

GateEmulatedHost
Measured 2026-10-21, 11 MB Primftpd, before this ADRp50 2,190 / max 2,356 msp50 548 / max 589 ms
Hard targetmax < 1,500 msmax < 375 ms
Design pointp50 ≤ 1,040 msp50 ≤ 260 ms

Root causes (verified in tree):

  1. Whole-file read: Apk::MAX_INPUT_BYTES=512MiB (rd-apk/src/lib.rs:63), fs::read in Apk::open + tool_install (rd-agent/src/mcp.rs:1213), Zip{data:Vec<u8>} (rd-apk/src/zip.rs:41). 15 GB impossible; RSS grows with APK size before any code runs.
  2. Deep clone per cold launch: app.apk.clone() (mcp.rs:1390, fixed by this ADR).
  3. Eager DEX: dexes_of_apk (mcp.rs:480) inflates+CRC32s every DEX; Dex::parse (rd-dex/src/dex.rs:252) decodes all MUTF-8 strings (strings.rs) and id tables; first find_class builds OnceLock<HashMap<String,usize>> (dex.rs:500). Cold path touches <2–5% of classes/strings.
  4. Eager ARSC: Arsc::parse/StringPool::parse (rd-apk/src/arsc.rs, pool.rs) decode all pools + BTreeMap<u32,Vec<ResEntry>> over all configs.
  5. String-heavy VM: Classpath::method_ref/field_ref/resolve_method (rd-vm/src/classpath.rs), Engine::statics: HashMap<(String,String),Value>, HeapObj::Instance{class:String, fields:Vec<(String,Value)>} (rd-vm/src/heap.rs); CodeItem decodes to Vec<(usize,Insn)> (rd-dex/src/code.rs, rd-vm/src/interp.rs).
  6. Conservative GC roots via Debug formatting of ~40 host tables (rd-vm/src/gc.rs:184 write_gc_roots).
  7. Engine detection caps at 100k entries (rd-engine-registry/src/detect.rs DETECTION_LIMIT); native .so payloads risk JSON serialization to native_worker.py (rd-ndk).
  8. Profiling OOM: [profile.release] lto="thin", codegen-units=1 over rd-vm (60+ modules) OOMs a symbols build in 2 GB (observed SIGKILL).

2. Decision summary

PillarDecision
ZIP/APK I/OSafe positional I/O only (FileExt::read_at/pread64) + bounded LRU page cache (64 KiB pages, 16 MiB cap). No mmap in the default path (see §3). MAX_APK_BYTES = 16 GiB (ZIP64).
DEXLazyDex: O(1) header/map validation, on-demand fixed-stride table reads, raw-MUTF-8 compare, binary search over sorted string_ids/class_defs; no eager Vec<String>, no HashMap<String,usize>.
ResourcesLazyStringPool + LazyArsc with config-filtered O(1) 0xPPTTEEEE resolution.
InstallSession-scoped InstalledApkIndex (manifest, LAUNCHER, multi-DEX class directory by u64 descriptor hash, STORED-DEX direct slices / DEFLATE checkpoints).
LaunchArc<Apk> end-to-end (done), pre-mounted DEX from the install index.
VMSymbolId interning, ClassLayout slot tables, flat resolution cache, lazy/arena CodeItem, TraceRoots GC trait, startup GC watermark.
Assets/NDKStreaming AssetManager (openFd slices), file-path+offset PT_LOAD descriptors to the native worker, streaming engine detection (2M+ entries, O(1)).
Render/PNGPre-allocated framebuffer reuse; identical-row Up-filter fast path (done, byte-identical).
Telemetryrd perf phase fields (done: install_ms, launch_ms, screenshot_ms, rss_after_mb per run + ADR sub-phases in VM behind a zero-cost-when-off hook, Stage 1b).
Profiling[profile.profiling] (done): lto=false, codegen-units=16, debug=1, strip="none"; documented CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1, optional -Wl,--no-keep-memory.

3. The mmap/RSS trap (why pread64 wins)

peak_rss_mb() reads VmHWM from /proc/self/status. File-backed mmap pages faulted in count toward VmRSS/VmHWM; scanning >512 MB of a mapped 15 GB APK fails the 512 MB gate, and MADV_DONTNEED eviction is racy, platform-specific, and requires unsafe (forbidden). pread64 copies only requested ranges into a user-space cache whose size we choose: with 64 KiB × 256 pages the APK layer can pin at most 16 MiB, mathematically, forever — independent of APK size. Any future windowed-mmap fast path needs its own ADR, an RSS-eviction hard cap, and may never be the default.

5. Concrete Rust designs (exact types; MSRV 1.76, no new unsafe)

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
// rd-apk/src/zip.rs — replaces Zip { data: Vec<u8>, .. }
pub enum ZipSource {
    InMemory(std::sync::Arc<[u8]>),                    // unit-test fixtures only
    Paged { file: std::sync::Arc<std::fs::File>, len: u64,
            cache: std::sync::Mutex<LruPageCache> },   // production path
}
impl ZipSource {
    pub fn read_at(&self, off: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> RdResult<()>;
    pub fn slice(&self, off: u64, len: usize) -> RdResult<std::borrow::Cow<'_, [u8]>>;
    pub fn len(&self) -> u64;
}
pub struct LruPageCache { /* 64 KiB pages, VecDeque<(u64 page, Box<[u8]>)>, cap 256 pages = 16 MiB */ }
impl LruPageCache { pub fn read_exact_at(&mut self, f: &std::fs::File, off: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> RdResult<()>; pub fn pinned_bytes(&self) -> usize; }

#[repr(C)]
pub struct CdRecord { pub name_off: u32, pub name_len: u16, pub method: u16,
    pub crc32: u32, pub comp_size: u64, pub uncomp_size: u64, pub local_off: u64 } // 32 B
pub struct CompactCdIndex { pub records: Vec<CdRecord>, pub names: Vec<u8>, // flat arena
    pub by_hash: Vec<(u64, u32)>,                       // sorted (name-hash, record idx): binary search, no HashMap<String,_>
    pub boot: BootEntries }                             // manifest/arsc/dex/.so record indices found during the CD pass
impl CompactCdIndex { pub fn find(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&CdRecord>; pub fn stream_build(src: &ZipSource) -> RdResult<Self>; }

// rd-apk/src/signing.rs — windowed v2/v3 detection
pub fn detect_paged(src: &ZipSource, cd_offset: u64) -> RdResult<SigningInfo>; // 32 B footer + block header via read_at only

// rd-dex/src/lazy.rs
pub struct LazyDex { src: DexBacking, hdr: Header, map: Vec<MapItem>, // small, validated O(1)
    str_cache: Vec<Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>>, type_cache: Vec<Option<u32>> }
pub enum DexBacking { StoredSlice { zip: ZipSource, off: u64, len: u64 }, Owned(std::sync::Arc<[u8]>) }
impl LazyDex {
    pub fn mount(backing: DexBacking) -> RdResult<Self>;              // < 0.2 ms: header+map bounds only
    pub fn string(&self, idx: u32) -> RdResult<std::borrow::Cow<'_, str>>; // decode-on-demand + memo
    pub fn string_eq(&self, idx: u32, s: &str) -> RdResult<bool>;     // raw MUTF-8 compare, zero alloc
    pub fn find_class(&self, desc: &str) -> Option<ClassDef>;         // binary search: string_ids sorted (UTF-16), type_ids sorted by string idx, class_defs by type idx
    pub fn method_id(&self, idx: u32) -> RdResult<MethodId>;          // base + idx*8, checked
}
// rd-apk/src/arsc.rs + pool.rs
pub struct LazyStringPool { src: ZipSource, off: u64, count: u32, utf8: bool, memo: Vec<Option<String>> }
pub struct LazyArsc { pools: Vec<LazyStringPool>, types: Vec<TypeChunkIndex> } // chunk headers only at mount
impl LazyArsc { pub fn resolve(&self, id: u32, cfg: &DeviceProfile) -> RdResult<Option<ResValue>>; } // O(1): winning type offset table

// rd-agent/src/mcp.rs — built in tool_install, consumed by tool_launch
pub struct InstalledApkIndex { pub manifest: Manifest, pub launcher: ComponentName,
    pub application_desc: Option<String>,
    pub class_dir: Vec<(u64 /*desc hash*/, u16 /*dex*/, u32 /*class_def*/)>, // sorted, binary search
    pub dex_mounts: Vec<DexMount> } // StoredSlice | DeflateCheckpoint{..}
pub enum DexMount { Stored { entry: u32 }, Inflated(std::sync::Arc<[u8]>) }

// rd-vm: interning, layouts, GC (Stage 4)
pub struct SymbolTable { map: std::collections::HashMap<Box<str>, u32>, rev: Vec<Box<str>> }
pub struct ClassLayout { pub desc: SymbolId, pub fields: Vec<(SymbolId, FieldKind)> } // slot = index
pub struct ResolvedCache { /* Vec-keyed (class,name,proto) SymbolIds -> ResolvedMethod, generation-stamped */ }
pub trait TraceRoots { fn trace_roots(&self, out: &mut RootSet); } // replaces Debug-stream scanning in gc.rs
}

Invariants: every fixed-stride read is bounds-checked with base + idx*stride overflow checks returning RdError (Law 1); raw offsets retained on all records (Law 2); caches are insertion-ordered/LRU-deterministic, never hash-iteration-ordered (Law 4); crc32 still verified on any entry actually extracted; inflate budget (512 MB declared) unchanged.

6. Pillar-by-pillar specification

  1. ZIP64 VFS (Stage 2): tail read ≤ 64 KiB+22 B locates EOCD → ZIP64 locator/EOCD; CD streamed entry-by-entry through the page cache (prototype rd-apk/src/paged.rs: PagedZip, landed: 25 rd-apk tests incl. 600 MiB sparse container opened/looked-up with ≤ 256 KiB pinned). signing::detect_paged reads only the footer/header window before cd_offset. Arc<Apk>/set_resources_arc eliminates the launch clone (landed; RSS 99.7→83.3 MB measured). Full swap of Apk.zip to ZipSource + CompactCdIndex remains Stage 2b (API-compatible read/find/names surface preserved).
  2. LazyDex (Stage 1b): mount = header (112 B) + map validation; find_class = 2 binary searches + 1 def read; strings decode on first use into str_cache; multi-DEX directory from the install index means launch mounts only DEX files containing touched classes. Expected: dex_mount ~180 ms → ≤25 ms on Primftpd-class APKs.
  3. LazyArsc (Stage 3): pool header (28 B) + offsets validated O(1); type chunks indexed by header scan; config ranked against moto-e5 (720×1440, 280 dpi, API 36-capped); resolution indexes the winning offset table directly. rd inspect keeps full-fidelity offsets.
  4. Install index (Stage 1b/2b): install pays CD+class-def scans once (off the perf timer today, reported via install_ms); launch reuses mounts. .rdcache on-disk persistence is explicitly out of scope (session-scoped only) until a cache-integrity ADR exists.
  5. VM (Stage 4): SymbolId interning in Classpath, slot-indexed instance fields, flat method cache; CodeItem decoded into a reusable slab, raw-code-unit interpreter fallback for one-shot <clinit> methods; TraceRoots for the ~40 host tables in gc.rs; minor GC suppressed below a startup slot watermark unless pressure demands.
  6. Assets/NDK/registry (Stage 3): AssetManager streaming over ZipSource::read_at (openFd = offset/len slice, O(1) RAM); native worker receives {path, file_offset, pt_load[]} instead of payload bytes; detect.rs becomes a streaming CD visitor (bounded counters, 4-sample cap, 2M+ entries).
  7. Raster/PNG (Stage 1, landed): identical consecutive rows emit the all-zero Up row in O(stride) memcmp — byte-identical to the adaptive heuristic’s choice (score 0), proven by md5-stable screenshots across runs and the rd-render suite; buffer reuse in AgentSession follows in Stage 3.

7. Profiling without OOM (landed)

  • [profile.profiling] in workspace Cargo.toml: inherits="release", lto=false, codegen-units=16, debug=1, strip="none". Verified: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo check --profile profiling -p rd-apk finishes in 24.5 s in this 2 GB sandbox (the equivalent release+symbols build was SIGKILLed). Recommended full build: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo build --profile profiling -p rd-cli (optionally RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-Wl,--no-keep-memory").
  • rd perf --json per-run phases (landed): install_ms, launch_ms, screenshot_ms, rss_after_mb. Stage 1b adds VM sub-phases (dex_mount_ms, app_clinit_oncreate_ms, activity_lifecycle_ms, inflate_layout_ms, render_raster_ms, png_encode_ms) via a counters struct read after the frame — zero cost when not queried (single atomic-free struct fill per phase boundary).

What actually closed the gap (profile-driven, in order of impact):

  1. jannotations::method_annotations scanned all method_ids (50k+) per call to find one declared method; it now searches only the declaring class’s ClassData (the single largest win, ≈50 ms).
  2. Parallel DEX mount in dexes_of_apk (scoped threads, declaration order preserved, deterministic Vec<Dex>) + slicing-by-8 CRC32 (bit-identical). Note this partially revises §10: parallel mount of the few DEX files proved deterministic and within the 1-core quota; eager parse remains the Stage 1b target.
  3. Classpath caches: method_ref / field_ref / resolve_method memoization (DEX sets are immutable per Engine) + a find_class index memo re-borrowed from the live DEX per call.
  4. Android-style measure() short-circuit (same specs + no bubbled requestLayout ⇒ skip onMeasure) and a zero-allocation fast path in do_invoke when no wide register is present.

Two documented dead ends, kept here so they are not retried: (a) binary -search find_class (type_ids + sorted-class_idx index) was slower end-to-end (cross-DEX misses and per-call string compares) and was reverted to the lazy HashMap build; (b) memoizing is_subtype results is unsound — a differential test deliberately mutates DEX metadata in place and asserts subtype answers stay live.

Still outstanding (unchanged from §8): full LazyDex mount, the ZipSource/CompactCdIndex swap (Stage 2), LazyArsc (Stage 3), Stage 4 VM internals, and the 15 GB sparse launch fixture — the ≤1,500 ms bar above is met on the M7 gate APK, not yet on a 15 GB APK.

9.2 Stage 1b LazyDex, PagedStringCache & RawClassIndex addendum (2026-10-25)

Stage 1b’s rd-dex lazy decoding and zero-allocation class directory are now implemented in crates/rd-dex:

  1. LazyDex + DexBacking (crates/rd-dex/src/lazy.rs): O(1) header + map_list + fixed-stride section bounds validation (LazyDex::mount measured at 4–8 µs on 9 MB DEX files with 65k strings and 9.5k classes), positional DexBacking::Slice window support, raw MUTF-8 zero-alloc string_eq, and on-demand fixed-stride readers (method_id, field_id, proto_id, class_def, find_class, class_data, code).
  2. 2-level PagedStringCache (crates/rd-dex/src/strings.rs) wired into Dex::parse_unverified / Dex::parse_lazy: validates string_ids offsets at mount without decoding untouched strings (256 slots/page via OnceLock<Box<str>>, ~4 KiB top-level directory for a 65k-string DEX vs ~1.5 MiB eager Vec<String> + heap strings). Dex::parse remains eager for rd inspect / api_usage / fuzz parity.
  3. Cache-colocated RawClassIndex (16 B open-addressing ClassSlot { hash, str_off, class_def_idx } + 8-byte SWAR MUTF-8 hashing): eliminates all per-class String allocations on first find_class while preserving first-definition-wins semantics and keeping warm_p50 faster than HashMap<String, usize> (442–450 ms vs 450–547 ms emulated on org.primftpd_71.apk).
  4. Measured before/after (org.primftpd_71.apk, 5 DEXs / 20.04 MB raw DEX / 135,777 strings / 17,809 classes, profiling profile, moto-e5):
    • dex_parse:classes.dex (9.36 MB): 10.0–12.5 ms → 0.47–0.97 ms (>10× faster)
    • dex_parse:classes4.dex (9.05 MB): 7.4–10.5 ms → 0.93–1.14 ms (~9× faster)
    • dex_parse:classes5.dex (1.62 MB): 1.0–11.3 ms → 0.06–0.37 ms
    • Process peak RSS (VmHWM): 108–111 MB → 88.7–89.3 MB (−21.7 MB / −19.6%)
    • Disassembly (rd dex disasm): 100% byte-for-byte identical to eager Dex::parse.

10. Alternatives considered

  • mmap (even windowed): rejected as default (§3, RSS trap + unsafe ban); may return via dedicated ADR with hard eviction accounting.
  • On-disk .rdcache: deferred — cache integrity/versioning is its own trust problem; session-scoped index captures the perf win first.
  • Raising MAX_INPUT_BYTES only: rejected — removes the error, not the O(n) RSS/time blow-up.
  • Forking DEX parsing to threads: rejected for now — determinism (Law 4) and the 1-core quota make lazy mounting strictly better than parallel eager mounting.

11. Addendum (2026-10-25): Stage 2 integration and the Zip::raw_bytes contract change

Context. Stage 2 moved from a prototype to integration (PR #216). Zip now holds a private ZipSource with two variants:

  • Whole(Vec<u8>): the legacy in-memory container;
  • Paged(Arc<PagedZip>): payloads stay on disk behind the 16 MiB LRU page cache.

Apk::open routes any file above Apk::MAX_INPUT_BYTES to Zip::open_paged instead of rejecting it, so the issue #38 INVALID_FORMAT path is gone.

Contract change. Zip::raw_bytes changes from pub fn raw_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] to pub fn raw_bytes(&self) -> Option<&[u8]>. A paged container has no contiguous in-memory image to borrow. The alternatives were:

  • materialize the file, which defeats Stage 2 and breaks the RSS cap;
  • panic in paged mode, which is banned on production paths;
  • return an empty slice, which silently lies to callers.

None makes paged mode explicit at the type level.

New public surface, all mode-agnostic:

  • Zip::is_paged();
  • Zip::file_len();
  • Zip::read_range(off, len), which copies from memory in whole mode and reads through the page cache in paged mode;
  • PagedZip::read_range.

Callers. The only in-tree caller of raw_bytes is rd_apk::detect_signing:

  • whole mode keeps the original full-buffer signing::detect;
  • paged mode reads only the 24-byte APK Signing Block trailer and then the block window before cd_offset.

The paged window is capped at 64 MiB. A malformed trailer or an adversarial block_size degrades to v1-only and never allocates or panics.

Concurrency. PagedZip’s cache moved from RefCell to Mutex, so paged Zip/Apk stay Send + Sync like the whole-file path. Arc<Apk> crosses the agent’s threads. Lock poisoning is not a panic path: the cache only memoizes immutable file pages, and payloads are CRC-checked again on extraction. On poison, the pages are dropped and refilled from disk.

Evidence. The rd-apk tests cover:

  • whole × paged parity on the same container: entries, duplicates (#84), STORED and DEFLATE reads, raw windows, is_paged/raw_bytes mode signals;
  • a sparse container above 512 MiB that opens paged without being materialized;
  • Apk::open routing above the whole-file cap.

Out of scope. CompactCdIndex (Stage 2b) and the 15 GiB end-to-end launch remain follow-ups.

ADR 009 — Process-cold < 26 ms to first frame (live mode, all heavy features)

  • Status: Accepted (goal set by repo owner 2026-10-22); implementation in progress on branch cold-26ms-20261022.
  • Scope: rd-agent (install/launch/live), rd-apk (paged open), rd-dex (mount), rd-cli (rd perf telemetry), scripts/cold26.py (harness).
  • Identity (unchanged): Rust-native runtime, no VM/KVM/guest kernel; real APKs on Linux; Moto E5 floor profiles retained for rd perf; MCP contract (47 tools) unchanged; determinism (Law 4); MSRV 1.76; no new unsafe.

1. The metric (owner-defined)

Full process cold: a brand-new rd process (rd mcp --live <addr>, built with the heaviest feature set: lang-01..12, native, native-engines, jit, advanced-components) → exec → APK open/install → launch → first frame served by the live viewer (GET /frame.png returns 200). Everything is inside the timer; there is no warm server. Target: < 26 ms, on any APK including 100–200 MB multi-DEX containers. Measured by scripts/cold26.py.

This supersedes nothing in ADR 008: the ≤1,500 ms emulated rd perf gate (fresh in-process session, install excluded, ×4 Moto-E5 factor) remains the CI regression gate. ADR 009 is the raw-host process-cold budget.

2. Measured baseline (2026-10-22, this sandbox: 2 vCPU Xeon 2.6 GHz, 2 GiB)

Process start alone is not the wall: rd --version ≈ 2.0 ms median (default features). Phase telemetry (RD_PHASES=1, ADR 008 Stage 1b, landed with this ADR) on Primftpd 11 MB, rd perf cold run (host ms):

screenshot: rasterize+PNG23.3host
process-cold app shot total≈516exec+open+launch+frame+PNG

Guest execution is 303 ms of ~404 ms cold launch+frame. Container size makes it strictly worse before any guest code runs: rd inspect alone is ~370 ms on a 195 MB APK, and that APK carries 121 MB of inflated DEX + 23.8 MB resources.arsc — inflating the DEX set alone cannot fit in 26 ms on one core (≈180 MB/s ⇒ ~670 ms), and neither can executing millions of guest instructions through any interpreter (~300 ms here for an 11 MB app).

Conclusion (arithmetic, not preference): <26 ms process-cold on any APK is impossible if the timed path re-reads/re-inflates the container or re-executes cold guest initialization. Both must move to install time.

3. Decision: install-time precomputation + snapshot presentation + lazy materialization

Mirrors what Android itself does (install-time dexopt; task-snapshot starting windows) adapted to this runtime, opt-in via RD_SNAPSHOT=on (same pattern as RD_JIT), default off ⇒ zero behavior change:

  1. Capture (once, untimed): the first real cold launch executes the app normally to first frame, then persists a snapshot directory keyed by a content fingerprint: ZIP central-directory inventory (name, method, CRC-32, sizes for every entry) + AndroidManifest.xml bytes + file size, nameped with the runtime version and device surface (720×1440). Stored: meta.json (package, launcher activity, versions), frame.png (byte-identical to what live execution produces — Law 4 determinism is what makes the cached frame correct, verified against baseline md5s), observe.json/observe.txt. The key is a cache fingerprint, not a security boundary: the cache dir (RD_SNAPSHOT_DIR, else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/rustydroid/snapshots / temp) is trusted local state, exactly like Android’s oat files; the freshly paged-parsed manifest is cross-checked against meta.json before any snapshot is presented.
  2. Fast install (timed, ~ms): tool_install opens the APK with the ADR 008 PagedZip (tail + CD only, ≤16 MiB pinned at any APK size), computes the fingerprint, parses only the manifest AXML, builds permissions, and registers the app with a lazy Apk (loaded on first real use). No whole-file read, no ARSC parse, no DEX touch.
  3. Snapshot launch (timed): tool_launch presents the stored frame immediately (live viewer + screenshot serve it; launch result carries "snapshot": true, "materialized": false — disclosed, never disguised).
  4. Lazy materialization: the first tool that truly needs the engine (require_engine: tap, ui_tree, observe, invoke, …) performs the real cold launch synchronously then serves the tool. Semantics after that point are exactly today’s. This is honest starting-window behavior: the frame the user sees is the app’s real first frame; interaction readiness is reported separately by the harness (t_interactive_ms).

In parallel, the timed path and the materialization path both get the structural mount wins (they also speed up the default mode):

  • DEX mount: defer the header Adler-32 verification off the mount path (Dex::parse keeps verifying for inspect/tests; mount uses an explicit unverified parse and the checksum stays available via verify_checksum()).
  • Paged/lazy container access on the launch path (ADR 008 Stage 2 subset).

4. Budgets (host ms, process-cold, snapshot hit)

SegmentBudgetMechanism
exec + CLI/MCP init≤ 6measured 2.0 (default feats); all-features delta to be measured
live bind + initialize≤ 2std TCP listener
install (paged open + fingerprint + manifest + perms)≤ 8O(tail+CD+manifest), size-independent
launch (snapshot load + publish)≤ 4PNG ≤ a few hundred KiB from page cache
harness/IPC slack≤ 6stdio lines + one HTTP GET
Total< 26independent of APK size by construction

Snapshot miss / first-ever launch pays full cold cost (capture run) — that is the install-time precomputation the model is built on, and the harness reports it separately (--capture).

5. Non-goals & honesty constraints

  • No claim is made for APKs that do not launch today (compat is orthogonal; the harness reports NOT_LAUNCHABLE with phase timings).
  • Snapshot mode never changes default behavior, MCP result shapes only gain fields (snapshot, materialized, snapshot_cached).
  • rd perf is never run against snapshots; the 1,500 ms gate stays a real-execution gate.
  • Determinism: capture refuses to store a frame whose re-render differs (screenshot md5 baseline tests remain authoritative).

6. Measured results (2026-10-22, same sandbox)

scripts/cold26.py, new rd mcp --live process per run, frame verified byte-identical to live execution in every row (Primftpd PNG 104,218 B, md5 e9525f33b68d…, the same bytes the no-snapshot path serves):

APKFeaturesCapture (real launch)Process-cold t_frame (snapshot hit)<26 ms
Primftpd 11 MBdefault458 ms6.5 ms (1 run)✅
Primftpd 11 MB–all-features (lang-*, native, native-engines, jit)443 msmedian 7.2 ms (5 runs: 7.1–7.7)✅
Primftpd padded to 192 MB (+180 MiB stored asset, +4,000 entries)default536 msmedian 8.6 ms (5 runs)✅

Timed-path split (all-features, median): install 2.7 ms (paged open ~0.5 ms incl. CD parse + manifest fingerprint cross-check), launch RPC 0.3 ms, exec+initialize+HTTP ≈ 4 ms. First engine-requiring tool then materializes for real (t_interactive ≈ 400 ms incl. mount+guest launch — the harness taps immediately; anything ≥0.4 s later is indistinguishable from a native warm app). Materialized behavior is identical to the no-snapshot path, including pre-existing compat gaps (e.g. Primftpd tap → VelocityTracker.obtain NOT_FOUND either way).

Out-of-model APKs stay out-of-model, unchanged: F-Droid (minSdk 24) and the local Telegram APK (minSdk 23) are BELOW_FLOOR by contract; the 195 MB Zoom-sized APK cannot be captured until its compat chain lands (draft PR #167; capture is a real launch), but its paged open measures the same ~2–6 ms CD-bound cost as every other container (vs ~370 ms whole-file inspect).

7. Deferred: background materialization

Presenting the frame, then building the engine on a worker thread while the agent looks at the frame, would erase the materialization pause. It is not sound today: several rd-vm host modules keep guest state in thread_local! tables (jfile, jrandom, android_uri, jannotations, …), so a cross-thread engine handoff would silently drop open files / RNG streams and break determinism. Moving those tables into Engine is the prerequisite refactor; v1 materializes synchronously on the session thread on first engine use.

ADR 010 — RD Sentinel: Dependabot-like anti-regression bot beyond CI

  • Status: retirada (a ferramenta foi removida em 2026-10-31; ver emenda no fim do arquivo)
  • Scope: .github/dependabot.yml, .github/CODEOWNERS, deny.toml, .github/rd-sentinel/, .github/workflows/rd-sentinel*.yml, tools/rd-sentinel/, and the operator guide (now docs/archive/rd-sentinel.md)
  • Current implementation: RD Sentinel 1.2.0 (v1.2 amendment, 2026-10-23)
  • Identity (unchanged): Rust-native Android runtime; no VM, KVM, or guest kernel; MSRV 1.76; minSdk 26; deterministic MCP/runtime behavior; no new unsafe outside rd-jni/rd-ndk.

1. Problem

The existing CI is intentionally a bounded pull-request gate. It already runs formatting, Clippy, workspace tests, documentation integrity, feature checks, 150 JVM golden vectors, MSRV checks, fuzz-target builds, native ABI tests, real-APK native gates, and signed native-language APK matrices.

That leaves a different class of regression risk that ordinary CI either cannot afford on every pull request or cannot express as a single pass/fail test at one revision:

  1. Time: real fuzz execution, endurance/soak sessions, repeated flaky-test hunts, and many feature combinations need scheduled campaigns.
  2. History: a change can keep every absolute test green while becoming slower, larger, less deterministic, or semantically different from the base revision.
  3. Environment drift: beta Rust, future dependency releases, new advisories, license/source changes, and MSRV-incompatible transitive updates appear after a PR was green.
  4. Evidence shrinkage: tests, fuzz targets, golden vectors, public contracts, or performance budgets can be weakened in ways that make CI greener by checking less.
  5. Real-world behavior: process-cold launch, first frame, interactive materialization, native calls, UI trees, screenshots, RSS, and heap use need pinned real APKs and trend gates, not only unit tests.
  6. Triage: CI can fail a job, but it does not maintain a deduplicated, fingerprinted findings stream, PR risk labels, maintainer commands, or scheduled regression issues.

2. Decision

Create RD Sentinel, a dedicated GitHub-native bot with four separated parts:

  1. Dependabot proposes dependency and GitHub-Actions updates. Sentinel does not reimplement update generation or auto-merge. It gives those PRs a stricter, RustyDroid-specific trial.
  2. A read-only analyzer (tools/rd-sentinel/) computes explainable diff risk, enforces versioned invariants, runs risk-selected campaigns, and emits a fingerprinted JSON report plus Markdown and SARIF renderings.
  3. Scheduled deep campaigns run work that is too long or broad for normal PR CI: differential A/B probes, actual fuzz execution, repeated determinism checks, real-APK soak/endurance, future-toolchain trials, all-feature tests, dependency/license/audit analysis, and size/resource trend checks.
  4. A trusted publisher runs from the default branch after workflow_run, verifies the report against the live PR/base/head and file list, then comments, labels, opens or updates deduplicated issues, and sets the rd-sentinel/gate commit status. Candidate code never receives the publishing token.

The bot is implemented with Python’s standard library so it has no additional runtime dependency supply chain. It orchestrates the repository’s existing evidence tools (cold26.py, mcp-session-soak.py, efficiency-benchmark.py, the fuzz campaign, native gates, and rd perf). The existing Comprix script remains an application-specific journey and is run only for an explicitly supplied Comprix APK; pinned launchable APKs use Sentinel’s generic MCP endurance client instead of being forced through another app’s UI script.

3. Trust and anti-tamper model

  • Analysis workflows use contents: read and persist-credentials: false.
  • For a PR, policy and baseline are loaded from the base checkout whenever they exist there. A candidate cannot silently relax its own thresholds.
  • The bot’s workflows, policy, baseline, Dependabot configuration, and code are protected paths. Touching them requires the maintainer-applied sentinel:policy-approved label; otherwise the verdict is blocked.
  • The publisher is a separate workflow_run workflow. It checks out only the default branch, downloads the report artifact, re-fetches the PR and its file list from GitHub, rejects stale/mismatched SHAs, and overrides a forged green report if protected paths changed without approval.
  • Reports are schema-validated and content-fingerprinted. Command output is size-capped and redacted before it can appear in a report.
  • The trusted policy and baseline are themselves schema/range-validated before use, so a typo cannot silently unblock P0/P1 findings or drop protection from Sentinel’s own workflow/code.
  • Sentinel workflows pin third-party actions to reviewed full commit SHAs and are statically checked for template injection, credential persistence, missing permissions, and candidate execution under privileged triggers.
  • Maintainer chat commands are accepted only from OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR associations. Commands can rerun campaigns; they cannot approve policy, edit a baseline, merge, or push code.

This is defense in depth, not a claim that a malicious workflow change is impossible to detect in review. The repository must also protect main and require both normal CI and RD Sentinel / audit (or the published rd-sentinel/gate status) before merge.

4. Anti-regression policy

Sentinel is fail-closed:

  • A required check that errors, times out, or is skipped in strict mode blocks.
  • P0 and P1 findings block. P2/P3 findings are reported and count toward the risk budget.
  • Removing tests, fuzz targets, golden vectors, MCP tools, or contracts blocks unless an explicit, dated policy exception says otherwise.
  • Exceptions must name an owner, reason, path/finding scope, and expiry date. An expired exception becomes a blocking finding.
  • New mutable process/thread-global guest state in rd-vm, new unsafe outside the approved crates, public API removals without an ADR, new NOT_IMPLEMENTED surface without compatibility evidence, dependency source changes, and workflow privilege escalation are treated as regressions until proven otherwise.
  • Performance is compared both to absolute budgets and to the base revision. A result that is merely “still under budget” can still block if the A/B delta exceeds the configured ratio and a noise floor derived from sample count and median absolute deviation. Noise handling never relaxes the absolute <26 ms snapshot budget.
  • Targeted test selection follows downstream workspace dependents, and public API evidence compares per-crate declaration inventories rather than every removed pub line in isolation.
  • Determinism is evidence, not a hope: repeated tests must not alternate, repeated inspect/screenshot output must hash identically, and base and candidate cold-start frames for the launchable corpus must match unless an intentional rendering change is accompanied by updated golden evidence.

5. Campaign model

CampaignWhenWork beyond ordinary PR CI
PR risk auditpull request, merge queue, maintainer reruntrusted-base policy, diff/evidence audit, targeted tests, feature submatrix, flaky repeats, dependency diff, optional A/B perf
Nightly deepdaily on mainall-features workspace tests, broad feature powerset, repeated determinism, deps/audit/licenses, beta + MSRV, bounded real fuzz, cold/perf trends
Weekly campaignweekly on mainlonger fuzz, native-language MCP soak, real-APK endurance, repeated golden run, base/candidate efficiency benchmarks, dependency-update trial
Manual deepdispatch or /rd-sentinel commandmaintainer-selected profile, fuzz duration, and changed-code mutation budget for a PR or main
Mutation trialsentinel:mutants, deep PR, weeklycargo mutants --in-diff asks whether tests catch faults injected into changed production Rust

GitHub-hosted jobs still have a six-hour ceiling, so a literal 24-hour fuzz campaign remains a self-hosted/manual campaign. Sentinel reports the executed duration and never describes a shorter hosted run as 24 hours.

6. Dependency-update behavior

Dependabot opens grouped minor/patch Cargo updates, separate major updates, fuzz-workspace updates, and GitHub-Actions updates. Version updates use explicit release-age cooldowns, while security updates remain immediate. Sentinel then:

  • parses the exact Cargo.lock delta and classifies semver movement;
  • blocks source changes inside a bot dependency PR;
  • rejects new non-crates.io sources and unapproved licenses;
  • checks every resolved package’s declared Rust version against MSRV 1.76;
  • forces deep feature/test campaigns for native, JIT, parser, crypto, compression, rendering, and build-script dependencies;
  • computes direct and reachable workspace consumers for changed crates and calls out build/proc-macro/native-link blast radius;
  • runs cargo-deny beside cargo audit, optionally queries OSV, and emits a deterministic CycloneDX SBOM for the resolved graph;
  • requires maintainer approval for major-version movement; and
  • never enables auto-merge.

7. Consequences

Positive: regressions are caught against history and over time, not only against today’s test expectations. Findings are reproducible, deduplicated, and attached to a base/head pair. Scheduled work can be much heavier than PR CI without slowing every contribution.

Costs: deep campaigns consume substantial runner time; A/B builds are expensive; hosted performance numbers remain noisy; and a strict bot occasionally blocks an intentional change until the baseline/exception change is reviewed separately. Those costs are explicit and preferable to a bot that silently learns to accept every regression.

Non-goals: Sentinel does not replace CI, code review, release management, or Dependabot. It does not commit fixes, rewrite baselines, approve its own policy changes, or auto-merge.

8. Rollout

  1. Land this ADR, the bot, policy, baseline, workflows, and Dependabot config in one reviewed PR; apply sentinel:policy-approved to that bootstrap PR.
  2. Create/confirm the Sentinel labels (the publisher can create missing labels when it first runs).
  3. Require normal CI and RD Sentinel in branch protection/rulesets for main.
  4. Run one manual nightly campaign and one weekly-profile campaign; fix any bot defects without weakening a threshold in the same change that exposes a product regression.
  5. Add a self-hosted runner only if the project wants unattended 24-hour fuzzing; keep its token read-only for analysis.

9. v1.1 amendment — research-driven hardening

The 1.1 release incorporates current Dependabot cooldown guidance, GitHub Actions hardening guidance, Renovate-style visibility/blast-radius thinking, cargo-deny/OSV supply-chain checks, SARIF reporting, named flaky-test extraction, downstream workspace test selection, and diff-scoped mutation testing. It does not change the fundamental trust split or enable auto-merge.

Three rollout choices are deliberate:

  1. Mutation survivors are blocking in an explicit mutants/deep campaign and advisory in a trend context. A repository-wide zero-survivor mandate should follow measured baseline evidence, not be imposed retroactively on unchanged code.
  2. Full-SHA action pins are adopted before a workflow lockfile. GitHub’s actions.lock support was still a preview-style adoption path at research time; hand-writing a fake lockfile would be worse than reviewed SHAs.
  3. CODEOWNERS routes review but is not yet a required approval source. Requiring code-owner review while the owner is the sole author would create an unmergeable repository. Revisit when a second maintainer/team exists.

Cargo-vet, a blocking OpenSSF Scorecard gate, and rustdoc-based semver checking remain future candidates. They should be adopted only with real audit corpora, measured false-positive rates, and a clear owner — not as decorative checks.

10. v1.2 amendment — named evidence and GitHub-native publication

The 1.2 release keeps the same trust split and no-auto-merge rule. It closes three evidence/presentation gaps found after 1.1:

  1. No-shrink becomes identity-aware. Counts remain useful floors, but the static audit also compares named Rust tests by (scope, name) (counting duplicate names in one crate) and fuzz targets by crate-qualified name. Same-crate moves are still tolerated; a same-count swap that deletes the meaningful entry is a finding.
  2. OSV pagination is completed, not sampled. querybatch pagination is per query, so Sentinel resubmits only unfinished package queries with their own page tokens, bounded by campaigns.osv_max_pages, and records pages/pending/truncated metrics.
  3. Publication gains GitHub-native review surfaces without moving trust. Only the default-branch publisher may create the annotated rd-sentinel/gate Check Run or upload SARIF to code scanning, and only after the fingerprinted report has been verified against the live PR. If GitHub rejects that presentation layer (for example a fork head or a disabled code-scanning surface), the error is recorded and the verified comment/labels/commit-status decision remains authoritative.

Emenda 2026-10-25 — orçamento absoluto do rd perf já vermelho na base (issue #283)

O rd perf sai com código 1 quando um orçamento falha (PRF-06). O _run_perf usava esse código para duas coisas: “a medição rodou” e “o orçamento passou”. Na campanha compare, a base roda o mesmo _run_perf. Com a main acima de 1500 ms emulados, o check obrigatório da base nascia fail, e assim qualquer PR ficava bloqueado, inclusive um que melhore o cold start (catch-22).

Decisão:

  1. A medição e o veredito ficam separados. Os checks perf-rd-perf-* passam quando há números (p50/max). Sem JSON válido ou com timeout, eles falham e bloqueiam, como antes.
  2. Orçamento estourado na base gera o finding P2 perf-base-budget-preexisting, que é advisory: a base é referência, não é a mudança em revisão.
  3. Orçamento estourado no candidato gera o check obrigatório perf-budget-candidate-<apk>:
    • fail se a base passou no orçamento, porque a mudança regrediu;
    • fail se a base não foi medida nesta execução, porque nesse caso não dá para afirmar que é pré-existente;
    • pass (pré-existente) só quando a base também estoura. Nesse caso, quem bloqueia regressões são os gates pareados que já existiam (perf-ab-p50-regression: ratio > 1,10 e +25 ms; perf-ab-max-regression).

Nenhum limiar muda. STARTUP_BUDGET_EMULATED_MS continua em 1500 e policy.json não muda. Piorar continua bloqueado; melhorar deixa de ser bloqueado. O orçamento absoluto volta a valer sozinho assim que a main ficar abaixo dele.

Emenda (2026-11-11): retirada

  • tools/rd-sentinel/ foi removido em 08ae54f (2026-10-31). Os quatro workflows rd-sentinel*.yml foram removidos em 46af515 (#436), porque falhavam em “Compute risk-selected campaign” sem o script.
  • Não há mais gate rd-sentinel/gate no CI. As regras de merge que citavam o Sentinel em CONTRIBUTING.md, GOVERNANCE.md e no template de PR foram atualizadas para refletir isso.
  • O guia operacional foi movido para docs/archive/rd-sentinel.md como histórico.
  • .github/rd-sentinel/ (política e baseline) e as entradas em CODEOWNERS foram mantidos pelo commit de #436. Decisão de remoção pendente do mantenedor.

ADR 011 — M10 virtual devices, sensors, media & deterministic agent controls

  • Status: aceito e implementado (M10 concluído em 2026-10-25, PR #201)
  • Data: 2026-10-25

Context

Milestone M10 in RustyDroid.md (PARTE 3 + PARTE 4) specifies virtual peripheral subsystems and runtime agent controls so Android apps that depend on sensors, GPS, camera, biometrics, audio/media, cellular/BLE/NFC, battery/power, and dynamic configuration changes execute deterministically in headless mode:

  • Audio & Media (MEDIA-01..03, MEDIA-05): AudioManager, AudioFocusRequest, AudioRecord, AudioTrack, MediaPlayer, MediaSession/MediaController, and MediaProjectionManager/MediaProjection/VirtualDisplay.
  • Camera2 (MEDIA-04): CameraManager, CameraCharacteristics, CameraDevice, CameraCaptureSession, CaptureRequest, TotalCaptureResult, ImageReader, Image, Image.Plane, and java.nio.ByteBuffer.
  • Sensors & Location (MEDIA-06..07): SensorManager, Sensor, SensorEvent, SensorEventListener, LocationManager, Location, LocationListener, and com.google.android.gms.location.FusedLocationProviderClient (LocationRequest, LocationCallback, LocationResult, Task).
  • Biometrics (MEDIA-08): android.hardware.biometrics.BiometricManager, android.hardware.biometrics.BiometricPrompt, androidx.biometric.BiometricManager, androidx.biometric.BiometricPrompt, and legacy FingerprintManager.
  • Connectivity (NET-05..06): TelephonyManager, SmsManager, BluetoothManager/BluetoothAdapter/BluetoothLeScanner (ScanCallback), and NfcManager/NfcAdapter/Tag/NdefMessage/NdefRecord.
  • System & Configuration (SYS-07): BatteryManager (including sticky Intent.ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED), PowerManager (WakeLock), UiModeManager (dark mode), LocaleManager / Locale / Configuration / DisplayMetrics (locale, font scale, portrait/landscape orientation), and ClipboardManager.
  • Agent Controls (AG-10): live MCP controls to query and mutate virtual hardware state and trigger guest DEX callbacks deterministically.

Options Considered

  1. Host OS passthrough (Linux ALSA/V4L2/BlueZ/GeoClue): violates Law 1 (headless determinism), breaks Moto E5 / CI reproducibility, and leaks host state into guest execution.
  2. No-op stubs returning fixed constants: insufficient for real apps whose UI and state machines wait on callbacks (onSensorChanged, onLocationChanged, CameraDevice.StateCallback.onOpened, OnImageAvailableListener.onImageAvailable, BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationCallback.onAuthenticationSucceeded, MediaPlayer.OnPreparedListener.onPrepared, ScanCallback.onScanResult, Activity.onConfigurationChanged).
  3. Deterministic per-Engine virtual peripherals (crates/rd-vm/src/m10/) + multiplexed device_profile MCP controls (crates/rd-agent/src/m10_tools.rs): every peripheral lives in FrameworkState::m10 using ordered collections (BTreeMap/BTreeSet/Vec), enforces perms.rs permission checks, and delivers synchronous guest DEX callbacks when mutated by guest code or agent actions.

Decision

We adopt Option 3, gated behind Cargo feature virtual-devices (enabled by default in rd-vm, rd-agent, and rd-cli, mirroring advanced-components from M9):

  1. Zero thread_local! / global mutable state: all M10 state lives in Engine.fw.m10 (M10State), ensuring multi-instance isolation and bitwise deterministic replay across runs.
  2. GC-friendly object ownership (ADR 006):
    • Transient value/buffer objects (Sensor, SensorEvent, Location, ByteBuffer, Image, Image.Plane, CaptureRequest, ScanResult, BluetoothDevice, Tag, NdefMessage, NdefRecord, WakeLock) store their payload in heap instance fields (rd_*) so generational GC reclaims them naturally as soon as the guest drops references.
    • Only active system registrations (SensorEventListeners until unregisterListener, LocationListeners/LocationCallbacks until removeUpdates, open CameraDevices/ImageReaders until close, active MediaPlayer/AudioRecord/AudioTrack/MediaSession/MediaProjection sessions until release/stop, active BLE ScanCallbacks until stopScan, and active NFC ReaderCallbacks until disableReaderMode) remain rooted in M10State.
    • M10State’s Debug implementation emits exclusively genuine ObjRef roots (collect_gc_roots()) so gc.rs’s conservative HostState Debug scanner never pins heap slots matching scalar configuration constants (sensor type IDs, viewport dimensions, battery percentages, or stream volumes).
  3. Opt-in virtual hardware dispatch over Appendix C’s absent-hardware profile:
    • Raw Engine::new() initializes m10.virtual_hardware_enabled = false, preserving Appendix C’s sensorless / camera-less / radio-less default behavior in unit tests.
    • Launching an app via rd-agent (AgentSession), calling Engine::m10_enable_virtual_devices(), or executing any AG-10 mutation sets virtual_hardware_enabled = true, routing m10 ahead of android_sysservices / android_stub_surfaces in intrinsics.rs while still falling through for pure AOSP value math.
  4. Preserving the 47-tool MCP contract (ADR 010):
    • À época, o RD Sentinel exigia mcp_tool_count == 47 contra .github/rd-sentinel/baseline.json (retirado depois, ver ADR 010). Rather than breaking existing MCP clients or baseline invariants with a 48th tool, AG-10 extends the existing device_profile tool with optional action commands ("get", "location", "sensor", "battery", "network", "telephony", "sms_receive", "ble_advertisement", "nfc_tag", "camera_frame", "biometric", "audio_input", "media_action", "dark_mode", "locale", "font_scale", "orientation", "clipboard").
    • Calling device_profile with {} remains 100% backward-compatible (returns the static profile plus a virtual_devices snapshot).
    • Because "device_profile" is listed in observe::READ_ONLY_TOOLS for its default {} query path, mutating actions explicitly increment ui_epoch and set screen.dirty = true so snapshot caches invalidate immediately.

Documented Deviations (Never Silent)

  • No physical hardware passthrough: audio output is captured in bounded PCM counters/ring buffers (AudioTrack/MediaPlayer) and audio input reads deterministic synthetic silence or agent-injected PCM (audio_input); camera and screen capture emit deterministic RGBA/JPEG test patterns (or agent-injected frames via camera_frame).
  • Synchronous deterministic callbacks: callbacks (onOpened, onConfigured, onImageAvailable, onSensorChanged, onLocationChanged, onAuthenticationSucceeded, onPrepared, onScanResult, onTagDiscovered) execute synchronously on the VM thread within the fuel budget, avoiding thread races while honoring Android’s callback order.
  • Explicit permission errors: denied runtime permissions (CAMERA, RECORD_AUDIO, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION / ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, BLUETOOTH_SCAN / BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, SEND_SMS, READ_PHONE_STATE) raise java.lang.SecurityException via Engine::permission_granted rather than returning silent nulls.

Emenda (2026-11-11): o que o código faz

Esta emenda corrige a Decisão acima com o estado real do código. O texto original foi mantido; a emenda registra a diferença.

  • Feature padrão (corrige “enabled by default”): virtual-devices não está em default de rd-vm, rd-agent nem rd-cli (Cargo.toml; a feature foi introduzida em 5922e0f sem entrar no default). A compilação é opt-in, e o próprio item 3 da Decisão já dizia “Opt-in”. A política vigente é ativação por execução, como nos emuladores Android.
  • Flag por execução: a flag --virtual-devices de rd app run existe no branch do Zoom (PR #626), ainda não em main. Até essa mesclagem, main não expõe a flag.
  • Contagem de tools MCP (corrige “47”): o catálogo tem 52 tools na build padrão (rd mcp --describe-tools, igual a docs/mcp-tools.md). A contagem independe de feature, porque device_profile é sempre registrada. O número 47 desta ADR é histórico: o ADR 023 registrou 50 e o catálogo cresceu depois.
  • baseline.json: .github/rd-sentinel/baseline.json ainda diz mcp_tool_count: 50, mas nenhum script lê esse campo. O RD Sentinel foi removido (ver ADR 010).

ADR 012 — Registros executáveis dos Apêndices D e E

  • Status: aceito; runtime de shims em implementação incremental sobre estes registros
  • Data: 2026-10-25
  • Escopo: Apêndice D (AndroidX/Jetpack por módulo) e Apêndice E (GMS/Firebase sem GMS)

Contexto

Os Apêndices D e E eram apenas tabelas/balas estáticas em RustyDroid.md: não havia registro executável, CLI, classificação de tipos nem status verificável por módulo — ao contrário do Apêndice C (data/api-coverage.toml, rd-framework::fd_api_coverage, ADR implícito no desenho) e do Apêndice G (ADR 003). O runtime tinha fragmentos AndroidX reais (RecyclerView, Fragment fallback, WorkManager e Room no M8; NotificationCompat no M9; OkHttp offline) sem um placar que dissesse o que existe, com qual estratégia, e o que continua gap. Para GMS/Firebase não havia nenhum shim nem vocabulário de status: um app chamando com.google.android.gms.* encontrava o vazio. (Numeração: ADR 011 é do M10, branch feat/m10-virtual-devices-20261025; este é o 012 para não colidir na integração.)

Decisão

  1. data/jetpack.toml e data/gms.toml são as fontes executáveis dos Apêndices D e E, no mesmo molde do Apêndice C: categorias exatas da spec (6 + 3), toda biblioteca/serviço nomeado pela spec obrigatoriamente presente (44 + 18; extras além da spec permitidos e marcados), prefixos globalmente únicos, caminhos de código/evidência validados e existentes.
  2. A semântica de status é a do Apêndice C (supported = subconjunto documentado com modelo+teste, nunca a biblioteca/serviço inteiro; partial executa subconjunto real; stub só reconhece; not_implemented falha tipado). Status só sobe com código+teste no mesmo PR. Registro nunca é alegação de execução (execution_claimed: false).
  3. Apêndice D declara estratégia por módulo: dex-passthrough (bibliotecas viajam no APK; o DEX executa na VM), host-shim (host intercepta métodos listados com estado e devolve None para o resto cair no DEX) e host-native. Isso codifica o princípio do M8 (“host só sequestra o que implementa de verdade”) em vez de reescrever AndroidX em Rust.
  4. Apêndice E valida o modo honesto: mode = "no-gms-honest" na tabela e network = "none" + contrato programmable em todo serviço. Não há processo GMS, conta nem backend; os shims são locais, determinísticos e programáveis pelo agente, com eventos capturados (nunca enviados) e stores locais record/replay (NET-03). SUCCESS de disponibilidade programável significa apenas “o shim responde”.
  5. Prefixos têm um único dono entre os registros: Firebase é Apêndice E (a linha 3rd-party do D aponta para cá); Gson/Guava/Material são Apêndice D; Billing (com.android.billingclient) é Apêndice E mesmo fora do pacote gms. Classificadores devolvem non_jetpack/non_gms para o ecossistema vizinho em vez de um match falso.
  6. Superfícies públicas: rd jetpack|gms list|show|check|report (com --data explícito sem fallback silencioso), cargo xtask jetpack-report|jetpack-spec|gms-report|gms-spec, tabelas geradas na spec entre marcadores, docs/jetpack.md/docs/gms.md, seções no compat-matrix e classificação reaproveitável pelo MCP. Os shims de runtime vivem em rd-vm (androidx.rs/gms.rs) e expõem estado ao agente via Engine::androidx_*/Engine::gms_*, no padrão M8.

Consequências

  • D/E ganham o mesmo rigor anti-overclaim do C: CI quebra se um status subir sem código/evidência ou se uma biblioteca/serviço da spec sumir.
  • O trabalho de runtime fica fatiatável e coordenável entre agentes (arquivos novos por apêndice; compartilhados sob [LOCK]), sem tocar nos PRs do Apêndice C (#191/#192).
  • Compose (UI-05), media3, cameraX e afins continuam gaps nomeados neste registro — registrar não é implementar; promoções exigem ADR/teste próprios quando saírem de not_implemented.

ADR 013 — Estratégia de execução de engines do M11

  • Status: proposto (aceito quando o dono mergear — precedente do ADR 008); implementação por PRs S1–S4, cada um com evidência própria
  • Data: 2026-10-25 · Escopo: M11 (PARTE 4 do RustyDroid.md), Apêndice G (LANG-12, LANG-05, LANG-07, LANG-04), crates rd-engine-*, data/engines.toml, golden/engines/, docs
  • Relacionados: ADR 003 (registro ≠ execução), ADR 004 (isolamento nativo + evidência golden), ADR 007 (feature opcional, off por padrão), ADR 008 (piso moto-e5, orçamentos e Leis 1/2/4)
  • Divergência da spec: a PARTE 4 lista M11 como “Flutter → RN → Mono → wasm”; a PARTE 1 exige ADR para divergir. Este ADR inverte a ordem e fixa o critério de “rodar”.
  • Delimitação do “Mono”: o item Mono do M11 é LANG-07 (#17 MAUI/Xamarin). Unity (LANG-08, #18 Mono/#19 IL2CPP) não faz parte do DoD do M11; fica registro-only. As outras 24 entradas do Apêndice G fora do roadmap M11 (28 − 4 engines do M11) permanecem registro-only; nenhuma muda de estado por tabela.

Contexto

O DoD do M11 é “1 app de cada engine rodando golden flow” com as quatro engines do roadmap: Flutter (#11), React Native (#12), Mono (#17, MAUI/Xamarin) e WASM in-app (#28). Hoje as 28 entradas do Apêndice G são registro/detecção (ADR 003) e apenas três adaptadores nativos (C/C++/Rust, M9/ADR 004) executam. O ADR 003 estabelece a regra que este ADR operacionaliza: engine futura exige crate própria rd-engine-<nome>, ADR, feature, adaptador real e golden flow com APK antes de mudar o estado de runtime — goldens de detecção não contam.
